inclusion: General intangible assets lacking specific alternative standards
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates general scope items from specialized assets governed by separate accounting pronouncements.

descriptors.definition: When an asset combines tangible and intangible elements, an entity applies judgment to determine the primary component. Software integral to hardware is treated as property, plant, and equipment, whereas non-integral software is treated as an intangible asset.
inclusion: Computer software not integral to related hardware
Knowledge component of prototypes
exclusion: Operating systems and software integral to machine tools
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between tangible assets containing incidental software under Ind AS 16 and standalone intangible software under Ind AS 38.

descriptors.definition: Rights under licensing agreements for items like motion pictures, plays, and patents are excluded from lease accounting standards and governed instead by the intangible asset standard. This ensures specialized intellectual property licenses are evaluated under appropriate criteria.
inclusion: Licensing rights for motion pictures, video recordings, plays, manuscripts, patents, and copyrights
exclusion: Standard asset leases governed by lease accounting rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between standard property/equipment leases under Ind AS 116 and intellectual property licensing rights under Ind AS 38.

descriptors.definition: The standard excludes exploration, development, and extraction expenditures in extractive industries as well as insurance contracts. However, it applies to separate operational intangible assets utilized within these sectors, such as computer software or start-up costs.
inclusion: Computer software used by insurers or in extractive industries
Start-up costs incurred in extractive or insurance sectors
exclusion: Mineral exploration and development expenditures
Insurance contract acquisition cash flows
nearby_distinctions: Separates core mineral/insurance extraction activities from standard general administrative intangibles like software used by these entities.

descriptors.definition: Entities applying optional transition exemptions may bypass standard amortisation methods for toll road service concession arrangements recognized prior to their first reporting period. This exception accommodates specific grandfathering rules permitted under initial adoption standards.
inclusion: Intangible assets from toll road service concession arrangements recognized before the first reporting period
exclusion: Standard intangible asset amortisation methods
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard intangible amortisation rules from grandfathered treatment permitted for specific toll road concessions under first-time adoption.

descriptors.definition: This section provides core terminology for applying the standard, defining parameters such as amortisation, carrying amount, cost, development, and fair value. These definitions establish the structural basis for recognizing and measuring intangible items.
inclusion: Key defined terms governing intangible asset accounting
exclusion: General business terms outside accounting standards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes entity-specific value from fair value and monetary assets from non-monetary assets.

descriptors.definition: An intangible asset is characterized as an identifiable, non-monetary resource without physical substance. It encompasses various categories including marketing-related, customer-related, artistic-related, contract-based, and technology-based items.
inclusion: Computer software, patents, copyrights, customer lists, franchises, and domain names
exclusion: Monetary assets
Tangible assets with physical substance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes intangible assets from monetary and tangible assets based on physical substance and monetary characteristics.

descriptors.definition: An intangible asset is defined as an identifiable non-monetary asset lacking physical substance. Entities often invest in resources such as technical knowledge, intellectual property, and brand names that fall under this classification.
inclusion: Scientific knowledge, licenses, trademarks, customer lists, and motion pictures
exclusion: Physical inventory and monetary claims
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes qualifying intangible assets from unidentifiable internal enhancements and goodwill.

descriptors.definition: An asset is identifiable if it is separable and capable of being sold, transferred, licensed, or exchanged, or if it arises from contractual or legal rights. Items that fail to meet this criterion cannot be recognized as separate intangible assets and are instead absorbed into goodwill when acquired in a business combination.
inclusion: Assets capable of being individually rented, sold, or licensed
Rights arising from legal or contractual agreements
exclusion: General market share not protected by contract or separability
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes separately identifiable intangible assets from unidentifiable goodwill arising in a business combination.

descriptors.definition: An asset is a resource controlled by an entity resulting from past events from which future economic benefits are expected to flow. Control requires the power to obtain future economic benefits while restricting access by others, typically established via legal enforceability.
inclusion: Resources protected by legal rights, confidentiality agreements, or restraint of trade clauses
exclusion: Skilled staff teams and customer loyalty lacking specific legal protection or control
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes controlled proprietary knowledge protected by legal rights from general workforce skills and uncontracted customer relationships.

descriptors.definition: An item meeting the definition of an intangible asset is recognized when it is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity and its cost can be measured reliably. Subsequent expenditures are generally recognized in profit or loss as incurred unless they specifically enhance an existing asset.
inclusion: costs incurred initially to acquire or internally generate an intangible asset
subsequent expenditures that add to, replace part of, or service an existing intangible asset meeting criteria
exclusion: subsequent expenditure on brands, mastheads, publishing titles, and customer lists
expenditures that cannot be distinguished from developing the business as a whole
nearby_distinctions: Initial acquisition costs versus subsequent maintenance expenditures
Intangible assets versus general business development expenses

descriptors.definition: An intangible asset is recognized only if future economic benefits are probable and the cost can be reliably measured based on management's best estimates. Subsequent expenditures are rarely capitalized because they typically maintain existing benefits rather than create a new recognizable asset.
inclusion: initial acquisition costs
qualifying subsequent replacement costs
exclusion: subsequent expenditure on brands and customer lists
general business upkeep costs
nearby_distinctions: General recognition criteria versus specialized internal generation rules

descriptors.definition: Intangible assets are initially measured at cost upon acquisition or self-generation. Separately acquired assets automatically satisfy probability criteria and include purchase price and directly attributable preparation costs.
inclusion: purchase price including import duties and non-refundable taxes
employee benefits cost arising directly from bringing the asset to working condition
professional fees and testing costs
exclusion: general administrative overhead
costs incurred after asset is ready for intended use
nearby_distinctions: Initial cost measurement versus subsequent measurement models

descriptors.definition: Separately acquired intangible assets are measured at cost comprising purchase price and direct preparation expenses, with the probability criterion automatically considered satisfied. Capitalization ceases once the asset is capable of operating in the manner intended by management.
inclusion: cash price equivalent for deferred payments
costs of testing whether the asset works properly
exclusion: interest expense recognized over credit period
costs incurred after cessation of capitalization
nearby_distinctions: Separate acquisition cost components versus business combination fair value measurement

descriptors.definition: Intangible assets acquired in a business combination are measured at fair value at the acquisition date, which incorporates market expectations of future economic benefits. The acquirer recognizes these identifiable assets separately from goodwill even if the acquiree had not previously recognized them.
inclusion: identifiable intangible assets arising from contractual or legal rights
in-process research and development projects meeting asset definitions
exclusion: goodwill components not meeting identifiable asset criteria
nearby_distinctions: Business combination fair value recognition versus separate acquisition historical cost

descriptors.definition: Intangible assets acquired free of charge or for nominal consideration via government grants are recognized initially at fair value or at a nominal amount plus direct preparation costs. Asset exchanges are measured at fair value unless the transaction lacks commercial substance or fair values are unreliable.
inclusion: airport landing rights and radio licenses
assets received in commercial exchanges measured at fair value
exclusion: exchanges lacking commercial substance measured at fair value
nearby_distinctions: Government grant nominal recognition versus standard fair value acquisition

descriptors.definition: Intangible assets acquired in exchange for other assets are measured at fair value unless the transaction lacks commercial substance or fair values cannot be measured reliably. If fair value is not used, the cost is measured at the carrying amount of the asset given up.
inclusion: assets acquired via exchange of non-monetary or mixed assets
reliable fair value measurements of received or given assets
exclusion: transactions lacking significant changes in future cash flow configurations
nearby_distinctions: Exchange valuation using fair value versus carrying amount of asset given up

descriptors.definition: Internally generated goodwill is prohibited from recognition as an asset because it lacks an identifiable, separable resource controlled by the entity with a reliably measurable cost. Discrepancies between an entity's fair value and its net identifiable assets do not represent recognizable intangible asset costs.
inclusion: unrecognized business value drivers contributing to overall corporate worth
exclusion: recognized goodwill arising strictly from business combinations
identifiable intangible assets separately acquired
nearby_distinctions: Prohibited internally generated goodwill versus acquired goodwill in business combinations

descriptors.definition: The generation of an internal intangible asset is split into a research phase and a development phase to determine recognition eligibility. Expenditures incurred during the research phase must be expensed immediately as no asset can be demonstrated to exist at that stage.
inclusion: original investigation activities aimed at obtaining new knowledge
search for alternative materials and processes
exclusion: development phase expenditures meeting strict capitalization criteria
internally generated brands, mastheads, and customer lists
nearby_distinctions: Research phase immediate expensing versus development phase capitalization criteria

descriptors.definition: Expenditures on intangible items are recognized as expenses when incurred unless they form part of a recognized intangible asset cost or business combination goodwill. Specific outlays like research, start-up costs, training, advertising, and relocation must always be expensed.
inclusion: establishment and pre-opening costs
advertising and promotional expenditures
training and reorganization costs
exclusion: expenditures forming part of the cost of a qualifying intangible asset
prepayments for goods or services before rights are obtained
nearby_distinctions: Immediate expense recognition versus capitalization into intangible asset carrying amounts

descriptors.definition: Entities must choose either the cost model or the revaluation model as an accounting policy for subsequent measurement of intangible assets. Under the cost model, assets are carried at cost less accumulated amortization and impairment, whereas the revaluation model uses fair value based on active markets.
inclusion: carrying amount adjustments for amortization and impairment
fair value revaluations referenced to an active market
exclusion: initial recognition of unrecognized intangible assets via revaluation
selective revaluation of isolated assets without revaluing their entire class
nearby_distinctions: Cost model carrying value tracking versus active market revaluation model

descriptors.definition: Following initial recognition, an intangible asset is accounted for using the cost model by carrying it at cost less any accumulated amortisation and any accumulated impairment losses. This model forms the baseline measurement approach unless the revaluation model option is elected for an entire class of assets.
inclusion: historical cost less amortisation and impairment adjustments
exclusion: fair value adjustments without an active market revaluation policy
nearby_distinctions: Cost model historical tracking versus revaluation model fair value adjustments

descriptors.definition: An intangible asset is carried at a revalued amount representing its fair value at the date of revaluation less subsequent amortisation and impairment losses. Fair value must be determined by reference to an active market, and applying this model requires revaluing all other assets in the same class.
inclusion: Intangible assets with active markets
Assets received via government grant at nominal amounts
exclusion: Previously unrecognized intangible assets
Initial recognition of intangible assets at non-cost amounts
nearby_distinctions: Unlike the cost model which uses historical cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment, the revaluation model uses fair value based on active markets.

descriptors.definition: Useful life defines the period over which an intangible asset is expected to generate economic benefits or the number of production units constituting that life. Entities must assess whether this life is finite or indefinite based on relevant technical, commercial, and legal factors.
inclusion: Expected usage and product life cycles
Legal, regulatory, or contractual limits
exclusion: Planned future expenditures exceeding standard maintenance requirements
nearby_distinctions: Finite useful lives trigger mandatory systematic amortisation, whereas indefinite useful lives require annual impairment testing without amortisation.

descriptors.definition: Intangible assets with finite useful lives are subject to systematic allocation of their depreciable amount over their operational lifespan. Their residual value is presumed to be zero unless a third-party purchase commitment exists or an active market guarantees realizable value.
inclusion: Assets with limited periods of economic benefit
Assets with third-party purchase commitments
exclusion: Assets assessed to have indefinite useful lives
nearby_distinctions: Finite life assets undergo regular amortisation over time, distinguishing them from indefinite life assets which are tested solely for impairment.

descriptors.definition: The depreciable amount represents the cost or substituted valuation of an intangible asset minus its residual value. This amount is systematically allocated across the asset's determined useful life and typically recognized directly in profit or loss.
inclusion: Amortisation costs absorbed in producing other assets like inventories
exclusion: Assets with indefinite useful lives
nearby_distinctions: Depreciable amount calculation relies strictly on asset cost less residual value, distinct from gross carrying values.

descriptors.definition: Residual value is the estimated net disposal amount of an intangible asset at the end of its useful life. It is assumed to be zero unless a third-party commitment or active market reliably supports a higher expected recovery.
inclusion: Third-party commitments to purchase at useful life end
Active market-backed estimated disposal values
exclusion: Standard assumptions of terminal value without active market support
nearby_distinctions: Residual value adjusts the total depreciable base of the asset, separate from periodic impairment losses or amortisation method changes.

descriptors.definition: Amortisation commences when an intangible asset is available for use and ceases at the earlier of classification as held-for-sale or derecognition. The underlying amortisation period must be reviewed annually at each financial year-end to account for changed lifespan estimates.
inclusion: Assets in the location and condition necessary for intended operation
exclusion: Assets idled while still retaining active operational status
nearby_distinctions: Amortisation does not stop simply because an asset is idle, separating it from cessation triggers tied strictly to held-for-sale status or derecognition.

descriptors.definition: The chosen amortisation method must reflect the consumption pattern of the asset's future economic benefits, reverting to straight-line if that pattern is unreliable. A strict rebuttable presumption applies against revenue-based methods unless economic consumption directly correlates with revenue generation.
inclusion: Straight-line, diminishing balance, and units of production methods
exclusion: Revenue-based methods, unless strictly justified under exceptional presumptions
nearby_distinctions: Method selection focuses purely on benefit consumption patterns, which differs from determining the operational length of the amortisation period.

descriptors.definition: Assets with indefinite useful lives are exempt from periodic amortisation but must be tested for impairment annually or whenever indicators arise. Management must continuously review supporting circumstances each period to validate that the indefinite classification remains appropriate.
inclusion: Assets with no foreseeable limit to expected net cash inflows
exclusion: Assets with finite or determinable operational life windows
nearby_distinctions: Indefinite classification replaces systematic amortisation with rigorous annual impairment reviews, unlike finite assets.

descriptors.definition: Intangible asset impairment evaluation follows the framework outlined in Ind AS 36 to verify carrying amounts against recoverable amounts. Assets with indefinite useful lives must be evaluated for impairment at least on an annual basis.
inclusion: Annual reviews for indefinite-life assets
Event-driven impairment checks
exclusion: Standard routine amortisation charges
nearby_distinctions: Impairment captures unexpected declines in service potential or value below carrying cost, distinct from scheduled periodic amortisation.

descriptors.definition: An intangible asset is derecognized upon disposal or when no future economic benefits are expected from its use or retirement. Gains or losses are computed as the difference between net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount, recognized directly in profit or loss.
inclusion: Disposals via sale, finance lease, or donation
Derecognition of replaced component parts
exclusion: Classification of gains as ordinary revenue
nearby_distinctions: Derecognition permanently removes the asset and isolates disposal gains/losses from operating revenue classifications.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive class-by-class disclosures for intangible assets, distinguishing between internally generated assets and other types. Required disclosures cover useful life assessments, amortisation methods, gross carrying balances, and full reconciliation statements of changes.
inclusion: Breakdowns of additions, disposals, and revaluations
Justifications for indefinite useful life assumptions
exclusion: Omission of class-level distinction between internal and external development
nearby_distinctions: Disclosure mandates structured reconciliations of opening to closing carrying amounts, extending beyond basic balance sheet presentations.

descriptors.definition: Financial statement extracts illustrate practical corporate accounting policies, asset measurement rules, and footnote disclosures for intangible assets. They detail specific amortization parameters applied to technical know-how, software, and development rights.
inclusion: Practical company accounting policy disclosures
Applied amortisation schedules for specific asset categories
exclusion: Theoretical framework guidelines without empirical reporting context
nearby_distinctions: Financial extracts provide real-world application examples of standard accounting policies rather than setting new standard rules.

descriptors.definition: The comparative framework highlights key divergences between reporting standards, specifically noting that Ind AS 38 removes certain use-related restrictions from asset definitions and introduces explicit identifiability criteria based on separability or legal rights. These regulatory distinctions alter how entities recognize and evaluate intangible assets compared to previous Indian GAAP frameworks.
inclusion: Differences in scope exclusions
Variations in intangible asset definitions
Divergence in identifiability rules
exclusion: General recognition criteria outside the scope of comparison
Detailed measurement rules of tangible assets
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between Ind AS 38 recognition thresholds and legacy AS 26 requirements regarding separability and probable future economic benefits.
source_ambiguities: The source text is truncated at the end of the excerpt regarding separately acquired intangible assets.

descriptors.definition: The objective is to prescribe the accounting treatment and disclosure requirements for property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation. It establishes the cost model framework for measuring such properties.
inclusion: land held for rentals or capital appreciation
buildings held to earn rentals
exclusion: biological assets
mineral rights
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general asset standards by specifically focusing on rental-generating or appreciation-driven real estate.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies to the recognition, measurement, and disclosure of investment property. It explicitly excludes biological assets tied to agricultural activity and mineral reserves.
inclusion: properties held by owners or lessees as right-of-use assets for rental or appreciation
exclusion: agricultural biological assets
non-regenerative resources like oil and gas
nearby_distinctions: Excludes operating properties covered under agricultural or extractive industry standards.

descriptors.definition: Provides core accounting terminology including investment property, owner-occupied property, fair value, cost, and carrying amount. These definitions govern the classification and valuation rules across financial statements.
inclusion: properties held to earn rental income
properties held for capital appreciation
exclusion: properties used in production or administrative functions
properties held for sale in ordinary course
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between investment properties generating independent cash flows and owner-occupied assets dependent on broader entity operations.

descriptors.definition: Classification depends on whether the property is held for rental or capital appreciation rather than operational use or ordinary sale. Investment properties generate cash flows largely independent of other assets.
inclusion: land held for long-term capital appreciation
vacant buildings held to be leased out
exclusion: properties intended for sale in ordinary course of business
owner-occupied production facilities
nearby_distinctions: Separates investment assets generating independent cash flows from owner-occupied assets requiring operational support.

descriptors.definition: An investment property is recognized when future economic benefits are probable and its cost can be measured reliably. Subsequent day-to-day servicing costs are expensed, while qualifying replacement parts are capitalized and replaced parts derecognized.
inclusion: initial acquisition or construction costs
qualifying subsequent replacement expenditures
exclusion: routine repairs and maintenance labor costs
consumables of day-to-day servicing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between capitalizable structural replacements and expensed routine maintenance.

descriptors.definition: Purchased investment properties are initially measured at cost, including transaction costs and directly attributable expenditures. Start-up costs, abnormal waste, and pre-occupancy operating losses are excluded from initial cost.
inclusion: legal professional fees
property transfer taxes
exclusion: start-up costs
abnormal waste
operating losses before planned occupancy
nearby_distinctions: Separates necessary acquisition overheads from abnormal development inefficiencies and general operational losses.

descriptors.definition: Entities must adopt the cost model as their accounting policy for all investment properties subsequent to initial recognition. Fair value must still be measured and disclosed for informational purposes even when applying the cost model.
inclusion: cost-based carrying amounts adjusted for depreciation and impairment
exclusion: carrying value adjustments via upward revaluations into profit or loss under the cost model
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts the mandatory cost model for balance sheet recognition with the mandatory fair value disclosure requirement.

descriptors.definition: Property transfers to or from investment property occur only when there is an actual change in use supported by evidence. A mere change in management intention does not constitute a change in use and does not alter the carrying amount.
inclusion: commencement of owner-occupation
inception of an operating lease to another party
exclusion: changes in management intent without physical or operational alterations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between substantive operational changes requiring reclassification and subjective intent shifts that do not.

descriptors.definition: Investment properties are derecognized upon disposal or permanent withdrawal when no future economic benefits are expected. Gains or losses are determined as the difference between net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount, recognized in profit or loss.
inclusion: sales of investment property
disposals via finance leases
exclusion: temporary withdrawals from active use
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates permanent derecognition due to retirement or sale from temporary idle holding status.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose their measurement accounting policy, criteria for distinguishing investment properties, rental income amounts, and direct operating expenses. Comprehensive reconciliations of carrying amounts from beginning to end of the period are also required.
inclusion: rental income amounts recognized in profit or loss
gross carrying amount and accumulated depreciation reconciliations
exclusion: omission of fair value disclosures when cost model is adopted
nearby_distinctions: Complements general lease disclosures with property-specific operating and reconciliation disclosures.

descriptors.definition: Provides practical illustrations of financial statement presentation and accounting policy disclosures for investment properties using corporate reporting examples. These extracts demonstrate the application of reporting standards in corporate practice.
inclusion: published financial statement disclosures from listed infrastructure entities
exclusion: hypothetical or unverified reporting formats
nearby_distinctions: Provides empirical presentation examples distinct from theoretical standard definitions.

descriptors.definition: The standard specifies the accounting, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements for non-current assets held for sale and discontinued operations. This segregation helps users evaluate an entity's future cash flows, earnings capacity, and financial position by separating them from continuing operations.
inclusion: Non-current assets held for sale
Disposal groups
Discontinued operations results
exclusion: Continuing operations assets and liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between ongoing operational activities and assets whose value is recovered principally through a sale transaction.

descriptors.definition: The classification and presentation rules apply to all recognized non-current assets and disposal groups, while measurement rules apply generally with specific exclusions. Assets scoped out from measurement under this standard include deferred tax assets, employee benefit assets, financial assets, biological assets, and insurance contracts.
terminology: Fair value less costs to sell
inclusion: All recognized non-current assets
Disposal groups containing scoped-in assets
exclusion: Deferred tax assets
Employee benefit assets
Financial assets under Ind AS 109
Biological assets under Ind AS 41
Insurance contracts under Ind AS 117
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general non-current assets subject to full standard rules and specific asset categories governed by separate financial standards.

descriptors.definition: Key terms include cash-generating units, components of an entity, costs to distribute, costs to sell, and disposal groups utilized throughout the standard. These definitions establish boundaries for identifying separable operations, associated disposal costs, and asset groupings transferred in a single transaction.
inclusion: Definitions governing asset groupings
Disposal costs
Discontinued operations criteria
exclusion: General operational definitions outside the scope of non-current asset disposal
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes individual operational assets from multi-asset disposal groups and cash-generating units.

descriptors.definition: An entity must classify a non-current asset or disposal group as held for sale if its carrying amount will be recovered principally through a sale transaction rather than continuing use. The asset must be available for immediate sale in its present condition, and the sale must be highly probable.
inclusion: Non-current assets available for immediate sale
Disposal groups meeting high probability criteria
exclusion: Current assets sold individually outside a disposal group
Assets held for distant future sale
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes assets utilized continuously in operations from assets held exclusively for immediate recovery through sale.

descriptors.definition: An asset or disposal group must be ready for sale in its current condition with only normal and customary terms for such sales. Assets are not available for immediate sale if they remain vital to ongoing operations or require substantial value-enhancing refurbishments prior to disposal.
inclusion: Assets transferable under standard customary sales terms
Vacating properties within usual timeframes
exclusion: Assets delayed by operational dependencies or enhancement renovations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes customary transitional delays from intentional operational retention or pre-sale value enhancement.

descriptors.definition: A highly probable sale requires management commitment, active marketing at reasonable prices, an active buyer search, and an expected completion within one year without significant plan withdrawal likelihood. Shareholder approval requirements must also be evaluated for feasibility within this assessment.
inclusion: Management commitment plans
Active marketing programs
One-year completion expectations
exclusion: Tentative plans without active marketing or management commitment
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes general management intentions to sell from concrete, highly probable execution plans meeting rigorous procedural criteria.

descriptors.definition: Loss of control in a subsidiary requires classifying all its assets and liabilities as held for sale in consolidated statements regardless of retained non-controlling interests. The one-year completion period can be exceeded if delays stem from events beyond the entity's control and there is sufficient evidence of continued sales commitment.
inclusion: Subsidiary loss of control scenarios
Beyond-control delay circumstances satisfying the one-year exception
exclusion: Delays caused by internal management indecision or controllable factors
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes entity-controlled delays from external, unforeseeable impediments permitting timeframe extensions.

descriptors.definition: Non-current assets or disposal groups classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Costs to sell expected beyond one year are discounted to present value, with time-value increases recognized as financing costs in profit or loss.
terminology: Fair value less costs to sell
inclusion: Measurement at lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell
Present value adjustments for extended disposal periods
exclusion: Continued depreciation after classification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard operational asset valuation models from the lower-of-carrying-amount and fair-value-less-costs-to-sell rule.

descriptors.definition: Assets held for sale are remeasured prior to classification and subsequently evaluated at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Newly acquired assets meeting the criteria are initially measured at what their carrying amount would have been or fair value less costs to sell if acquired in a business combination.
inclusion: Pre-classification carrying amount verification
Business combination initial measurement rules
exclusion: Standard cost-based depreciation models post-classification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard asset acquisition measurement from initial held-for-sale criteria application.

descriptors.definition: Impairment losses are recognized for initial or subsequent write-downs to fair value less costs to sell, while subsequent gains are recognized up to the cumulative impairment previously recorded. Depreciation and amortization of the asset cease immediately upon classification as held for sale.
inclusion: Impairment loss allocation starting with goodwill
Cessation of depreciation
Subsequent gain reversals
exclusion: Interest and liability-associated expenses which continue to be recognized
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes the suspension of depreciation for held-for-sale assets from active operational asset depreciation models.

descriptors.definition: When an asset or disposal group no longer meets held-for-sale criteria, it ceases to be classified as such and is measured at the lower of its pre-classification carrying amount adjusted for intervening depreciation and its recoverable amount. Adjustments are included in continuing operations profit or loss.
inclusion: Reclassification out of held for sale status
Carrying amount adjustments for missed depreciation
exclusion: Retroactive adjustments violating standard transition rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes active held-for-sale assets from assets reverting to operational use due to cancelled sale plans.

descriptors.definition: Non-current assets and disposal group assets and liabilities held for sale must be presented separately on the balance sheet without offsetting them against each other. Major classes of these assets and liabilities must be disclosed, and comparative balance sheet amounts for prior periods are not re-presented.
inclusion: Separate balance sheet presentation of assets and liabilities
Disclosure of major asset and liability classes
exclusion: Offsetting assets against liabilities as a single net amount
Re-presentation of prior period comparative balance sheets
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes current presentation requirements from prior period balance sheet comparative restatement rules.

descriptors.definition: Entities must present non-current assets and disposal groups held for sale separately from other assets and liabilities in the balance sheet without offsetting them. Major classes of these assets and liabilities require separate disclosure, and cumulative income or expense in other comprehensive income must be presented distinctly.
inclusion: Separate balance sheet presentation of assets and liabilities
Separate presentation of cumulative OCI items
Disclosure of major classes of assets and liabilities
exclusion: Offsetting assets and liabilities of a disposal group as a single net amount
Re-presentation of comparative balance sheet amounts for prior periods
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard non-current asset presentation by requiring distinct balance sheet grouping and specific measurement rules.

descriptors.definition: Financial statements must display non-current assets and disposal groups held for sale in a manner that allows users to evaluate their financial effects. Assets and liabilities within a disposal group must be shown separately without netting them against each other.
inclusion: Separate presentation of held for sale assets
Separate presentation of held for sale liabilities
exclusion: Netting off disposal group assets against liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on balance sheet arrangement and layout rules rather than measurement or note disclosure.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive notes detailing the description, facts, circumstances, and expected timing of disposal for assets or disposal groups classified as held for sale. Additional required disclosures include recognized gains or losses, operating segment information, and the operational impacts of any cancelled sale plans.
inclusion: Descriptions of non-current assets or disposal groups
Circumstances and timing of expected disposal
Segment reporting classifications
exclusion: Face of balance sheet line-item values
Cash flow statement line items
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from balance sheet presentation by requiring qualitative descriptive narratives and supplementary details within the notes.

descriptors.definition: A discontinued operation is a component of an entity that has either been disposed of or classified as held for sale and represents a separate major line of business or geographical area. It can also be part of a single coordinated disposal plan or represent an exclusive resale-oriented subsidiary acquisition.
inclusion: Disposed components representing major lines of business
Components classified as held for sale under a coordinated plan
Subsidiaries acquired exclusively for resale
exclusion: Operations merely winding down existing contracts while continuing revenue-earning activities
Ongoing core operations without a formal disposal plan
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general asset sales because it requires the component to represent a separate major line of business or distinct geographical area.

descriptors.definition: A discontinued operation is defined as a component of an entity that is disposed of or classified as held for sale, provided it constitutes a separate major line of business or geographic area. It also encompasses subsidiaries acquired exclusively with a view to resale.
inclusion: Major operating segments disposed of or held for sale
Geographically distinct operational areas
Subsidiaries acquired solely for resale
exclusion: Minor business units that do not constitute a major line of business
Wind-down phases where revenue earning continues normally
nearby_distinctions: Narrower than general asset disposals, applying strictly to significant operational components or major segments.

descriptors.definition: Entities must separate discontinued operations from continuing operations in financial reports to help users evaluate future cash generation capabilities. Prior period comparative figures must be re-presented to reflect operations discontinued by the end of the latest reporting period.
inclusion: Post-tax profit or loss of discontinued operations
Post-tax fair value or disposal gains and losses
Re-presentation of prior comparative periods
exclusion: Merging discontinued operational metrics directly into continuing operational totals
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on comparative restatements and segregating past performance from continuing business lines.

descriptors.definition: The statement of profit and loss must feature a single composite amount representing post-tax results of discontinued operations combined with post-tax disposal or fair value remeasurement gains. An accompanying breakdown of revenues, expenses, pre-tax results, and related income taxes must be provided either on the face or in the notes.
inclusion: Single line item for discontinued operations results
Detailed revenue and expense breakdown
Attributable income disclosures for parent owners
exclusion: Detailed line-item breakdown for newly acquired subsidiaries meeting held-for-sale criteria on acquisition
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between the aggregate single-line disclosure on the income statement face and the detailed supporting analysis.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose net operating, investing, and financing cash flows attributable to discontinued operations either within the financial statements or notes. Earnings per share figures for discontinued operations must also be presented with equal prominence alongside continuing operations.
inclusion: Net cash flows of discontinued operations
Basic and diluted earnings per share for discontinued operations
exclusion: Cash flow disclosures for newly acquired subsidiaries meeting held-for-sale criteria at acquisition
nearby_distinctions: Extends reporting requirements beyond the income statement to cash flow tracking and per-share performance metrics.

descriptors.definition: Basic and diluted earnings per share metrics for discontinued operations must be disclosed separately in the statement of profit and loss or notes. These figures are presented alongside continuing operations metrics with equal prominence.
inclusion: Basic EPS for discontinued operations
Diluted EPS for discontinued operations
exclusion: Combining discontinued EPS directly into a single blended EPS total without separate disclosure
nearby_distinctions: Applies per-share calculation rules distinctively to discontinued segments rather than aggregate company performance alone.

descriptors.definition: Current period adjustments directly linked to prior period discontinued operations must be classified separately within discontinued operations with disclosed natures and amounts. Such adjustments typically arise from resolving transaction purchase prices, indemnifications, or retained environmental, warranty, and employee benefit obligations.
inclusion: Resolution of purchase price uncertainties
Indemnification and warranty settlements
Employee benefit plan settlements directly tied to the disposal
exclusion: Adjustments unrelated to the original disposal transaction or prior component operations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from normal current-year operating adjustments by their retrospective origin tied directly to historical discontinued transactions.

descriptors.definition: When an entity abandons its held-for-sale classification for a component, it must reclassify prior results previously shown under discontinued operations into income from continuing operations for all presented periods. The prior amounts must be clearly described as re-presented.
inclusion: Reclassification of historical operational results
Updating all presented comparative periods
exclusion: Keeping historical results categorized under discontinued operations after a sale plan is cancelled
nearby_distinctions: Applies when operational intent reverses, requiring retrospective reclassification rather than prospective adjustments.

descriptors.definition: Entities committed to sale plans that involve losing control over a subsidiary must disclose relevant discontinued operation information when the subsidiary qualifies as a disposal group. This ensures transparent reporting of structural changes affecting group composition.
inclusion: Disclosures for subsidiaries meeting discontinued operation criteria upon losing control
exclusion: Subsidiary sales that do not result in a loss of control or fail to meet the definition of a discontinued operation
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on ownership control loss events rather than standard asset sales or internal operational restructuring.

descriptors.definition: This section outlines practical examples of financial statement extracts from listed entities regarding assets held for sale and related accounting policies. It highlights structural differences between reporting frameworks for non-current assets and discontinued operations.
inclusion: Financial statement extracts of listed companies
Accounting policy disclosures for held for sale assets
exclusion: General corporate governance disclosures
Tax audit reports
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard-level theoretical provisions by illustrating practical application in corporate annual reports.

descriptors.definition: This section compares normative treatments between Ind AS and previous standards regarding asset classification and disposal frameworks. It contrasts measurement bases, time limitations, and definitions of discontinued versus discontinuing operations.
terminology: fair value less costs to sell
inclusion: Comparative analysis of scope and objectives
Distinctions in measurement and time period criteria
exclusion: Detailed numerical computational problems
Tax accounting rules
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts Ind AS 105 which governs held for sale assets and discontinued operations with AS 24 which focuses solely on discontinuing operations.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 116 establishes a single lessee accounting model requiring recognition of assets and liabilities for most leases on the balance sheet. It ensures that both lessees and lessors provide relevant, faithful representation of lease transactions to assess financial position, performance, and cash flows.
inclusion: Leases conveying the right to use an asset without transferring ownership
exclusion: Fundamental changes to the existing lessor accounting model
nearby_distinctions: Differs from erstwhile Ind AS 17, which used a dual classification model separating operating and finance leases

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 116 applies to all leases including sub-leases of right-of-use assets, except for specific exclusions like mineral exploration, biological assets, service concession arrangements, and certain licenses. It requires evaluating contract terms and substance to identify arrangements that convey the right to control the use of an identified asset for consideration.
inclusion: All standard lease contracts conveying asset control
exclusion: Leases to explore for minerals, oil, and natural gas
Leases of biological assets
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard lease arrangements from specialized contracts governed by separate standard frameworks like Ind AS 41 or Ind AS 106

descriptors.definition: The standard governs all lease contracts universally, provided they do not fall under specific category exemptions such as mineral exploration or biological assets. It mandates consistent application across agreements presenting similar characteristics and factual circumstances.
inclusion: Standard property and equipment leases
exclusion: Intellectual property licences granted by a lessor
Motion picture film licensing agreements
nearby_distinctions: Excludes intangible asset licensing agreements governed by alternative standards while allowing lessee application for certain intangibles

descriptors.definition: Lessees can elect to exempt short-term leases and leases of low-value underlying assets from standard balance sheet recognition requirements. Such exempted lease payments are recognized as an expense on a straight-line or other systematic basis over the lease term.
inclusion: Leases with a term of 12 months or less without purchase options
Leases of low-value assets
exclusion: Leases containing a purchase option evaluated at commencement
nearby_distinctions: Short-term exemptions apply strictly based on terms determined at commencement rather than subsequent duration reductions

descriptors.definition: A contract is or contains a lease if it conveys the right to control the use of an identified asset for a period of time in exchange for consideration. This assessment is performed at the inception date, defined as the earlier of the lease agreement date or the date of commitment to principal terms.
inclusion: Contracts granting rights to use explicitly or implicitly specified assets with economic benefit control
exclusion: Agreements lacking an identified asset or failing to grant asset use direction rights
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes pure service contracts from lease arrangements based on control over the underlying asset use

descriptors.definition: An arrangement requires an identified asset that can be either explicitly specified or implicitly specified when made available to the customer. Assets that are not initially built or whose serial numbers are unstated can still qualify as identified if the supplier must fulfill the contract using a specific asset.
inclusion: Assets uniquely required to fulfill a contract even if unbuilt at inception
exclusion: Assets possessing substantive substitution rights permitting the supplier to swap units freely
nearby_distinctions: Unlike AS 19, Ind AS 116 provides explicit criteria for evaluating implicit asset specification and control direction

descriptors.definition: Contracts combining multiple asset rights or lease elements with services require component separation if the lessee can benefit from the asset independently and the asset is not highly dependent on or interrelated with other assets. If these conditions fail, the bundle is treated as a single lease component.
inclusion: Distinct asset rights usable independently or alongside readily available resources
exclusion: Highly dependent or functionally integrated asset groupings treated as single units
nearby_distinctions: Separates standalone asset usage rights from heavily integrated ancillary equipment combinations

descriptors.definition: Multiple contracts entered near the same time with related counterparties are combined into a single contract if negotiated as a package, priced interdependently, or containing single lease components. Additionally, entities may apply a portfolio approach as a practical expedient for similar leases if financial statement impacts remain immaterial.
inclusion: Contracts negotiated together with interdependent pricing or performance
exclusion: Unrelated individual agreements lacking commercial and financial dependency
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes individual contract assessments from aggregated portfolio treatments designed for large volumes of similar assets

descriptors.definition: The commencement date is when the lessor makes the underlying asset available for use by the lessee, marking the start of the lease term. This date can precede contractual rent due dates or lease agreement stipulations if the lessee takes possession or modifies the asset beforehand.
inclusion: Periods where lessees modify leased spaces prior to commercial operations
exclusion: Dates strictly defined by financial payment schedules disregarding physical asset availability
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes contractual execution milestones from physical operational readiness and asset control transfer

descriptors.definition: Inception date governs contract classification assessments while commencement date triggers initial financial statement recognition. On the commencement date, lessees recognize lease liabilities and right-of-use assets, whereas lessors recognize finance lease net investments.
inclusion: Initial asset and liability recognition events occurring on the asset availability date
exclusion: Recognition procedures delayed until first payment or formal billing milestones
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts the evaluation timing at inception with the actual financial recognition milestone at commencement

descriptors.definition: Contract evaluation occurs at inception, defined by agreement dates or commitment to principal terms. Asset availability dictates the commencement date, which initiates lease accounting recognition irrespective of payment start dates.
inclusion: Evaluation of lease status based on initial commitment milestones
exclusion: Reliance on older accounting standards lacking contract combination guidance
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates the administrative commitment phase from the operational delivery phase of leasing arrangements

descriptors.definition: The lease term comprises the non-cancellable period together with rent-free intervals, optional renewal periods reasonably certain to be exercised, and termination option periods reasonably certain not to be triggered. Assessment of extension certainty depends on economic incentives created by contract, asset, entity, or market factors at commencement.
inclusion: Periods covered by renewal options with economic incentives for exercise
exclusion: Optional periods assessed without supporting economic incentives or based solely on past intentions
nearby_distinctions: Separates baseline contractual periods from extended durations contingent on economic viability and operational incentives

descriptors.definition: Lease payments are consideration components paid by a lessee to a lessor for the right to use an underlying asset throughout the lease term. They incorporate fixed amounts, variable amounts linked to an index or rate, purchase option exercise prices, termination penalties, and specific residual value guarantees.
inclusion: Fixed and in-substance fixed payments
Index or rate-dependent variable payments
Guaranteed residual amounts
exclusion: Non-lease component allocations
Non-index/rate variable payments
nearby_distinctions: Differs from non-lease service component payments unless a single lease component election is made

descriptors.definition: Pre-commencement negotiations may require a lessee to fund asset construction or design costs before use. If the lessee controls the asset prior to transfer to the lessor, the arrangement constitutes a sale and leaseback transaction rather than a standard lease.
inclusion: Pre-commencement asset design expenses
Construction funding by lessee
exclusion: Right-of-use asset payments
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard lease execution payments by focusing on pre-availability asset modifications and control transfer

descriptors.definition: Initial direct costs are incremental expenses incurred to secure a lease that would otherwise have been avoided. Lessees incorporate these amounts into their initial right-of-use asset valuation.
inclusion: Commissions to selling agents
Execution-stage legal fees
exclusion: General employee salaries
Pre-execution legal advice
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from ongoing administrative or pre-execution expenses because they are strictly incremental to obtaining the specific contract

descriptors.definition: Discount rates convert future lease payments to present value for measuring liabilities and assets. Lessees apply the interest rate implicit in the lease, or their incremental borrowing rate if the implicit rate is unobservable.
inclusion: Interest rate implicit in the lease
Lessee incremental borrowing rate
exclusion: Underlying asset borrowing rates unaligned with the right-of-use asset
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by prioritizing the lessor's implicit rate before falling back on the lessee's specific borrowing rate matching the right-of-use asset term

descriptors.definition: Economic life represents either the duration an asset is economically usable by single or multiple users or the total production units obtainable from it. It serves as a benchmark for evaluating lease terms and asset utility.
inclusion: Multi-user operational duration
Total expected production output units
exclusion: Shorter arbitrary contractual terms
nearby_distinctions: Differs from lease term by capturing total potential asset utility across all users rather than just the contractual period

descriptors.definition: Fair value is the exchange price for an asset or liability between informed, willing parties in an arm's length transaction under lessor accounting requirements. It is determined exclusively under legacy provisions without invoking broader measurement standards.
inclusion: Arm's length exchange valuations
exclusion: Valuations derived via Ind AS 113 for this specific scope
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard fair value measurement rules by carrying forward historical principles instead of current general valuation standards

descriptors.definition: Lessee accounting mandates that entities acquiring a right to use an asset recognize a right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability at the commencement date. All qualifying leases are brought onto the balance sheet unless specific short-term or low-value exemptions apply.
inclusion: Initial lease liability present value calculation
Right-of-use asset recognition
exclusion: Exempted short-term leases
Low-value asset leases
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with historical off-balance-sheet operating lease treatment by mandating universal asset and liability capitalization

descriptors.definition: At commencement, a lessee measures its lease liability at the present value of remaining lease payments discounted at the implicit or incremental rate. Simultaneously, a right-of-use asset is recognized incorporating initial direct costs and advance payments.
inclusion: Remaining lease payment discounting
Initial direct cost capitalization
exclusion: Pre-commencement payments
nearby_distinctions: Differs from subsequent measurement by establishing baseline asset and liability values using rates active at lease inception

descriptors.definition: Post-commencement, right-of-use assets are generally measured using a cost model adjusted for depreciation and impairment losses. Alternatively, entities can apply a revaluation model if the asset class matches specific property, plant, and equipment categories.
inclusion: Cost model adjustments
Depreciation over useful life or lease term
exclusion: Initial transaction value without depreciation updates
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial recognition by incorporating continuous adjustments for asset consumption, impairments, and liability remeasurements

descriptors.definition: Lessees update lease liabilities and corresponding right-of-use assets following changes in lease terms, expected residual guarantees, or index-linked payments. Revised discount rates are applied for term or purchase option reassessments, while original rates are retained for index or residual updates.
inclusion: Lease term reassessments
Index-linked payment updates
exclusion: Unresolved negotiating period estimates prior to finalization
nearby_distinctions: Differs from lease modifications by adjusting existing parameters due to reassessments or triggers rather than executing contractual structural changes

descriptors.definition: A lease modification changes the scope or consideration of a lease outside original terms, such as altering the lease term or adding underlying assets. Modifications are accounted for as separate leases if scope increases by commensurate standalone pricing.
inclusion: Scope additions with standalone pricing
Contractual term extensions
exclusion: Routine exercise of existing contractual purchase or renewal options
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from internal remeasuring events because modifications represent legally altered contract scope and consideration negotiated post-commencement

descriptors.definition: Lessees present right-of-use assets and lease liabilities distinctly in the balance sheet, separating depreciation and interest expenses in the profit and loss statement. Cash outflows are split between financing activities for principal and interest, and operating activities for short-term or uncapitalized variable payments.
inclusion: Separate ROU asset presentation
Financing cash flow categorization for principal and interest
exclusion: Combining depreciation and interest expense lines
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes operating cash outflows for short-term leases from financing cash outflows dedicated to capitalized lease liabilities

descriptors.definition: Lessees must present comprehensive qualitative and quantitative disclosures in a single note or separate section to give users a basis to assess the effects of leases. This includes information on right-of-use assets, maturity analyses of lease liabilities, and expenses related to short-term or low-value leases.
inclusion: Additions and carrying value of right-of-use assets
Depreciation and interest expense
Expenses for short-term and low-value leases
Summary of leasing activities and potential cash outflows
exclusion: Leases with terms of one month or less from certain expense disclosures
Non-lease components unless integrated into asset measurement
nearby_distinctions: Differentiated from lessor disclosures which focus heavily on net investment risks, whereas lessee disclosures focus on liability obligations and right-of-use asset utilization.

descriptors.definition: Recognition of lease assets and liabilities by lessees impacts deferred tax asset and liability measurements and recoverability assessments. Lessors classify all leases at inception into either finance or operating leases based on the transfer of risks and rewards incidental to ownership.
inclusion: Deferred tax recognition and measurement
Assessment of deferred tax asset recoverability
Substance-over-form lease classification by lessors
exclusion: Direct lessee tax deductions computed outside the scope of lease capitalization rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between lessee tax timing differences caused by capitalized lease adjustments and initial lessor classification rules based on ownership risks.

descriptors.definition: Lessors evaluate lease agreements at inception to classify them as finance or operating leases according to the transfer of ownership risks and rewards. Indicators include transfer of title, purchase options, major economic life lease terms, and specialized asset nature.
inclusion: Leases transferring ownership by the end of the term
Leases with bargain purchase options
Leases covering the major part of an asset economic life
exclusion: Leases failing to meet risk and reward transfer thresholds which default to operating leases
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts finance leases which shift ownership risks to the lessee with operating leases where the lessor retains those primary asset risks.

descriptors.definition: Lease classification depends on economic substance rather than legal form at the time of inception. The transaction is categorized based on whether substantially all risks and rewards incidental to ownership are transferred to the lessee.
inclusion: Evaluation of transfer of ownership
Assessment of specialized asset utility
exclusion: Form-based legal classifications that ignore underlying cash flow and risk distribution
nearby_distinctions: Focuses purely on the foundational evaluation standard rather than subsequent measurement mechanics.

descriptors.definition: At commencement, a lessor recognizes assets held under a finance lease as a receivable equal to the net investment in the lease. Manufacturer or dealer lessors recognize selling profit or loss in accordance with general revenue policies for outright sales.
inclusion: Recognition of lease receivables discounted at the interest rate implicit in the lease
Derecognition of the underlying asset carrying amount
Recognition of selling profit or loss for dealer lessors
exclusion: Inclusion of initial direct costs in net investment for manufacturer or dealer lessors
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates standard lessors who capitalize initial direct costs into the receivable from manufacturer lessors who expense them immediately.

descriptors.definition: Lessors recognize operating lease payments as income on a straight-line basis or another systematic basis that reflects the benefit pattern. Initial direct costs incurred by lessors are added to the carrying amount of the underlying asset and recognized as an expense over the lease term.
inclusion: Straight-line or systematic recognition of lease income
Capitalization and systematic amortization of initial direct costs
Depreciation and impairment testing of underlying assets
exclusion: Immediate recognition of selling profit upon entering an operating lease
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with finance lease accounting where the asset is derecognized and a net investment receivable is recorded instead.

descriptors.definition: A lease modification is a change in scope or consideration not part of the original terms. It is accounted for as a separate lease if scope increases due to additional underlying assets at standalone prices; otherwise, non-separate modifications are reassessed prospectively.
inclusion: Evaluation of scope and consideration changes
Separate lease accounting when criteria for added assets are fulfilled
Prospective reclassification assessment for non-separate modifications
exclusion: Retrospective adjustments for changes that were anticipated in the original contract terms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between modifications that expand distinct asset rights treated as separate contracts versus changes requiring a combined prospective reassessment.

descriptors.definition: Lessors present finance lease assets as receivables representing the net investment, while operating lease assets are presented according to their specific asset nature. Extensive quantitative and qualitative disclosures are required to communicate cash flow timing and uncertainties.
inclusion: Balance sheet presentation of net investment for finance leases
Asset nature-based presentation for operating leases
Tabular quantitative maturity breakdowns
exclusion: Omission of residual risk management descriptions in qualitative notes
nearby_distinctions: Compares lessor presentation rules under Ind AS 116 with older standards like AS 19 which lacked formal lease modification guidance.

descriptors.definition: Lessor disclosure requirements provide users with insights into the amount, timing, and uncertainty of cash flows from leasing activities. Entities must outline risk management strategies concerning residual values, buy-back agreements, and variable payments.
inclusion: Explanation of leasing activity nature
Risk management practices on retained asset rights
Quantitative breakdowns of finance income and selling profits
exclusion: Standard financial statement line items duplicated without explanatory notes
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on lessor-specific risk exposures like buy-back guarantees rather than lessee liability repayment schedules.

descriptors.definition: A sublease is a transaction where an underlying asset is re-leased by an intermediate lessor to a third party while the original head lease remains active. The intermediate lessor classifies the sublease with reference to the right-of-use asset arising from the head lease rather than the underlying asset.
inclusion: Classification using the head lease right-of-use asset
Operating lease classification if the head lease is a short-term lease
Dual role tracking where the entity acts as both lessee and lessor
exclusion: Using the economic life of the original physical underlying asset for sublease classification criteria
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts primary lease classification which evaluates the underlying physical asset against sublease classification which evaluates the head lease right-of-use asset.

descriptors.definition: An intermediate lessor maintains primary obligations under the head lease while entering a secondary lease agreement with an ultimate sub-lessee. The sublease classification is determined by evaluating terms against the right-of-use asset created by the head contract.
inclusion: Maintenance of head lease accounting obligations
Separate lessor accounting for the sublease agreement
exclusion: Release of primary liability by the intermediate lessor upon executing a sublease
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates the original lessor-lessee dynamic from the layered intermediate structure involving three separate contractual parties.

descriptors.definition: A sale and leaseback involves an asset transfer from a seller-lessee to a buyer-lessor followed by a leaseback of that same asset. Accounting treatment depends on whether the transfer satisfies performance obligations to transfer control under revenue standards.
inclusion: Application of control criteria to determine sale validity
Accounting for transfers as true sales combined with a lease
Treatment of failed sales as financing transactions
exclusion: Automatic off-balance sheet financing classification for lessees
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes valid sales where asset control transfers from failed sales where the transaction is accounted purely as a collateralized borrowing.

descriptors.definition: Entities apply Ind AS 116 starting from the annual reporting period beginning on or after April 1, 2019. The date of initial application represents the start of this annual reporting period when the entity first adopts the standard.
inclusion: Application of lease transition rules from the start of the reporting period
exclusion: Retrospective application prior to the designated inception date without chosen options
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from subsequent measurement rules by focusing exclusively on initial adoption timing.

descriptors.definition: Entities can elect a practical expedient to bypass reassessing whether ongoing contracts contain leases upon transition. This provision applies to all ongoing contracts collectively rather than individual selections.
inclusion: Exempting all existing contracts from lease definition reassessment at transition
exclusion: Selective application of the practical expedient to individual leases
nearby_distinctions: Differs from full reassessment requirements because it preserves historical classifications under older standards for existing agreements.

descriptors.definition: Lessees must transition to the standard using either the full retrospective approach or the modified retrospective approach applied consistently to all leases. The chosen method governs how prior periods and cumulative adjustments are reported.
inclusion: Application of either full retrospective or modified retrospective transition methods
exclusion: Mixing different transition approaches across individual lease contracts
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by whether comparative prior periods are fully restated or adjusted via opening retained earnings.

descriptors.definition: Under the modified retrospective approach, lease liabilities are measured at the present value of remaining payments using the incremental borrowing rate. Right-of-use assets are measured either retrospectively or equal to the lease liability adjusted for prepayments.
inclusion: Measurement of remaining lease payments using the incremental borrowing rate
Adjustment of opening retained earnings for cumulative effects
exclusion: Restatement of comparative prior period financial figures
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with the full retrospective approach by avoiding prior period comparative restatements.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose specific policy details depending on whether they applied the full or modified retrospective transition approach. Required disclosures include the nature of the accounting change and weighted average incremental borrowing rates.
inclusion: Disclosures of financial statement line item impacts under full retrospective adoption
Explanations of differences in operating lease commitments under modified retrospective adoption
exclusion: Omission of transition adjustment explanations when practicable
nearby_distinctions: Varies based on the specific transition path chosen by the entity.

descriptors.definition: Lessors make no transition adjustments except for intermediate lessors reassessing ongoing subleases based on head lease terms. Historical sale and leaseback transactions are not reassessed for sale criteria under newer revenue standards.
inclusion: Reassessment of operating subleases by intermediate lessors
Continuation of historical finance and operating leaseback accounting treatments
exclusion: Retrospective reassessment of historical sale qualifications under revenue standards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard lessors from intermediate lessors who must evaluate ongoing subleases against head lease right-of-use assets.

descriptors.definition: Historical sale and leaseback transactions remain unadjusted, with prior operating leasebacks adjusting right-of-use assets for off-market deferred gains or losses. Favourable or unfavourable operating lease terms previously recognized in business combinations are derecognized against right-of-use assets.
inclusion: Adjustment of leaseback ROU assets for deferred items
Derecognition of pre-existing business combination lease term assets or liabilities
exclusion: Retrospective adjustments to historical sale determinations
nearby_distinctions: Differs from new transactions by locking in historical classifications while only adjusting carrying amounts for specific deferred items.

descriptors.definition: Pre-existing assets or liabilities recognized for favourable or unfavourable lease terms from business combinations are derecognized on transition. Their carrying amounts are adjusted directly into the corresponding right-of-use asset.
inclusion: Derecognition of business combination lease intangibles
Offsetting adjustments to right-of-use asset carrying amounts
exclusion: Retaining separate intangible assets or liabilities for acquired lease terms
nearby_distinctions: Substitutes legacy business combination adjustments with direct modifications to the newly recognized right-of-use asset.

descriptors.definition: Published financial statement extracts illustrate practical balance sheet presentation formats for right-of-use assets and lease liabilities. These disclosures provide empirical reference points for corporate adopters.
inclusion: Illustrative balance sheet line items for listed entities
exclusion: Normative accounting rules or mandatory calculation formulas
nearby_distinctions: Serves as an illustrative disclosure exhibit rather than a standard measurement principle.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 116 replaces risk-and-reward lease classification for lessees with a single control-based right-of-use model requiring asset and liability recognition. Exemptions are introduced for short-term leases and low-value asset leases.
inclusion: Single lessee accounting model for all qualifying leases
Exemptions for short-term and low-value leases
exclusion: Dual operating and finance lease classification for lessees
nearby_distinctions: Replaces the dual classification framework of older standards with a unified capitalization model.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 116 introduces comprehensive guidance centered on control and lease modifications, eliminating lessee lease classification found in older local standards. It also aligns sale and leaseback accounting with revenue recognition standards.
inclusion: Detailed control assessment guidance
Unified lessee accounting without operating and finance distinctions
exclusion: Deferral and amortization of sale and leaseback profits under older local rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes modern control-based accounting frameworks from older local accounting standards that relied on risk transfer classifications.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 116 incorporates specific national carve-outs from global standards, notably prohibiting fair value models for investment property right-of-use assets. Furthermore, it mandates that interest payments on lease liabilities be classified exclusively as financing activities.
inclusion: Mandatory financing activity classification for lease interest payments
Deletion of fair value measurement options for investment property right-of-use assets
exclusion: Operating activity classification options for lease interest payments
nearby_distinctions: Differs from international norms by enforcing rigid cash flow classifications and disallowing fair value options for investment properties.

descriptors.definition: The standard prescribes accounting and disclosure for employee benefits, requiring entities to recognize a liability for services received and an expense when economic benefits are consumed. Accrual accounting principles govern these obligations so that employment costs are recorded in the periods corresponding to the services rendered.
inclusion: Formal employee benefit plans
Statutory or industry arrangement contributions
Informal practices creating constructive obligations
exclusion: Share-based payment transactions under Ind AS 102
Reporting by employee benefit plans themselves
nearby_distinctions: Unlike equity transactions with owners, employee benefits are operating expenses reflecting consumption of services.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 19 applies to all employer accounting for employee benefits except those covered under share-based payment standards. The framework encompasses formal agreements, legal mandates, and informal practices that generate constructive obligations.
inclusion: Benefits provided under formal agreements
Nation, state, or industry multi-employer contributions
Informal company practices
exclusion: Share-based payment transactions
Financial reporting by employee benefit plans
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general liability recognition by specifically addressing obligations arising from human resource deployment and service contracts.

descriptors.definition: Employee benefits include all forms of consideration given by an entity in exchange for services rendered or for the termination of employment. These provisions extend to payments made directly to employees, their dependents, beneficiaries, or external third parties such as insurance companies.
inclusion: Full-time and part-time employee provisions
Permanent, casual, and temporary worker benefits
Payments to third-party insurers
exclusion: Equity instruments governed strictly under share-based payment standards
nearby_distinctions: Encompasses direct remuneration as well as indirect provisions channeled to family members or insurance providers.

descriptors.definition: Employee benefits are categorized into short-term, post-employment, other long-term, and termination benefits based on their timing and settlement characteristics.
