Each classification requires distinct measurement rules reflecting when the related service is performed and when the liability is expected to be extinguished.
inclusion: Wages, salaries, and social security contributions
Retirement pensions and lump-sum payments
Sabbatical leave and jubilee benefits
Voluntary retirement scheme compensation
exclusion: Transactions addressed by other non-employment accounting standards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by the expected period of settlement relative to the annual reporting date rather than the nature of the work.

descriptors.definition: Short-term benefits are expected to be settled wholly before twelve months after the annual reporting period, whereas post-employment and other long-term benefits are payable after completion of employment or over extended periods. Termination benefits specifically arise from the early cessation of an employment contract.
inclusion: Annual salaries and paid sick leave
Retirement gratuities and pensions
Retrenchment compensation
exclusion: Share-based employee options
nearby_distinctions: Separates short-term settlement timelines from post-employment obligations requiring actuarial discounting.

descriptors.definition: Post-employment benefit plans comprise formal or informal arrangements to provide benefits upon completion of employment, categorized into defined contribution and defined benefit plans. Multi-employer plans pool assets from unrelated entities to provide common benefits without linking contributions to a specific employer's staff profile.
inclusion: Provident fund arrangements
Gratuity schemes
State and industry-managed contribution pools
exclusion: Short-term operational bonus agreements
nearby_distinctions: Defined contribution plans cap the entity's risk via fixed payments, whereas defined benefit plans expose the entity to actuarial and investment risks.

descriptors.definition: Net defined benefit liability or asset is the plan deficit or surplus adjusted for any asset ceiling limits. Plan assets and qualifying insurance policies are measured at fair value to offset the present value of the defined benefit obligation.
terminology: Present Value of Defined Benefit Obligation
inclusion: Funds held in legally separate long-term employee benefit entities
Insurance policies issued by unrelated parties dedicated to funding benefits
exclusion: Non-transferable financial instruments issued by the reporting entity itself
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general corporate assets and restricted plan assets unavailable to general creditors.

descriptors.definition: Defined benefit cost comprises service cost, net interest on the net defined benefit liability or asset, and remeasurements. Service cost includes current service cost, past service cost from plan amendments, and gains or losses on settlements.
inclusion: Current period service increases
Impact of plan amendments and curtailments
Actuarial experience adjustments and assumption changes
exclusion: Standard administrative costs of managing general corporate operations
nearby_distinctions: Isolates the time-value interest component and actuarial volatility from standard operational service expenses.

descriptors.definition: Short-term employee benefits are undiscounted obligations expected to be settled wholly within twelve months after the end of the annual reporting period. They encompass wages, salaries, paid absences, profit-sharing, and non-monetary perks provided to current workers.
inclusion: Wages and social security contributions
Paid annual and sick leave
Short-term bonuses and medical care
exclusion: Post-employment retirement benefits requiring actuarial valuation
nearby_distinctions: Measured without actuarial discounting because settlement occurs within a short twelve-month horizon.

descriptors.definition: Short-term benefits are recognized as an undiscounted liability after deducting any amounts already paid, or as a prepaid expense if excess payments generate future economic reductions. Paid absences are categorized into accumulating and non-accumulating types based on whether unused entitlements carry forward.
inclusion: Accrued salary expenses
Vesting and non-vesting accumulating leave entitlements
exclusion: Long-term sabbatical leaves evaluated under separate multi-period models
nearby_distinctions: Requires immediate expense recognition for non-accumulating absences only when the absence actually occurs.

descriptors.definition: Short-term paid absences allow employees to take time off for holidays, illness, or family milestones while continuing to receive compensation. Accumulating forms carry forward to future periods and may be vesting, granting cash payouts upon exit, or non-vesting.
inclusion: Paid annual leave balances
Sick leave and maternity leave compensations
exclusion: Post-employment retirement gratuities
nearby_distinctions: Vesting leave provisions create immediate exit-settlement obligations, whereas non-vesting entitlements depend on continued service utilization.

descriptors.definition: Profit-sharing and bonus obligations are recognized when an entity has a present legal or constructive obligation resulting from past events and a reliable estimate can be made. Because these payments stem from employee service, they are recorded as operating expenses rather than equity distributions.
inclusion: Formal formula-based bonus schemes
Informal bonus practices generating constructive obligations
exclusion: Dividend distributions to equity shareholders
nearby_distinctions: Classified as operating expenses rather than profit distributions because the obligation arises directly from employee labor input.

descriptors.definition: Short-term employee benefits do not mandate specific disclosures under the standard, though other frameworks such as Ind AS 1 and Ind AS 24 require reporting employee expenses and key management personnel benefits. Post-employment benefits encompass retirement pensions, lump-sum distributions, life insurance, and medical care, which are segregated based on plan substance.
inclusion: General employee benefit expenses
Key management personnel compensation disclosures
exclusion: Detailed actuarial tables for short-term obligations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general short-term disclosures and comprehensive post-employment actuarial reporting.

descriptors.definition: Post-employment benefits represent formal or informal arrangements providing retirement benefits and post-retirement medical or life care to employees. These arrangements are fundamentally categorized into defined contribution plans and defined benefit plans based on the underlying economic substance and risk allocation.
inclusion: Pensions
Lump-sum retirement payments
Post-employment life insurance and medical care
exclusion: Short-term employee wages
Termination benefits
nearby_distinctions: Separates long-term deferred post-retirement benefits from short-term compensation obligations.

descriptors.definition: Defined contribution plans limit the entity's obligation to predetermined amounts, placing actuarial and investment risks on the employee. Conversely, defined benefit plans oblige the entity to supply agreed benefits, shifting actuarial and investment vulnerabilities directly onto the employer.
inclusion: Plans with fixed contributions
Plans guaranteeing specific benefit formulas or minimum returns
exclusion: State-administered general security frameworks without entity guarantees
nearby_distinctions: Defined contribution shifts market volatility risks to employees, whereas defined benefit retains those financial risks with the reporting entity.

descriptors.definition: Multi-employer plans pool assets from multiple unrelated entities and must be classified as either defined contribution or defined benefit arrangements based on their terms. When sufficient information is absent for a multi-employer defined benefit plan, the entity accounts for it as a defined contribution plan alongside specific required disclosures.
inclusion: Pooled employer pension arrangements
Industry-wide benefit funds
exclusion: Single-employer standalone administration plans
nearby_distinctions: Unlike single-employer plans, multi-employer structures commingle assets and liabilities across unrelated employing entities.

descriptors.definition: Group administration plans aggregate single-employer plans exclusively for joint asset investment and administrative cost reduction while maintaining strict segregation of individual employer claims. Because individual identities and risks are preserved, these arrangements do not introduce complex multi-employer accounting hurdles.
inclusion: Aggregated single-employer investment pools
exclusion: Multi-employer pools where individual employee identities are lost
nearby_distinctions: Maintains distinct asset and liability tracking per participating entity, unlike multi-employer pools.

descriptors.definition: Plans sharing risks between entities under common control, such as parents and subsidiaries, require the participating entity to gather whole-plan assumptions and recognize net benefit costs according to formal group policy or contractual agreements. In the absence of an allocation policy, the sponsoring legal employer records the net cost while other group entities account only for their payable contributions.
inclusion: Intra-group parent-subsidiary pension arrangements
exclusion: Multi-employer plans involving unrelated entities
nearby_distinctions: Governs risk-sharing exclusively within corporate groups under common control rather than external pooled arrangements.

descriptors.definition: State plans are established by legislation across broad industries or sectors and operated by governmental or autonomous bodies independent of the reporting entity. These schemes are typically funded on a pay-as-you-go basis and are normally accounted for as defined contribution plans unless explicit entity obligations dictate otherwise.
inclusion: Government-mandated industry social security schemes
exclusion: Entity-established plans providing voluntary benefits supplementary to state provisions
nearby_distinctions: Operated entirely by external statutory authorities rather than internal corporate administration.

descriptors.definition: Entities funding post-employment obligations via insurance premiums normally classify the arrangement as a defined contribution plan unless legal or constructive retention of benefit obligations exists. Where obligations are retained, the policy is treated as a qualifying plan asset or reimbursement right rather than a direct settlement.
inclusion: Insurance policies funding employee retirement plans
Fixed premium settlements
exclusion: Policies where the entity holds ongoing constructive obligations without qualifying asset recognition
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between complete transfer of risk to an insurer versus entity-retained payout obligations.

descriptors.definition: Accounting for defined contribution plans involves recognizing the contribution payable for employee service rendered during the period as an accrued liability or prepaid asset. These obligations are measured on an undiscounted basis unless they fall due beyond twelve months after the reporting period.
inclusion: Accrued contributions payable
Prepaid contributions leading to refunds or future reductions
exclusion: Actuarial gains and losses associated with defined benefit obligations
nearby_distinctions: Excludes complex actuarial discount estimations required for defined benefit structures.

descriptors.definition: The entity recognizes contributions payable for employee services as an expense or asset cost, offset by any pre-payments made. Excess contributions paid are recorded as prepayments to the extent that they secure future reductions or cash refunds.
inclusion: Undiscounted short-term contribution liabilities
exclusion: Multi-period actuarial adjustments
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on matching payable contributions to service periods without actuarial revaluation.

descriptors.definition: Entities must explicitly disclose the total amount recognized as an expense for defined contribution plans during the reporting period. Additional disclosures regarding key management personnel contributions must also be provided where mandated by related party standards.
inclusion: Total defined contribution plan expense amount
exclusion: Detailed actuarial sensitivity analyses applicable to defined benefit plans
nearby_distinctions: Requires simplified expense totals rather than comprehensive asset-liability reconciliation schedules.

descriptors.definition: Accounting for defined benefit plans is inherently complex because it requires actuarial assumptions, accounts for potential actuarial gains and losses, and discounts long-term obligations to present value. Statutory requirements such as gratuity obligations must be recognized via accrual accounting rather than cash-basis recording.
inclusion: Statutory gratuity provisions
Discounted long-term employee retirement obligations
exclusion: Simple cash-basis accounting policies for long-term employee liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Demands rigorous actuarial estimation models, differentiating it from straightforward undiscounted defined contribution accounting.

descriptors.definition: Defined benefit plans involve estimating employee benefits earned in current and prior periods using actuarial techniques and discounting them to present value. The resulting obligation is adjusted by deducting the fair value of plan assets to determine any net deficit or surplus.
inclusion: Unfunded and funded defined benefit plans
Actuarial estimations of demographic and financial variables
exclusion: Contributions due for the period without actuarial valuation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from defined contribution plans where an entity's obligation is strictly limited to the amount it agrees to contribute to the fund.

descriptors.definition: Constructive obligations arise from informal entity practices where there is no realistic alternative to paying employee benefits, forcing the assumption that benefit promises will continue. When a plan generates a surplus, the net defined benefit asset is measured at the lower of the surplus and the asset ceiling.
inclusion: Obligations resulting from informal practices causing unacceptable damage to employee relations
Surplus assets measured against the asset ceiling
exclusion: Formal plan terminations executed without retaining employees or incurring payment obligations
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Ind AS 12 deferred tax assets where establishing probability of future taxable profit is mandatory, whereas Ind AS 19 requires no such probability assessment for net defined benefit assets.

descriptors.definition: Entities must recognize the net defined benefit liability or asset directly on the balance sheet. Net defined benefit assets are restricted to the lower of the plan surplus or the asset ceiling determined through discounting.
inclusion: Presentation of deficits as non-current liabilities under provisions
Control of resources providing future economic benefits via contribution reductions or cash refunds
exclusion: Unfunded commitments not assessed through formal present value and plan asset matching
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with standard deferred tax assets that depend strictly on future taxable profit probabilities rather than explicit plan asset trust investments.

descriptors.definition: Measuring post-employment benefit obligations requires applying an actuarial valuation method, attributing benefits to service periods, and utilizing appropriate actuarial assumptions. Because final costs depend on uncertain long-term variables like salaries and turnover, structured valuation is necessary.
inclusion: Variables including final salaries, mortality, employee turnover, and medical cost trends
exclusion: Fixed-cost assumptions ignoring long-term demographic and financial fluctuations
nearby_distinctions: Differs from simple short-term accruals by factoring in multi-year service periods and compounding variables.

descriptors.definition: The Projected Unit Credit Method is employed to ascertain present values of obligations and current service costs by treating each service period as an independent unit of benefit entitlement. This method builds up the cumulative obligation through separate measurements of individual service units.
inclusion: Attribution of prior and current year benefits based on compounding salary growth rates and discount parameters
exclusion: Static benefit accounting that ignores future salary increments and service duration
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from total-obligation lump-sum approaches by segregating benefits into incremental yearly service units.

descriptors.definition: Entities attribute benefits to service periods based on the plan's formula, utilizing straight-line allocation if later service yields materially higher benefits. This attribution spans from the initial date service leads to benefits until further service yields no material benefit increases outside of salary adjustments.
inclusion: Obligations arising from employee service even prior to formal vesting
Discounted present values reflecting expected employee departure dates
exclusion: Attribution models failing to adjust for disproportionate benefit surges in later working years
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard period-cost matching by linking the liability creation directly to historical and current employee service delivery.

descriptors.definition: Actuarial assumptions represent an entity's unbiased and mutually compatible best estimates of demographic and financial variables determining ultimate benefit costs. Financial assumptions are typically established in nominal terms using market expectations at the reporting period end.
inclusion: Mortality, employee turnover, disability, early retirement, and medical claim rates
Discount rates, future salary levels, and plan contribution taxes
exclusion: Imprudent or excessively conservative estimates that lack mutual economic compatibility
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from static historical costs by relying on dynamic future market expectations and demographic projections.

descriptors.definition: Plan assets are measured at fair value and deducted from the present value of defined benefit obligations to determine deficits or surpluses. These assets exclude unpaid entity contributions, non-transferable entity instruments, and non-benefit fund liabilities.
inclusion: Qualifying insurance policies matching benefit amount and timing
Reimbursement rights recognized as separate assets when virtually certain
exclusion: Unpaid company contributions and non-transferable instruments issued by the entity
Non-qualifying insurance policies treated as general reimbursement rights rather than plan assets
nearby_distinctions: Differs from non-qualifying insurance policies which are handled as separate reimbursement assets rather than direct deductions from the obligation.

descriptors.definition: The fair value of plan assets is deducted from the present value of the defined benefit obligation to calculate plan deficits or surpluses. Plan assets exclude unpaid company contributions and non-transferable instruments issued by the reporting entity.
inclusion: Deduction of fair value of plan assets from obligation present values
Qualifying insurance policies matching benefit terms
exclusion: Fund liabilities unrelated to employee benefits such as trade payables and derivatives
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with non-qualifying insurance policies that cannot offset the obligation directly and must be accounted for as distinct reimbursement assets.

descriptors.definition: An entity recognizes a right to reimbursement as a separate asset only when recovery from a third party is virtually certain. Defined benefit costs are parsed into service costs, net interest, and remeasurements, with remeasurements recognized entirely in other comprehensive income.
inclusion: Separate asset recognition for non-qualifying insurance policy reimbursements
Non-reclassifiable remeasurements recognized in other comprehensive income
exclusion: Reclassification of OCI remeasurements back to profit or loss in subsequent periods
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes third-party insurer reimbursements from internal plan assets by requiring separate asset presentation unless tied to a qualifying insurance policy.

descriptors.definition: Defined benefit costs comprise service costs and net interest recognized in profit or loss, alongside remeasurements recognized in other comprehensive income. Net interest is determined by multiplying the net defined benefit liability or asset by the specified discount rate.
inclusion: Service costs recognized in profit or loss unless capitalized under specific standards
Net interest calculated using opening or remeasured discount rates
exclusion: Reclassification of OCI remeasurements into profit or loss during subsequent accounting periods
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes operating service and financing interest components routed through profit or loss from volatile actuarial remeasurements isolated in other comprehensive income.

descriptors.definition: Net interest on the net defined benefit liability or asset is calculated by applying the discount rate to the net liability or asset position at the start of the period. It integrates interest cost on obligations, interest income on plan assets, and interest on any asset ceiling effects.
inclusion: Products of fair value of plan assets and discount rates evaluated at the period start
Adjustments reflecting contributions and benefit payments
exclusion: Variations between actual return on plan assets and calculated interest income, which route to remeasurements
nearby_distinctions: Separates predictable interest income derived from discount rates applied to plan assets from actual total asset returns containing actuarial variances.

descriptors.definition: Remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability or asset comprise actuarial gains and losses, the return on plan assets excluding amounts included in net interest, and changes in the effect of the asset ceiling excluding net interest amounts. Actuarial gains and losses arise from changes in actuarial assumptions and experience adjustments in measuring the defined benefit obligation.
inclusion: Actuarial gains and losses from assumption changes
Experience adjustments
Return on plan assets excluding net interest components
Changes in asset ceiling effect excluding net interest
exclusion: Past service cost
Gains or losses on settlement
Current service cost
Net interest on net defined benefit liability
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from past service costs which stem from plan amendments or curtailments rather than demographic or financial assumption variances.

descriptors.definition: Presentation standards for post-employment benefits govern criteria for offsetting assets and liabilities across different plans and dictate adherence to general presentation frameworks. An entity offsets plan assets against liabilities only when it holds a legally enforceable right to use a surplus to settle obligations and intends to settle net or realize simultaneously.
inclusion: Criteria for offsetting assets and liabilities of separate plans
General presentation guidelines via other standards
exclusion: Mandatory strict bifurcation of current and non-current portions by this standard alone
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from disclosure obligations as it governs the face financial statement positioning and offsetting rules.

descriptors.definition: Plan assets and liabilities can be offset if and only if the entity possesses a legally enforceable right to use a surplus in one plan to settle another and intends to settle on a net basis or simultaneously realize and settle. These criteria align with the framework established for financial instruments.
inclusion: Offsetting asset relating to one plan against liability of another under strict conditions
exclusion: Offsetting without legal enforceability
Offsetting lacking simultaneous realization or net settlement intent
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general presentation since it imposes strict legal and operational prerequisites before balances can be netted.

descriptors.definition: The standard leaves the separation of current and non-current portions of post-employment benefit assets and liabilities unspecified. Entities determine financial statement presentation categories by applying broader accounting presentation standards.
inclusion: Deferral to general presentation standards for classifying employee benefit balances
exclusion: Explicit standard-prescribed formulas for splitting benefit assets into current buckets
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from explicit calculation rules since the standard intentionally omits a mandatory classification format.

descriptors.definition: The standard does not mandate a specific presentation format for current service cost and net interest cost components of defined benefit liabilities. Entities present these specific cost elements following general financial statement presentation standards.
inclusion: Application of general presentation standards to service and interest cost components
exclusion: Prescriptive sub-classifications mandated directly by the employee benefits standard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from measurement rules because it governs how recognized cost components appear in financial statements.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose information enabling financial statement users to evaluate the nature of defined benefit plans and the financial effects of changes during the period. Required disclosures cover plan characteristics, associated risks, and potential impacts on future cash flows.
inclusion: Evaluations of plan nature and financial effect
Explanations of plan characteristics and associated risks
exclusion: Unrelated general operational disclosures outside the scope of employee benefit liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from recognition and measurement requirements as it focuses entirely on informative note disclosures for statement users.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide disclosures explaining plan characteristics, associated risks, and the amounts recognized in financial statements arising from defined benefit plans. Additional supplemental details must be given if standard disclosures are insufficient to meet user evaluation objectives.
inclusion: Explanations of plan characteristics and risk concentrations
Supplemental analyses of defined benefit obligations
exclusion: Omission of details when standard disclosures fail to meet user evaluation needs
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from specific numerical reconciliations by serving as qualitative and contextual background for plan obligations.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose the nature of plan benefits, the operational regulatory framework, governance responsibilities, and unusual plan-specific risks. This includes detailing potential risk concentrations such as heavy asset exposure to specific market classes.
inclusion: Nature of plan benefits
Regulatory framework description and asset ceiling effects
Governance responsibilities and unusual risk concentrations
exclusion: Generic entity-wide business risks unrelated to specific employee benefit plans
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from financial reconciliations because it emphasizes qualitative governance, regulatory structures, and risk profiles.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive opening-to-closing reconciliations for net defined benefit liabilities or assets, plan assets, obligations, and asset ceilings. Disclosures must segregate items like current service costs, interest, remeasurements, past service costs, and disaggregate plan assets by quoted market price availability.
inclusion: Opening to closing balance reconciliations for net defined benefit items
Disaggregation of plan assets into quoted and unquoted classes
exclusion: Omission of separate past service cost tracking when permitted alongside simultaneous settlement adjustments
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from plan characteristic descriptions by focusing on quantitative ledger roll-forwards and financial statement line-item movements.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose a sensitivity analysis for each significant actuarial assumption alongside underlying methods and limitations to indicate future cash flow impacts. Furthermore, disclosures must detail funding arrangements, expected contributions for the next period, and the maturity profile of obligations.
inclusion: Sensitivity analyses for significant actuarial assumptions
Expected contributions for the next annual period
Maturity profile and duration of the defined benefit obligation
exclusion: General corporate cash flow forecasts unrelated to employee benefit plan obligations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from historical reconciliations by focusing on predictive metrics, future cash flow impacts, and assumption sensitivity.

descriptors.definition: Participating entities in multi-employer defined benefit plans must disclose funding arrangements, potential liabilities for other entities' obligations, and agreed deficit or surplus allocation terms. If accounted for as defined contribution plans due to data limits, specific alternative disclosures regarding deficits and participation levels are required.
inclusion: Funding arrangements and contribution determination methods
Liabilities for other participating entities' obligations
Surplus or deficit allocation terms upon wind-up or withdrawal
exclusion: Standard single-employer detailed asset and obligation reconciliations when sufficient data is absent and treated as defined contribution
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from single-employer plans due to shared risk structures and the need to disclose contingent liabilities involving other participating entities.

descriptors.definition: Entities participating in common control defined benefit plans must disclose cost-charging policies, contribution-determining methods, and relevant plan-wide disclosures or cross-references. Disclosures can reference another group entity financial statement if that report separately identifies information and is publicly available.
inclusion: Contractual agreements or policies for charging net defined benefit cost
Policies for determining entity contributions
Cross-referencing group entity statements under specific availability criteria
exclusion: Independent single-entity plans lacking common control risk-sharing arrangements
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from multi-employer plans by focusing on corporate group common control dynamics rather than unrelated participating entities.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide disclosures concerning post-employment benefit plans and key management personnel under separate accounting standards. Additionally, disclosures regarding contingent liabilities arising from employee benefit obligations are required.
inclusion: Related party transactions with post-employment benefit plans
Contingent liabilities from post-employment benefit obligations
exclusion: Direct standard-specific disclosures covered entirely within Ind AS 19
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard-internal disclosures by relying strictly on external standard mandates like Ind AS 24 and Ind AS 37.

descriptors.definition: Other long-term employee benefits are employee benefits not expected to be settled wholly within twelve months after the annual reporting period in which related services are rendered. They encompass long-term absences, jubilee benefits, and long-term disability benefits.
inclusion: Long-service or sabbatical leave
Long-term disability benefits
Profit-sharing and bonuses
exclusion: Short-term employee benefits
Post-employment benefits
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from short-term benefits by settlement timelines exceeding twelve months, and from post-employment benefits by lower measurement uncertainty and lack of OCI remeasurement recognition.

descriptors.definition: Entities recognize the net total of service cost, net interest, and remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability or asset in profit or loss. Obligations for long-term disability depend on service duration and payment probabilities, or trigger upon the disabling event.
inclusion: Service cost components
Net interest on net defined benefit liability or asset
Remeasurements in profit or loss
exclusion: Remeasurements recognized in other comprehensive income for post-employment benefits
nearby_distinctions: Differs from post-employment benefit accounting by routing remeasurements directly to profit or loss instead of other comprehensive income.

descriptors.definition: While specific disclosures are not mandated directly within the standard for other long-term benefits, general financial statement requirements and related party rules apply. Material expenses require separate presentation according to general presentation principles.
inclusion: Material expense disclosures
Key management personnel benefit disclosures
exclusion: Standard-specific standalone disclosure tables within Ind AS 19
nearby_distinctions: Relies on external standard frameworks for disclosure obligations rather than dedicated section requirements.

descriptors.definition: Termination benefits arise from an entity's decision to terminate employment or an employee's acceptance of an offer in exchange for termination. They are treated separately from other employee benefits because the obligating event is termination rather than service.
inclusion: Lump-sum termination payments
Enhancement of post-employment benefits
Salary until notice period without future economic service
exclusion: Benefits resulting from employee requests without entity offers
Mandatory retirement requirements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from post-employment benefits by being triggered by termination of employment rather than in exchange for employee service delivery.

descriptors.definition: An entity recognizes a liability and expense for termination benefits at the earlier of when the offer can no longer be withdrawn or when restructuring costs involving termination benefits are recognized under Ind AS 37. Withdrawal restrictions depend on employee acceptance criteria or formal communication of a termination plan.
inclusion: Recognition upon loss of withdrawal rights
Recognition alongside restructuring costs
exclusion: Deferred recognition past the point of irrevocable offer communication
nearby_distinctions: Differs from service-linked benefit recognition by anchoring the trigger to the irrevocable termination decision or formal plan announcement.

descriptors.definition: Termination benefits are measured based on their specific benefit nature, applying post-employment rules if they enhance post-employment benefits. Otherwise, short-term or other long-term employee benefit rules apply depending on settlement expectations.
inclusion: Post-employment benefit rules for enhancements
Short-term rules for short-term settlements
Other long-term rules for delayed settlements
exclusion: Attribution concepts relating to periods of service
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard service-based benefits because service attribution concepts do not apply since benefits are not given in exchange for service.

descriptors.definition: Termination benefits do not trigger specific standalone disclosures within the standard, but external standards require relevant information. Key management personnel termination disclosures and total employee benefit expenses must be reported.
inclusion: Key management personnel termination disclosures
Overall employee benefits expense reporting
exclusion: Detailed standalone termination benefit disclosure schedules within the standard
nearby_distinctions: Relies on general reporting rules and related party standards rather than specialized termination disclosure requirements.

descriptors.definition: Net defined benefit asset measurement is capped at the lower of the plan surplus and the asset ceiling, representing present economic benefits via refunds or contribution reductions. Minimum funding requirements can limit contribution reductions and potentially create additional liabilities.
inclusion: Asset ceiling limitations
Minimum funding requirement impact analysis
exclusion: Unrestricted asset measurements ignoring plan caps
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard asset recognition by imposing an external economic benefit ceiling and adjusting for statutory funding minimums.

descriptors.definition: The standard restricts defined benefit asset measurement to the lower of surplus or asset ceiling, which consists of available refunds or reduced future contributions. Minimum funding rules can restrict contribution reductions and create onerous liabilities if contributions are unavailable.
inclusion: Surplus versus asset ceiling comparisons
Onerous minimum funding liability assessments
exclusion: Uncapped asset surplus recognitions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard asset valuations from capped valuations influenced by minimum funding mandates.

descriptors.definition: This guidance applies universally to all post-employment and other long-term defined benefit plans governed by minimum funding obligations. It addresses when refunds or contribution reductions are available and how funding requirements interact with asset limits.
inclusion: Post-employment defined benefit plans
Other long-term employee defined benefit plans
exclusion: Short-term employee benefit arrangements
nearby_distinctions: Restricts application specifically to defined benefit structures and long-term plans subject to funding requirements, excluding short-term plans.

descriptors.definition: The framework resolves uncertainties regarding the availability of asset ceiling refunds, the impact of minimum funding requirements on future contribution reductions, and conditions triggering additional liabilities.
inclusion: Refund and contribution reduction availability
Minimum funding requirement impact determination
exclusion: Unrestricted asset ceiling assumptions
nearby_distinctions: Focuses directly on regulatory interaction issues rather than general calculation of service costs.

descriptors.definition: An entity evaluates economic benefits from a plan surplus as a refund or reduced future contributions based on plan terms and statutory rules. The maximum available benefit must be determined without mutually exclusive assumptions or reliance on uncertain future events outside the entity's control.
inclusion: economic benefits realizable during plan life or upon settlement
refunds based on gradual or full settlement of plan liabilities
exclusion: surplus refunds dependent on uncertain future events outside entity control
mutually exclusive combinations of refunds and contribution reductions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard post-employment liability measurements by focusing strictly on the asset ceiling limits and realizable surplus conditions.

descriptors.definition: Reporting entities disclose specific accounting policies for employee benefits encompassing short-term compensation, defined contribution plans, and defined benefit plans. Obligations for defined benefit gratuity plans are actuarially measured using the projected unit credit method with re-measurements routed through other comprehensive income.
inclusion: wages, salaries, and bonuses
gratuity plan obligations and actuarial gains and losses
exclusion: unrecognized informal commitments outside established plan parameters
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general provisions by applying specialized actuarial discounting and specific other comprehensive income recognition rules for post-employment benefits.

descriptors.definition: Accounting frameworks diverge regarding employee benefit definitions, constructive obligations, and the timing of past service cost recognition. Ind AS 19 mandates immediate expense recognition for past service costs upon plan amendment or curtailment, unlike the amortized vesting approach in older standards.
inclusion: comparative criteria for employee definition including non-whole-time directors
related party disclosures for common control risk-sharing defined benefit plans
exclusion: straight-line amortization of past service cost over the average vesting period
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from AS 15 by eliminating the deferred amortization window for past service costs and explicitly broadening the definition of an employee.

descriptors.definition: The standard ensures appropriate recognition criteria and measurement bases are applied to provisions, contingent liabilities, and contingent assets. It also requires sufficient note disclosures regarding their nature, timing, and amount.
inclusion: Provisions
Contingent liabilities
Contingent assets
exclusion: Financial instruments under Ind AS 109
Income taxes under Ind AS 12
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between recognized provisions and unrecognised contingent items based on probability and measurement reliability.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies to all entities for provisions, contingent liabilities, and contingent assets, excluding items addressed by other specific standards. However, it specifically covers executory contracts only when they become onerous in nature.
inclusion: Onerous executory contracts
Onerous leases before commencement date
exclusion: Standard financial instruments within Ind AS 109 scope
Revenue contracts under Ind AS 115 except onerous ones
nearby_distinctions: Executory contracts are generally outside the standard unless they result in an onerous obligation.

descriptors.definition: Executory contracts are those where neither party has performed any obligations or both have partially performed to an equal extent. Ind AS 37 applies to such contracts exclusively when they become onerous.
inclusion: Contracts with unperformed mutual obligations
Contracts where both parties performed equally
exclusion: Contracts where performance is disproportionate creating enforceable liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from completed or partially completed contracts with unilateral performance imbalances requiring immediate liability recognition.

descriptors.definition: Certain provisions relate to revenue recognition, such as fee-based guarantees, which are handled under separate standards. Asset valuation adjustments like depreciation and doubtful debts are excluded from the scope of Ind AS 37.
inclusion: Provisions for restructurings and discontinued operations
exclusion: Depreciation
Impairment of assets
Doubtful debts
nearby_distinctions: Valuation adjustments to asset carrying amounts differ from provisions for liabilities of uncertain timing or amount.

descriptors.definition: A provision is a liability of uncertain timing or amount arising from a present obligation due to past events. Legal obligations stem from contracts, legislation, or operation of law, whereas constructive obligations arise from an entity's established practices and created expectations.
inclusion: Obligations from explicit or implicit contract terms
Obligations from past practice and published policies
exclusion: Future commitments unconnected to past obligating events
nearby_distinctions: Legal obligations derive strictly from binding laws or terms, whereas constructive obligations derive from created valid expectations via past actions.

descriptors.definition: Provisions differ from trade payables and accruals due to a significantly higher degree of uncertainty regarding timing or amount. Trade payables and accruals represent invoiced or agreed liabilities for received goods and services with minimal estimation variance.
inclusion: Warranty obligations
Liabilities with uncertain settlement timing or amount
exclusion: Utility accruals with known timing
Uninvoiced goods under agreed trade terms
Financial guarantees under Ind AS 109
nearby_distinctions: Accruals involve minor estimation variance for known invoiced or received services, whereas provisions involve substantial uncertainty over timing and amount.

descriptors.definition: Provisions are recognized liabilities because an outflow is probable and measurable, whereas contingent liabilities remain unrecgonized due to being possible obligations or failing probability and measurement criteria.
inclusion: Recognized provisions where outflow is probable
Contingent liabilities for possible obligations
exclusion: Remote possibilities requiring no disclosure
nearby_distinctions: Provisions meet the probability and reliability criteria for immediate recognition, while contingent liabilities fail either probability or measurement thresholds.

descriptors.definition: An entity must recognize a provision only when it has a present legal or constructive obligation from a past event, a resource outflow is probable, and a reliable estimate of the amount is possible. When a present obligation existence is unclear, available evidence and post-reporting events are evaluated to determine probability.
inclusion: Obligations meeting all three recognition tests
Obligations backed by expert evidence or post-period events
exclusion: Future operating losses
Contingencies failing recognition criteria
nearby_distinctions: Unlike contingent liabilities, recognized provisions must satisfy all three strict criteria of past event, probable outflow, and reliable estimation simultaneously.

descriptors.definition: Provisions require the cumulative satisfaction of a present obligation from a past event, a probable resource outflow, and a reliable estimate. In ambiguous cases, entities must review post-reporting events and expert opinions to establish if a present obligation exists.
inclusion: Liabilities meeting criteria based on post-reporting evidence
exclusion: Obligations without confirmed past events
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general business risks by requiring a distinct past event creating an enforceable present obligation.

descriptors.definition: Contingent liabilities are never recognized in financial statements but must be disclosed unless the possibility of a resource outflow is remote. Items are continuously reassessed so that if an outflow becomes probable, a provision is recognized in the period of change.
inclusion: Disclosed contingent liabilities for non-remote possibilities
Portions of joint obligations expected to be met by other parties
exclusion: Remote obligations requiring no disclosure
Probable obligations recognized as provisions
nearby_distinctions: Contingent liabilities require disclosure rather than recognition unless the likelihood of resource outflow shifts from possible to probable.

descriptors.definition: Contingent assets are excluded from recognition in financial statements to prevent recognizing unrealized income, requiring disclosure only when an economic benefit inflow is probable. However, once an inflow becomes virtually certain, the asset and related income are recognized.
inclusion: Assets with virtually certain economic benefit inflows
Disclosed contingent assets with probable inflows
exclusion: Unrealized contingent assets with remote or merely possible inflows
nearby_distinctions: Contingent assets are strictly disclosed until realization becomes virtually certain, unlike provisions which require recognition upon a lower probable threshold.

descriptors.definition: Provisions are measured at the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the end of the reporting period, reflecting what an entity would rationally pay. Statistical expected values are used for large populations, while mid-points are applied to continuous outcome ranges.
inclusion: Probability-weighted expected values for large populations
Mid-point estimations for continuous ranges
exclusion: Arbitrary estimations unsupported by management judgment or expert reports
nearby_distinctions: Differs from fixed invoice valuations by incorporating probability-weighted outcomes and management judgment for uncertain liabilities.

descriptors.definition: The provision amount recognized must be the best estimate of the expenditure needed to settle the present obligation at the end of the reporting period. Management determines this by using professional judgment, historical transaction experience, and expected value probability weightings for large populations of items.
inclusion: Expenditure required to settle present obligations
Probability-weighted outcomes for large populations
Mid-points of continuous outcome ranges
exclusion: Contingent assets
Arbitrary provisions without historical or expert support
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from generic guesswork by requiring statistical expected value models or objective management judgment.

descriptors.definition: Risks and uncertainties surrounding events and circumstances must be factored into the best estimate of a provision. Entities can adjust for outcome variability by adding risk allowances to expected present value outflows, modifying future cash flow estimates, or altering the discount rate.
inclusion: Risk adjustments for liability uncertainty
Modifications to discount rates for specific liability risks
Disclosures concerning underlying expenditure uncertainties
exclusion: Deliberate overstatement of liabilities
Duplicate adjustments for the same risk and uncertainty
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard expected value estimation by explicitly accounting for the variability premium that entities would pay beyond base expected flows.
source_ambiguities

descriptors.definition: When the effect of the time value of money is material, provisions must be discounted to the present value of expected settlement expenditures. The applied discount rate must be a pre-tax rate reflecting current market assessments of the time value of money and specific liability risks without duplicating cash flow adjustments.
inclusion: Discounting cash flows where materiality thresholds are met
Pre-tax discount rates matching current market assessments
exclusion: Discounting provisions where the time value impact is immaterial
Reflecting risks in discount rates already adjusted in future cash flows
nearby_distinctions: Differs from undiscounted best estimates by explicitly incorporating financial discounting to account for timing differences in cash outflows.

descriptors.definition: Expected future events that impact the settlement amount should be incorporated into provisions when supported by sufficient objective evidence. Anticipation of existing technology refinements or new legislation is permitted only if objective documentation confirms enactment or reliable technical evolution is virtually certain.
inclusion: Refinements or adaptations of existing technologies backed by evidence
New legislation impacts when enactment is virtually certain
exclusion: Speculative creation of completely new, unproven technologies
Pending legislation without sufficient objective implementation evidence
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from pure speculation by requiring documented objective evidence or virtual certainty of enactment.

descriptors.definition: Gains expected from the disposal of assets must be excluded from the measurement of a provision, even when closely linked to the triggering event. Such asset sale gains must be recognized separately under the specific accounting standard governing the asset category.
inclusion: Full recognition of committed restructuring or closure liabilities
Separate asset derecognition accounting
exclusion: Netting expected asset sale gains against provision liabilities
Premature recognition of asset gains before standard criteria are met
nearby_distinctions: Separates liability measurement from asset derecognition principles, preventing premature offsets against provisions.

descriptors.definition: Expected settlement reimbursements from third parties must be recognized as a separate asset only when receipt is virtually certain upon the entity settling the obligation. The recognized reimbursement amount cannot exceed the total associated provision, though related expenses may be presented net in profit or loss.
inclusion: Separate asset for expected third-party reimbursements
Net presentation of provision expense in profit or loss
exclusion: Reimbursement assets exceeding the corresponding provision liability
Recording reimbursements when receipt is merely probable
nearby_distinctions: Differs from contingent assets by being tied directly to an established provision where recovery is virtually certain.

descriptors.definition: Provisions must be reviewed at each reporting period and adjusted to reflect current best estimates, with balances reversed if an outflow is no longer probable. When obligation amounts crystallize without uncertainty or discounting passes time, balances are reclassified to liabilities or recognized as finance costs.
inclusion: Periodic reviews of provisions at reporting dates
Reversal of provisions when outflows cease to be probable
Accretion of discount recognized as borrowing or finance cost
exclusion: Maintaining provisions after underlying settlement amounts are completely finalized
Omitting periodic updates to estimates
nearby_distinctions: Transitions provisions into standard liabilities once amounts and uncertainties are fully resolved and finalized.

descriptors.definition: Provisions must be utilized exclusively for the specific expenditures for which they were originally recognized, strictly prohibiting repurposing. Setting unrelated expenses against an established provision distorts reporting by concealing the true impact of distinct operational events.
inclusion: Application of provisions only to their designated original liabilities
Direct matching of related expenditures
exclusion: Repurposing existing provisions for unrelated operational expenditures
Absorbing losses from separate events into pre-existing balances
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general reserves by enforcing strict targeting to the exact liability incurred.

descriptors.definition: Provisions are governed by strict criteria preventing their recognition for future operating losses or non-onerous executory contracts. Expected operating losses instead signal potential asset impairments requiring evaluation under relevant asset impairment standards.
inclusion: Assessment of asset impairment during anticipated operational downturns
Exclusion of un-arisen operational losses
exclusion: Recognition of provisions for future operating losses
Liability creation without a preceding past obligating event
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates general future business losses from valid present obligations arising from past events.

descriptors.definition: Entities are strictly prohibited from recognizing provisions for future operating losses because they do not represent present obligations stemming from past events. Anticipated losses of this nature instead indicate that related operational assets may require impairment testing.
inclusion: Impairment testing of assets under dedicated standards
Identification of operational loss indicators
exclusion: Provision creation for anticipated future operating losses
Including projected segment losses inside restructuring provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from restructuring provisions by failing the past obligating event requirement.

descriptors.definition: Contracts where unavoidable meeting costs exceed expected economic benefits are classified as onerous, requiring present obligations to be recognized as provisions. Unavoidable costs represent the least net cost of exiting the contract, determined by comparing fulfillment costs against failure penalties.
inclusion: Provision recognition for contracts where fulfillment costs exceed benefits
Inclusion of incremental and directly attributable contract fulfillment costs
Prior asset impairment testing under Ind AS 36
exclusion: Non-onerous executory contracts
Contracts cancelable without financial penalty
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from routine executory contracts by the presence of net economic loss where unavoidable obligations exceed incoming benefits.

descriptors.definition: Restructuring provisions require a constructive obligation established by a detailed formal plan and a valid expectation raised among affected parties through implementation start or announcement. Qualifying restructuring events include business line sales, facility closures, management changes, and fundamental operational reorganizations.
inclusion: Provisions for sales or terminations of business lines
Closure or relocation of business locations with communicated plans
exclusion: Internal management decisions not communicated or acted upon before reporting dates
Future operating losses linked to restructuring groups
nearby_distinctions: Differs from internal management intentions by requiring outward communication or implementation to establish a constructive obligation.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose movements in carrying amounts, descriptions of expected outflows, uncertainties, and expected reimbursements for each class of provisions. For contingent liabilities, entities must disclose a brief description of the nature and financial effect unless an outflow is remote.
inclusion: Reconciliation of beginning and ending carrying amounts of provisions
Nature and timing details of provision obligations
Descriptions and financial estimates for non-remote contingent liabilities
exclusion: Comparative information for provisions
Remote contingent liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between mandatory comparative disclosures normally required elsewhere and provisions disclosures where comparatives are omitted.

descriptors.definition: Appendix C establishes principles for recognizing liabilities to pay government-imposed levies whose timing and amount are certain under Ind AS 37 scope. It excludes other specific outflows like fines, penalties, and contractual payments.
inclusion: Accounting for levy liabilities within standard scope
Identified obligating events triggering levy payments
exclusion: Costs arising from recognizing a levy liability
Fines or penalties for legal breaches
Contractual payments for asset acquisition or services
Emissions trading scheme liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes government levies from contractual payments, penalties for legal breaches, and emissions trading scheme liabilities.

descriptors.definition: Appendix C specifies accounting treatment for levy liabilities falling under Ind AS 37 when their timing and amount are certain. It explicitly omits the subsequent cost accounting arising from recognizing such levy liabilities.
inclusion: Liabilities to pay government levies with certain timing and amounts
exclusion: Subsequent cost accounting arising from levy recognition
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes direct levy liability accounting from the accounting treatment applied to resulting asset or expense costs.

descriptors.definition: The guidance excludes non-levy outflows like legislative fines, emissions trading scheme liabilities, and asset acquisition payments. Furthermore, future operational compulsion or going concern assumptions do not create present obligations for future levies.
inclusion: Outflows covered by other standards
Contractual asset or service payments
exclusion: Levies whose timing and amount are uncertain
Future operating obligations driven solely by going concern assumptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes statutory levies from penalties, contractual considerations, and broad operational activities.

descriptors.definition: A levy represents a governmental charge imposed on entities via laws or regulations that results in economic resource outflows. Government entities comprise local, national, or international agencies.
inclusion: Statutory charges imposed by national or local governments
exclusion: Contractual fees for services rendered
Fines for legal violations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes compulsory legislative levies from bilateral contracts and regulatory penalties.

descriptors.definition: A levy liability is triggered and recognized when the specified activity occurs, and if conditions span a period or reach a threshold, recognition aligns accordingly. Interim reporting periods apply these exact annual recognition principles without creating advance liabilities for future operations.
inclusion: Progressive recognition when activities occur over time
Recognition upon reaching specific minimum thresholds
Prepaid levy asset recognition
exclusion: Levy recognition absent a present obligation at interim period ends
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between past prerequisite activities and current period events that trigger present obligations.

descriptors.definition: This section provides practical illustrations using financial statement excerpts from listed entities applying Ind AS 37. It contextualizes theoretical standard requirements with actual corporate reporting examples.
inclusion: Corporate annual report disclosures
exclusion: Hypothetical scenarios without corporate backing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes empirical disclosure examples from standalone theoretical rules.
source_ambiguities: The source text provides a heading with no accompanying substantive rules or text snippets.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 37 differs from AS 29 through explicit constructive obligation definitions, mandatory discounting for material time-value impacts, probable contingent asset disclosures, and dedicated onerous contract asset impairment rules. Additionally, Ind AS 37 offers comprehensive guidance on specific funds, waste electrical equipment, and government levies.
inclusion: Discounting comparison for general provisions
Contingent asset disclosure contrasts
Onerous contract impairment precedence
exclusion: Prohibitions on discounting under AS 29 for standard provisions
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts Ind AS frameworks with legacy AS 29 guidelines regarding discounting, contingent assets, and future operating losses.

descriptors.definition: The standard prescribes accounting treatment for income taxes, addressing timing differences between book profits and taxable profits caused by accelerated tax deductions. It ensures financial statements properly reflect future tax liabilities arising from these temporary divergences over asset useful lives.
inclusion: Accounting for tax consequences of current period events
Future tax consequences from recovery or settlement of carrying amounts
exclusion: Methods of accounting for government grants
Methods of accounting for investment tax credits
nearby_distinctions: Differs from pure cash-flow tax accounting by recognizing prospective tax liabilities and assets.

descriptors.definition: The standard governs domestic and foreign taxes based on taxable profits, including withholding taxes on distributions. The core principle requires recognizing a deferred tax liability or asset when the recovery or settlement of an asset or liability's carrying amount makes future tax payments larger or smaller.
inclusion: Domestic income taxes
Foreign income taxes
Withholding taxes payable on profit distributions by subsidiaries, associates, or joint ventures
exclusion: General accounting treatments for government grants unconnected to tax base differences
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between current operational tax consequences and future recovery-driven tax consequences.

descriptors.definition: Defines key financial elements including accounting profit, taxable profit, tax expense, temporary differences, and tax bases. Unlike older standards employing a profit and loss timing-difference approach, this standard utilizes a balance sheet approach comparing asset and liability carrying amounts to their tax bases.
inclusion: Definitions for current and deferred tax components
Classification of temporary differences into taxable and deductible types
exclusion: Detailed recognition rules outside standard definitions
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts Ind AS 12 balance-sheet temporary differences with AS 22 profit-and-loss timing differences.

descriptors.definition: Tax expense or tax income represents the aggregate amount included in determining the profit or loss for a period. It combines both current tax and deferred tax components and can result in either a positive expense or negative tax income.
inclusion: Aggregation of current tax amounts
Aggregation of deferred tax amounts within profit or loss
exclusion: Taxes recognized directly in equity or other comprehensive income
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from cash tax paid by incorporating non-cash deferred tax adjustments.

descriptors.definition: Current tax liabilities and assets for current and prior periods are measured at the amount expected to be paid to or recovered from taxation authorities. Computations rely on enacted or substantively enacted tax rates and laws, treating any revisions resulting from uncertain tax positions as changes in estimates.
inclusion: Unpaid current tax recognized as a liability
Excess advance tax or TDS recognized as an asset
Use of statistical tools for uncertain tax interpretations
exclusion: Deferred tax asset calculations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes current period tax obligations settled via cash from future timing-based tax allocations.

descriptors.definition: Current tax is defined as the specific amount of income taxes payable or recoverable relating to the taxable profit or loss generated during a specific reporting period. It forms the primary baseline for calculating short-term fiscal obligations owed to tax authorities.
inclusion: Income taxes payable on current period taxable profits
exclusion: Long-term deferred tax impacts
nearby_distinctions: Represents immediate period obligations rather than cumulative temporary difference reversals.

descriptors.definition: Unpaid current tax for current and prior periods is recognized as a liability, while prepaid amounts exceeding actual dues are recognized as assets. The definitive liability crystallizes upon finalizing financial statements at the end of the reporting period.
inclusion: Recognition of tax liabilities net of advance tax and TDS
Recognition of tax refund assets
exclusion: Recognition rules for permanent differences
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on balance sheet recognition criteria for short-term tax balances.

descriptors.definition: Current tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted or substantively enacted tax rates and laws expected to apply upon settlement. Uncertain tax positions require estimation based on expected outcomes, with subsequent changes treated as changes in accounting estimates.
inclusion: Measurement using rates enacted by the balance sheet date
Statistical evaluations for uncertain tax interpretations
exclusion: Discounting of current tax assets and liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts enacted tax rates with tentative legislative proposals lacking formal enactment.

descriptors.definition: The accounting treatment for current tax effects must directly mirror the underlying transaction or event generating it. If an underlying item is recognized within the statement of profit or loss, its corresponding current tax effect must also be recognized there.
inclusion: Matching tax effects to the financial statement component housing the original transaction
exclusion: Independent tax treatments disconnected from source transactions
nearby_distinctions: Ensures consistency between primary transaction classification and subsequent tax allocation.

descriptors.definition: Entities can offset current tax assets and liabilities only if they possess a legally enforceable right to set off recognized amounts and intend either to settle net or simultaneously. Consolidated group entities must similarly demonstrate a legally enforceable right to make single net payments across member entities.
inclusion: Offsetting taxes levied by the same authority with single net payment permission
Intra-group tax offsetting under strict legal enforceability
exclusion: Offsetting taxes across completely separate taxation authorities without legal clearance
nearby_distinctions: Applies strict criteria analogous to financial instrument offsetting under Ind AS 32.

descriptors.definition: Deferred tax accounting follows a structured multi-step process involving the computation of carrying amounts, tax bases, and temporary differences. It requires classifying differences, evaluating exceptions and tax credits, determining tax rates, and correctly recognizing and offsetting resultant deferred balances.
inclusion: Step-by-step framework for calculating deferred tax items
Offsetting deferred tax assets and liabilities
exclusion: Standalone current tax computations
nearby_distinctions: Provides an exhaustive procedural workflow distinct from simple current tax liability assessments.

descriptors.definition: The carrying amount represents the balance sheet value at which an asset or liability is recognized after accounting for subsequent adjustments such as depreciation and impairment. It reflects the ledger balance determined under applicable accounting standards rather than tax rules.
inclusion: Balance sheet values adjusted for accounting depreciation
Balance sheet values adjusted for asset impairment
exclusion: Values computed purely under income tax depreciation schedules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes book values from tax base values utilized in temporary difference calculations.

descriptors.definition: The tax base of an asset or liability is the specific amount attributed to it for income tax purposes. It represents the deductible amount against taxable economic benefits that will flow to the entity upon recovering the carrying amount.
inclusion: Amount deductible against future taxable economic benefits
Cost less cumulative tax depreciation
exclusion: Accounting revaluations ignored for tax purposes
nearby_distinctions: Carrying amount reflects financial reporting value, whereas tax base is strictly determined by taxation laws.

descriptors.definition: Temporary differences are calculated as the difference between the carrying amount of an asset or liability in the balance sheet and its corresponding tax base. These differences ultimately reverse over time, resulting in a cumulative impact of zero.
inclusion: Differences between balance sheet carrying amount and tax base
Timing differences
exclusion: Permanent differences that never reverse
nearby_distinctions: Temporary differences encompass timing differences but are broader because they also capture balance sheet carrying value adjustments like revaluations.

descriptors.definition: Temporary differences are categorized into taxable temporary differences, which increase future tax liabilities, and deductible temporary differences, which reduce them. This classification dictates whether a deferred tax liability or asset should be recognized.
inclusion: Taxable temporary differences arising when asset carrying amount exceeds tax base
Deductible temporary differences arising when liability carrying amount exceeds tax base
exclusion: Permanent differences
nearby_distinctions: Taxable temporary differences result in future taxable amounts, whereas deductible temporary differences generate future tax deductions.

descriptors.definition: Specific exceptions apply to the general recognition rules for deferred taxes, such as the initial recognition of goodwill in a business combination. In jurisdictions where goodwill is not tax-deductible, its tax base is nil and no deferred tax liability is recognized to avoid circular computations.
inclusion: Goodwill arising from business combinations where tax base is nil and not deductible
exclusion: Standard asset and liability temporary differences subject to routine deferred tax accounting
nearby_distinctions: Goodwill exceptions prevent the circular inflation of carrying values that would occur if deferred tax liabilities were recognized on residual goodwill.

descriptors.definition: Deductible temporary differences and unused tax losses only provide economic benefits if the entity expects future taxable profits against which they can be utilized. Entities must assess and reassess the probability of sufficient future taxable profits to recognize deferred tax assets.
inclusion: Unused trading losses available for carry forward within legal limits
Assessment of future taxable profits
exclusion: Tax losses exceeding statutory carry-forward time limits
nearby_distinctions: Unlike taxable temporary differences that automatically create liabilities, deductible temporary differences and tax losses require positive profit evidence for asset recognition.

descriptors.definition: Deferred tax assets and liabilities must be measured using the tax rates and laws that have been enacted or substantively enacted by the end of the reporting period. These rates must reflect the expected manner of recovery or settlement of the asset or liability's carrying amount.
inclusion: Tax rates expected to apply during realization or settlement
Rates reflecting expected manner of asset recovery or liability settlement
exclusion: Tax rates enacted after the reporting period end
nearby_distinctions: Tax rates applied depend on whether an asset is recovered through use or sale if different statutory rates apply to each mode.

descriptors.definition: Deferred tax balances are computed by multiplying taxable or deductible temporary differences by the applicable enacted tax rates. Recognized deferred tax assets must be reviewed at each reporting date and reduced if sufficient future taxable profits are no longer probable.
inclusion: Multiplication of temporary differences by applicable tax rates
Periodic review and adjustment of deferred tax asset carrying amounts
exclusion: Discounting of deferred tax assets and liabilities to present value
nearby_distinctions: Calculation yields gross temporary impacts that are strictly prohibited from being discounted under standard rules.

descriptors.definition: The accounting treatment for deferred tax effects must align with the underlying transaction or event, being recognized in profit or loss, other comprehensive income, or directly in equity. Subsequent changes in deferred tax balances driven by tax rate changes are also routed through profit or loss unless tied to prior non-P&L items.
inclusion: Tax effects recognized in profit or loss, OCI, or equity
Pro rata allocation for complex items recognized outside profit or loss
exclusion: Disconnecting tax accounting from the classification of the underlying economic event
nearby_distinctions: Items originating in equity or OCI mandate that their corresponding deferred tax adjustments bypass the statement of profit and loss.

descriptors.definition: Entities can offset deferred tax assets against deferred tax liabilities only if they possess a legally enforceable right to set off current tax assets against current tax liabilities. Furthermore, both deferred balances must relate to income taxes levied by the same taxation authority on the same taxable entity or qualifying distinct entities.
inclusion: Net presentation when legally enforceable set-off rights exist
Taxes levied by the same authority on the same or intentionally simultaneous settling entities
exclusion: Offsetting across different unrelated taxation authorities without legal rights
nearby_distinctions: Offsetting is restricted solely to instances with legal enforceability and matching tax jurisdictions, avoiding arbitrary aggregation.

descriptors.definition: Practical application of income tax standards involves recognizing deferred tax assets and liabilities arising from fair value adjustments in business combinations. These recognized tax balances directly affect the determination of goodwill or bargain purchase gains on the acquisition date.
inclusion: Deferred tax impacts from asset and liability fair value uplifts in acquisitions
Adjustments to goodwill calculations
exclusion: Deferred tax liabilities on initial goodwill recognition exceptions
nearby_distinctions: Acquisition-date fair value adjustments create temporary differences that directly alter consolidated goodwill, distinguishing them from routine standalone asset shifts.

descriptors.definition: Temporary differences arising from fair value adjustments of identifiable assets and liabilities in a business combination require the recognition of resulting deferred tax assets or liabilities. These tax balances impact the quantum of goodwill or bargain purchase gain recognized at acquisition.
inclusion: Deferred tax on fair value adjustments of property, plant, equipment, and inventory
Impact on goodwill or bargain purchase
exclusion: Deferred tax liabilities on initial recognition of un-deductible goodwill
nearby_distinctions: Unlike routine internal asset revaluations, business combination fair valuation adjustments instantly integrate tax effects into acquisition accounting and goodwill.

descriptors.definition: Share-based payment remuneration expenses recognized under accounting standards often generate tax deductions in later periods or based on future share prices. The difference between the future tax deduction tax base and the nil carrying amount creates a deductible temporary difference and associated deferred tax asset.
inclusion: Tax deductions linked to employee share options
Deferred tax assets derived from estimated future share-price-based deductions
exclusion: Deductions exceeding cumulative remuneration expense which must be routed to equity
nearby_distinctions: Excess tax deductions over cumulative accounting remuneration expenses are segregated and recognized directly in equity rather than profit or loss.

descriptors.definition: A modification in the taxation classification of an organization or its investors alters future tax rates and asset recovery consequences. Such adjustments impact profit or loss unless the underlying events directly affect equity or other comprehensive income.
inclusion: Tax consequences affecting profit or loss
Tax effects relating to items recognized in equity
Tax effects relating to items recognized in other comprehensive income
exclusion: Increases or decreases in amounts recognized outside profit or loss unrelated to equity or OCI
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from routine temporary difference reversals by stemming from structural status alterations rather than operational asset recovery.

descriptors.definition: Financial statement reporting mandates extend beyond recognition and measurement to encompass detailed disclosures regarding income taxes. These disclosures explain tax expenses, equity charges, and other tax-related line items.
inclusion: Major components of tax expense
Taxes related to items charged directly to equity
exclusion: Initial recognition and measurement rules detailed in earlier sections
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from core recognition principles by focusing strictly on note disclosures and explanatory breakdowns.
