descriptors.definition: Entities must separately disclose major components of tax expense or income within the financial statements. This includes current tax, prior period adjustments, and deferred tax movements.
inclusion: Current tax expense
Deferred tax expense relating to origination and reversal of temporary differences
Tax expense relating to accounting policy changes and errors
exclusion: Unrelated operating expense disclosures
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from aggregate balance sheet totals by itemizing specific profit or loss tax drivers.

descriptors.definition: Current and deferred taxes associated with items credited or charged directly to equity must be accounted for and disclosed accordingly. Examples include retrospective accounting policy adjustments and the initial equity component of compound instruments.
inclusion: Aggregate current and deferred tax related to equity items
Retained earnings opening balance adjustments from error corrections
exclusion: Taxes recognized through profit or loss or other comprehensive income
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from OCI tax disclosures by isolating items bypassing profit or loss straight into equity components.

descriptors.definition: Income taxes relating to items recognized in other comprehensive income must be accounted for and disclosed for each component. Examples include asset revaluations and foreign operation translation differences.
terminology: revaluation of property plant and equipment
inclusion: Tax relating to property, plant and equipment revaluations
Tax relating to foreign operation exchange differences
exclusion: Tax expenses affecting standard profit or loss from ordinary activities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from direct equity charges by applying specifically to elements traversing the statement of other comprehensive income.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide a numerical reconciliation explaining the variance between accounting profit multiplied by applicable rates and actual tax expense. This explanation can use either monetary tax amounts or effective tax rate percentages.
inclusion: Numerical reconciliation of tax expense against accounting profit product
Numerical reconciliation of average effective tax rate against applicable tax rate
exclusion: Standard balance sheet tax asset and liability schedules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from component breakdowns by offering a conceptual bridge between pre-tax accounting profits and final tax expense calculations.

descriptors.definition: Explanations must be provided whenever applicable tax rates shift compared to the prior period. These shifts can stem from legislative revisions, structural entity changes, or asset recovery alterations.
inclusion: Explanations for tax rate variations across accounting periods
exclusion: Static tax rate disclosures under constant legislative frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general tax expense breakdowns by explicitly targeting the rationale behind shifting statutory percentages.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose the monetary amounts and expiry dates of deductible temporary differences, unused tax losses, and tax credits lacking deferred tax asset recognition. This reporting applies when standard recognition criteria cannot be fulfilled.
inclusion: Amounts of unrecognised deductible temporary differences
Expiry dates of unrecognised tax losses and tax credits
exclusion: Deferred tax assets successfully recognized on the balance sheet
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from recognized asset disclosures by focusing exclusively on potential tax benefits excluded from the balance sheet due to strict criteria.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose the aggregate temporary differences linked to investments in subsidiaries, branches, associates, and joint ventures where deferred tax liabilities remain unrecognised. Disclosing the underlying differences satisfies requirements when computing precise unrecognised liabilities is impracticable.
inclusion: Aggregate temporary differences for unrecognised subsidiary and affiliate liabilities
exclusion: Direct computation of unrecognised deferred tax liabilities when impracticable
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard temporary difference disclosures by addressing complex group-structure investments where computation is burdensome.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose recognized deferred tax balances across balance sheet periods alongside associated profit or loss impacts. These figures must be categorized by each distinct type of temporary difference, tax loss, and tax credit.
inclusion: Amounts of deferred tax assets and liabilities recognized in the balance sheet
Deferred tax income or expense recognized in profit or loss
exclusion: Unrecognised tax positions and off-balance-sheet items
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from aggregate tax expense lines by offering granular balance sheet tracking for individual temporary difference categories.

descriptors.definition: Tax expenses connected to discontinued operations must be separately disclosed for both discontinuance gains or losses and ordinary operational profits. These disclosures must also incorporate comparative prior period amounts.
inclusion: Tax expense relating to gain or loss on discontinuance
Tax expense relating to profit or loss from ordinary activities of discontinued operations
exclusion: Taxes associated with continuing operations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from core continuing operation tax disclosures by segregating discontinued business lines and their unique exit metrics.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose the income tax consequences of dividends proposed or declared after the reporting date but prior to financial statement approval. Such dividend tax impacts are omitted from balance sheet liabilities but require explicit disclosure.
inclusion: Income tax consequences of dividends proposed after reporting date but before approval
exclusion: Recognized dividend liability tax provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from recognized liabilities by targeting post-reporting date unrecognised corporate distributions.

descriptors.definition: Acquirers must disclose changes in pre-acquisition deferred tax asset amounts resulting from business combinations. Additionally, entities need to describe events or circumstances that lead to the post-acquisition recognition of deferred tax benefits previously unrecognised at the acquisition date.
inclusion: Changes in pre-acquisition deferred tax assets due to business combinations
Post-acquisition recognition of previously unrecognised deferred tax benefits
exclusion: General tax expense disclosures
Routine temporary difference disclosures
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general deferred tax asset recognition disclosures by focusing specifically on changes originating from business combination transactions.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose the specific deferred tax asset amounts and the supporting evidence for their recognition under certain conditions. This applies when utilisation depends on future taxable profits exceeding reversing taxable temporary differences and the entity experienced recent losses.
inclusion: Disclosure of deferred tax asset amounts dependent on future profits
Nature of evidence supporting recognition following current or preceding period losses
exclusion: Deferred tax assets fully supported by existing taxable temporary differences
General tax rate reconciliation items
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from standard tax disclosures because it specifically mandates evidence disclosure when loss history or future profit dependency exists.

descriptors.definition: When tax rates depend on dividend distribution, entities must disclose potential income tax consequences and system features affecting them. If calculating the total amount is impracticable, entities must disclose practicably determinable amounts or refundable taxes along with uncomputable limitations.
inclusion: Nature of potential income tax consequences from paying dividends
Practicable amounts of refundable taxes or unrecognised deferred tax liabilities
exclusion: Taxes paid on regular operating income without dividend rate differentials
Standard corporate tax expense recognition
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on dividend-dependent tax rates rather than general temporary differences or standard operational tax expenses.

descriptors.definition: Entities are required to disclose tax-related contingent liabilities and assets in accordance with relevant provisions standards. Such contingencies typically originate from unresolved disputes with taxation authorities.
inclusion: Tax-related contingent liabilities
Tax-related contingent assets from unresolved disputes
exclusion: Recognized current or deferred tax liabilities
Certain future tax planning strategies
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from recognized deferred or current taxes by representing uncertain potential obligations or rights rather than measured temporary differences.

descriptors.definition: When tax rate or law modifications are enacted or announced after the reporting period, entities must disclose any significant effects on assets and liabilities. Such disclosures follow events after the reporting period principles.
inclusion: Significant effects of tax rate or law changes enacted after reporting date
Disclosures regarding announced post-period tax modifications
exclusion: Adjustments directly incorporated into financial statement balances if enacted before the reporting date
Internal tax calculations unaffected by legislative changes
nearby_distinctions: Applies specifically to post-period legislative changes rather than tax rates already substantively enacted by the balance sheet date.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 12 adopts a balance sheet approach focusing on temporary differences between asset and liability carrying amounts and tax bases, unlike the income statement approach of AS 22. Furthermore, Ind AS 12 recognizes deferred tax assets for deductible differences and losses based on probable future profits, whereas AS 22 requires virtual certainty or reasonable certainty thresholds.
inclusion: Comparison of timing versus temporary differences
Contrasting recognition criteria for deferred tax assets under loss conditions
exclusion: Detailed computation worksheets for current tax liabilities
Specific tax audit procedures
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts the modern asset-liability framework with older income statement matching methodologies and stringent realization criteria.

descriptors.definition: The standard prescribes accounting for foreign currency transactions and foreign operations, including translating financial statements into a presentation currency. It establishes key definitions such as functional currency, presentation currency, spot rate, and closing rate to govern currency translations.
inclusion: Accounting for foreign currency transactions and balances
Translation of foreign operations into a reporting entity's financial statements
Translation of financial statements into a presentation currency
exclusion: Hedge accounting for foreign currency items covered under Ind AS 109
Presentation of cash flows in statement of cash flows covered under Ind AS 7
nearby_distinctions: Functional currency represents the primary economic environment currency, whereas presentation currency is merely the currency used for publishing financial statements.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies to accounting for foreign currency transactions, foreign operations consolidation, and translating financial statements into presentation currency. It explicitly excludes specific areas like hedge accounting, cash flow statements, and specific long-term monetary item exemptions.
inclusion: Foreign currency derivatives not covered by Ind AS 109
Translation of results and financial position of foreign operations
Translation into presentation currency
exclusion: Hedge accounting for foreign currency items and net investment hedging
Statement of cash flows presentation of foreign currency cash flows
Long term foreign currency monetary items utilizing Ind AS 101 exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard foreign currency translation rules from specialised treatments governed separately by Ind AS 109, Ind AS 7, and Ind AS 101.

descriptors.definition: Entities measure their financial items using a functional currency determined by primary indicators like sales pricing and cost influences. Secondary indicators such as financing activities and operational generation provide supporting evidence for establishing this currency.
inclusion: Primary economic environment evaluation
Sales price influencing currency assessment
Labour, material, and cost currency determination
exclusion: Presentation currency selection choices
Group level currency determinations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between the primary economic pricing currency and the secondary financing or remittance currencies used for supporting evidence.

descriptors.definition: Foreign currency transactions must be initially recorded at the transaction date exchange rate using the functional currency. Items are categorized into monetary assets and liabilities with fixed currency units versus non-monetary items lacking such fixed terms.
inclusion: Transactions buying or selling goods/services in foreign currency
Borrowing or lending funds in foreign currency
Classification of employee benefits, provisions, and lease liabilities as monetary items
exclusion: Subsequent revaluations at reporting dates
Non-monetary assets like goodwill, inventories, and property plant and equipment
nearby_distinctions: Monetary items involve a fixed or determinable number of currency units for receipts or payments, whereas non-monetary items do not.

descriptors.definition: Foreign currency transactions are initially recorded by translating the foreign amount into the functional currency at the spot exchange rate on the transaction date. Approximations like weekly or monthly average rates are acceptable unless exchange rates fluctuate significantly.
inclusion: Translation of goods and services transactions at transaction date rates
Translation of borrowings and lendings at transaction date rates
Use of approximation rates under stable exchange rate conditions
exclusion: Subsequent reporting period closing rate valuations
Average rates usage during significant exchange rate fluctuations
nearby_distinctions: Differs from subsequent measurement by utilizing the specific transaction date rate rather than the closing balance sheet date rate.

descriptors.definition: Monetary items consist of currency held and assets or liabilities to be received or paid in fixed units of currency, whereas non-monetary items lack this fixed feature. Subsequent reporting dates require monetary items to use closing rates, historical-cost non-monetary items to use transaction rates, and fair-value non-monetary items to use valuation date rates.
inclusion: Monetary translations using closing rates
Non-monetary historical cost translations using transaction date rates
Non-monetary fair value translations using valuation date rates
exclusion: Initial transaction date recording rules
Presentation currency group translation methods
nearby_distinctions: Monetary items are always updated to closing rates at reporting dates, whereas historical-cost non-monetary items remain fixed at past transaction rates.

descriptors.definition: At each reporting date, foreign currency items are translated using closing rates for monetary elements, historical rates for cost-based non-monetary elements, and specific valuation dates for fair-value non-monetary elements. For items determined by comparing multiple values like lower of cost and net realizable value, each component is translated using the exchange rate appropriate to the date of its specific determination.
inclusion: Translation of carrying amounts determined by comparing two or more amounts
Comparison of historical cost at transaction date rate against net realizable value at closing rate
Impairment loss recognition arising from currency valuation differences
exclusion: Initial transaction date recognition mechanics
Functional currency re-determinations
nearby_distinctions: Comparison-based items require dual-rate evaluations where historical elements use transaction date rates and net realizable values use closing rates.

descriptors.definition: Exchange differences arising from settlement or translation of monetary items are recognized in profit or loss, except when specific hedge accounting or net investment rules apply. For non-monetary items, any exchange component follows the primary gain or loss recognition path, whether in profit or loss or other comprehensive income.
inclusion: Exchange differences on monetary settlements recognized in profit or loss
Cash flow hedge exchange differences recognized in other comprehensive income
Exchange components of non-monetary asset revaluations processed through other comprehensive income
exclusion: Standard translation of foreign operations presented in separate equity reserves
Unsettled long-term monetary items with specific equity recognition elections
nearby_distinctions: Monetary exchange differences default to profit or loss unless bound by specific hedging or net investment exceptions, unlike non-monetary exchange items that shadow the underlying asset's destination.

descriptors.definition: An entity changes its functional currency only when underlying economic transactions, events, and conditions shift, applying the change prospectively from that date. All items are translated into the new functional currency using the exchange rate on the change date, treating resulting amounts as historical costs.
inclusion: Prospective translation of all items at the exchange rate on the change date
Deferred reclassification of foreign operation equity reserves until disposal
Retrospective restatement of comparative amounts for presentation currency changes
exclusion: Immediate transfer of accumulated foreign operation reserves to profit or loss upon functional currency change
Prospective application of presentation currency alterations
nearby_distinctions: A change in functional currency is applied prospectively from the change date, whereas a change in presentation currency is applied retrospectively as an accounting policy choice.

descriptors.definition: When an entity's presentation currency differs from its functional currency, assets and liabilities are translated at closing rates while income and expenses use transaction date rates. Resulting translation differences are recognized in other comprehensive income and accumulated in a separate equity component until disposal.
inclusion: Translating assets and liabilities of non-hyperinflationary entities at closing rates
Translating income and expenses at transaction or average rates
Allocating translation differences to non-controlling interests for non-wholly-owned subsidiaries
exclusion: Entities with functional currencies of hyperinflationary economies
Group-level functional currency concepts since groups only maintain presentation currencies
nearby_distinctions: Differs from functional currency measurement by converting financial statement line items specifically for external reporting presentation rather than internal record-keeping.

descriptors.definition: The financial position and results of entities whose functional currency is not hyperinflationary are translated into a presentation currency using closing rates for balance sheets and transaction rates for income statements. Resulting translation adjustments are accumulated in a separate equity reserve until the foreign operation is disposed of.
inclusion: Translation of balance sheet comparatives at historical closing rates
Recognition of exchange differences in other comprehensive income
Attribution of translation reserves to non-controlling interests
exclusion: Hyperinflationary economy translation procedures
Direct recognition of translation differences in profit or loss prior to disposal
nearby_distinctions: Applies specific closing rate rules to all balance sheet components distinct from transaction-date rates applied to operational flows.

descriptors.definition: Foreign operations are translated using closing rates for assets and liabilities and transaction rates for income and expenses, with differences routed to other comprehensive income. When reporting dates differ, adjustments are made for significant transactions and exchange rate changes up to the parent entity's reporting date in accordance with consolidation standards.
inclusion: Translation of foreign operation assets and liabilities at reporting date exchange rates
Inclusion of net investment loans and hedging gains in translation reserves
Adjustments for significant exchange rate variations under differing reporting periods
exclusion: Operations differing by more than three months without special interim statements
Immediate recognition of translation reserves in profit or loss
nearby_distinctions: Differs from single-entity presentation currency translation by incorporating specific net investment loan adjustments and distinct parent-subsidiary reporting date alignment rules.

descriptors.definition: When reporting dates differ between a foreign operation and the reporting entity, additional statements are ideally prepared. If not, Ind AS 110 permits a maximum three-month gap, adjusting for significant intervening transactions and exchange rate fluctuations.
inclusion: Translation of assets and liabilities using the foreign operation's period-end exchange rate
Adjustments for significant exchange rate movements up to the reporting entity's end date
exclusion: Using a reporting date difference exceeding three months without specific consolidation adjustments
nearby_distinctions: Unlike standard same-date reporting, differing dates require explicit timing and exchange rate adjustment mechanisms to align consolidated financial statements.

descriptors.definition: Intra-group balances and unrealized profits or losses are eliminated on consolidation, but related foreign exchange gains or losses are recognized in profit or loss due to real currency exposure. Such eliminations and measurements utilize historical spot rates from the transaction date.
inclusion: Recognition of exchange differences on intra-group transactions in profit or loss
Elimination of unrealized intra-group profits or losses until realized by external sale or write-off
exclusion: Elimination of foreign exchange gains or losses arising on actual foreign currency settlement exposure
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general intra-group balance eliminations, foreign exchange variances on these items survive consolidation and impact profit or loss unless tied to a net investment monetary item.

descriptors.definition: Subsidiary dividends declared to a parent are recorded at the exchange rate on the declaration date. Subsequent exchange rate movements between declaration and receipt create exchange differences that remain in consolidated profit or loss.
inclusion: Exchange differences arising on dividend payment timing differences recognized in profit or loss
Elimination of declared dividends and intra-group balances upon consolidation
exclusion: Recognition of dividend-related exchange differences in other comprehensive income
nearby_distinctions: Unlike pre-declaration net investment exposures, declared dividends shift exposure toward standard monetary receivables, routing subsequent currency variances through profit or loss instead of equity.

descriptors.definition: Goodwill and fair value adjustments to asset and liability carrying amounts from acquiring a foreign operation are treated as assets and liabilities of that foreign operation. Consequently, they are expressed in the foreign operation's functional currency and translated using the closing exchange rate.
inclusion: Translating acquired goodwill at the closing exchange rate
Translating fair value adjustments of a foreign acquisition at the closing rate
exclusion: Translating acquisition-related adjustments at historical transaction dates rather than closing rates
nearby_distinctions: Unlike domestic combinations, foreign business combinations require translation of fair value increments and resulting goodwill using closing exchange rates as integral components of the foreign operation.

descriptors.definition: Upon full disposal of a foreign operation, cumulative exchange differences recognized in other comprehensive income are reclassified from equity to profit or loss. Partial disposals require specific treatments depending on whether control of a subsidiary or retention of interest in associates or joint arrangements occurs.
inclusion: Reclassification of cumulative OCI exchange differences to profit or loss upon full disposal
Derecognition of NCI-attributed exchange differences without profit or loss reclassification on subsidiary disposal
exclusion: Reclassifying NCI-attributed cumulative exchange differences to profit or loss on subsidiary disposal
nearby_distinctions: Differs from minor carrying-amount write-downs, which do not trigger reclassification of accumulated equity exchange differences into profit or loss.

descriptors.definition: Full disposal of a foreign operation occurs via sale, liquidation, or repayment of share capital, prompting the reclassification of cumulative exchange differences from equity to profit or loss. For subsidiaries, exchange differences attributed to non-controlling interests are derecognized without profit or loss reclassification.
inclusion: Transfer of accumulated OCI foreign exchange reserves to profit or loss on complete exit
Accounting for loss of control as a full disposal event
exclusion: Reclassifying exchange differences assigned to non-controlling interests into profit or loss
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with partial disposals where only a proportionate share of accumulated translation reserves is reclassified or re-attributed.

descriptors.definition: A partial disposal reduces ownership interest without triggering a full disposal, requiring either proportionate re-attribution of cumulative exchange differences to non-controlling interests or reclassification to profit or loss. Asset write-downs or impairments do not constitute partial disposals and prompt no OCI reclassification.
inclusion: Re-attributing proportionate OCI exchange differences to non-controlling interests upon partial subsidiary disposal
Reclassifying a proportionate share of cumulative exchange differences to profit or loss for associates or joint arrangements
exclusion: Reclassifying exchange differences to profit or loss upon an internal asset write-down or impairment
nearby_distinctions: Unlike full disposals that completely clear foreign currency translation reserves, partial disposals involve split reclassifications or re-attributions based on retained influence levels.

descriptors.definition: Income taxes associated with foreign currency transaction gains and losses, as well as translation differences from foreign operations, are accounted for under specific income tax standards. This ensures proper tax allocation on currency-driven financial adjustments.
inclusion: Applying income tax accounting principles to foreign exchange gains and losses
Tax effect evaluation on translated entity results and financial positions
exclusion: Excluding exchange-related tax allocation from consolidated financial statement adjustments
nearby_distinctions: Differs from pure currency translation calculations by incorporating jurisdictional tax rules governing temporary differences created by exchange fluctuations.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose specific foreign exchange details, including amounts recognized in profit or loss, OCI reconciliations, presentation currency deviations, and functional currency changes. Supplementary currency information requires explicit identification and methodology descriptions.
inclusion: Reporting exchange differences in profit or loss and other comprehensive income
Disclosing reasons and dates for any functional currency modifications
exclusion: Presenting supplementary currency data without clear identification as non-compliant with standard presentation frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Unlike standard financial line-item notes, these disclosures specifically mandate qualitative and quantitative tracking of currency definitions, translation methods, and reserve reconciliations.

descriptors.definition: Listed entities apply core standard principles by recording foreign transactions at transaction-date rates and retranslating monetary items at balance sheet dates, with variances hitting profit or loss. Foreign operation translations are routed through other comprehensive income into a translation reserve.
inclusion: Retranslation of monetary assets and liabilities at balance sheet dates
Recognition of foreign operation translation differences in other comprehensive income
exclusion: Retranslation of non-monetary assets and liabilities measured at historical cost in foreign currencies
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts monetary item settlement treatment with non-monetary historical cost items that omit periodic balance sheet retranslation.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 21 mandates a functional currency approach and excludes forward contracts covered elsewhere, whereas previous standards utilized integral classifications and permitted capital asset exchange capitalization options. Presentation currency flexibilities also differ significantly between the frameworks.
inclusion: Excluding forward exchange contracts from Ind AS 21 scope in favor of financial instrument standards
Enforcing functional currency determinations over legacy integral/non-integral operation classifications
exclusion: Applying previous GAAP options to capitalize long-term monetary exchange differences on new post-transition asset acquisitions
nearby_distinctions: Unlike legacy rules offering capitalization alternatives for long-term foreign currency items, Ind AS 21 generally routes variances directly through profit or loss or equity without direct asset cost adjustments.

descriptors.definition: Transactions and relationships between related entities frequently impact an entity's profit, loss, and financial position due to controlled or influenced operating policies. Users require comprehensive disclosures of such relationships and transactions to properly assess enterprise risks and opportunities.
inclusion: Relationships with subsidiaries
Relationships with joint ventures
Relationships with associates
exclusion: Transactions exclusively with completely unrelated independent third parties under pure market competition
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general commercial trading by incorporating elements of operational influence and ownership control rather than standard arm's-length dealings.

descriptors.definition: The standard ensures financial statements highlight the potential effects of related party relationships, transactions, balances, and commitments on the reporting entity. These disclosures draw users' attention to distinct operational conditions that might not occur with unrelated parties.
inclusion: Disclosures of related party relationships
Disclosures of outstanding balances
Disclosures of financial commitments
exclusion: General disclosures unrelated to ownership control or managerial influence
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on drawing user attention to governance and ownership-influenced terms rather than general business performance metrics.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies to individual, consolidated, and separate financial statements for identifying relationships, transactions, balances, and commitments. Exemptions apply when disclosures conflict with statutory confidentiality duties or regulator prohibitions.
inclusion: Individual financial statements
Consolidated financial statements
Separate financial statements
exclusion: Intra-group balances eliminated upon consolidation, except for specific investment entity exemptions measured at fair value through profit or loss
nearby_distinctions: Applies across multiple financial statement tiers while excluding standard intra-group balances that undergo formal consolidation elimination.

descriptors.definition: A related party is a person or entity connected to the reporting entity, where evaluation must prioritize the substance of the relationship over mere legal form. Relationships involve either person-to-entity connections or entity-to-entity connections.
inclusion: Relationships between reporting entity and individuals
Relationships between reporting entity and other corporate entities
exclusion: Connections lacking substantive economic or operational control, joint control, or significant influence
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes underlying economic substance and control rather than strictly formal legal categorization.

descriptors.definition: An individual or their close family member is related to a reporting entity if they hold control, joint control, or significant influence over it. Such relationship also arises if the individual serves as key management personnel for the reporting entity or its parent.
inclusion: Individuals holding control or joint control
Individuals exercising significant influence
Key management personnel of the reporting entity or its parent
exclusion: Ordinary employees without management authority or significant ownership influence
nearby_distinctions: Restricts personal related-party status to individuals holding designated governance, management, or ownership powers.

descriptors.definition: An entity is related to a reporting entity if they are group members, associates, joint ventures, or controlled by the same person. Additional links include post-employment benefit plans and entities providing key management personnel services.
inclusion: Fellow subsidiaries and group parents
Joint ventures and associates
Post-employment benefit plans for employees
exclusion: Entities linked merely by a shared common director without additional control or significant influence
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes structural corporate affiliations and shared control frameworks from casual operational partnerships.

descriptors.definition: Certain common associations do not automatically create related party connections, such as sharing a common director or key management personnel. Similarly, providers of finance, trade unions, public utilities, and dominant customers do not qualify as related parties solely due to normal commercial dealings or economic dependence.
inclusion: Entities sharing common directors without control
Customers or suppliers with significant business volume but no control
exclusion: Entities where common management actively exercises operational control or significant influence
nearby_distinctions: Separates heavy economic dependence or shared board members from actual legal or substantive control relationships.

descriptors.definition: A related party transaction involves a transfer of resources, services, or obligations between a reporting entity and a related party, regardless of whether a price is charged. These transactions encompass asset sales, leases, research transfers, guarantees, and commitments.
inclusion: Purchases or sales of goods and assets
Leases and rendering of services
Provision of guarantees or collateral
exclusion: Normal commercial dealings with entities that are excluded from being related parties like public utilities or trade unions
nearby_distinctions: Applies regardless of consideration pricing, making unpriced transfers or commitments valid transactions.

descriptors.definition: Compensation includes all employee benefits covering short-term, post-employment, long-term, termination benefits, and share-based payments provided in exchange for services. Government-related entities are entities controlled, jointly controlled, or significantly influenced by a government.
inclusion: Short-term employee monetary and non-monetary benefits
Post-employment pensions and medical care
Share-based payments and termination benefits
exclusion: General administrative payments made to public bodies that exercise no control or influence over the reporting entity
nearby_distinctions: Broadens compensation beyond simple cash wages to encompass complex long-term and share-based executive remuneration frameworks.

descriptors.definition: Reporting entities must disclose the name of their parent and ultimate controlling party, which can be an individual, irrespective of whether transactions occurred. If neither produces consolidated financial statements for public use, the name of the next senior parent doing so must be disclosed.
inclusion: Name of the direct parent company
Name of the ultimate controlling party
Name of the next most senior parent producing public consolidated financial statements
exclusion: Parent relationship disclosures where the reporting entity itself is the ultimate parent entity
nearby_distinctions: Mandates relationship disclosures unconditionally even when zero commercial transactions took place during the period.

descriptors.definition: Reporting entities must disclose their parent and ultimate controlling party regardless of transaction history because control relationships constrain independent decision-making. Such disclosures assist users in appraising prospects by revealing credit standing, funding sources, and pricing influences.
inclusion: Parent and ultimate controlling party identity
Nature of related party control relationships
exclusion: Disclosures of operational trade transactions when evaluating this specific structural parent reporting category
nearby_distinctions: Prioritizes structural governance disclosure to evaluate operational constraints over purely financial performance results.

descriptors.definition: Category 2 requires disclosing key management personnel compensation categories alongside transactional data when related party transactions occur during the period. Required minimum disclosures cover transaction amounts, outstanding balances with terms, guarantees, doubtful debt provisions, and bad debt expenses.
inclusion: Total compensation and category-wise breakdown for key management personnel
Transaction amounts and outstanding balance terms and conditions
Provisions and expenses recognized for bad or doubtful related party debts
exclusion: Transactional disclosures when no related party transactions occurred during the respective financial periods
nearby_distinctions: Requires active transaction history during the reporting period, unlike Category 1 disclosures which apply purely based on structural relationships.

descriptors.definition: A reporting entity is exempt from standard related party disclosures concerning transactions, balances, and commitments with a controlling government or other entities controlled by the same government. However, when applying this exemption, the entity must disclose specific details including the identity of the government and qualitative or quantitative information regarding significant transactions.
inclusion: Transactions with a government having control, joint control or significant influence
Transactions with another entity controlled by the same government
Alternative disclosures detailing the nature and amount of significant transactions
exclusion: Standard related party disclosure requirements when the exemption is not elected
Government assistance disclosures governed by other standards
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard commercial related party transactions by providing relief from full disclosures for entities under common government control, requiring instead targeted qualitative and quantitative transparency.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 24 expands related party definitions and reporting scopes compared to AS 18 by encompassing wider familial relationships, broader government-related entity frameworks, and extended key management personnel coverage. These divergences result in increased disclosure obligations for reporting entities under the Indian Accounting Standards framework relative to older Accounting Standards.
inclusion: Comparison of family member definitions
Comparison of state-controlled and government-related enterprise scopes
Comparison of key management personnel inclusions
Comparison of joint venture related party treatments
exclusion: Identical disclosure rules between the two frameworks
General accounting measurement principles
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts modern Ind AS reporting requirements with older AS rules, specifically highlighting wider inclusion thresholds for familial ties and government entities.

descriptors.definition: Earnings per share measures an entity's profitability and resource utilization efficiency by dividing net earnings by ordinary shares. It assists equity shareholders in gauging returns relative to business risks compared to debt-holders.
inclusion: Measures profitability
Serves as basis for price-earnings ratio
Assesses entity current net earnings
exclusion: Debt-holder return calculations
Direct asset valuation
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from debt yields because equity holders undertake residual business and financial risks.

descriptors.definition: The standard prescribes principles for determining and presenting earnings per share to enable performance comparisons across different entities for the same period or across different periods for the same entity. It outlines detailed guidelines for calculating earnings, weighted average shares, and both basic and diluted metrics.
inclusion: Guidelines for calculating basic earnings per share
Guidelines for calculating diluted earnings per share
Mandatory disclosures in consolidated and separate financial statements
exclusion: Non-standardized management performance metrics
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general financial statement objectives by focusing exclusively on per-share performance comparability.

descriptors.definition: Earnings per share data can be constrained because different entities may apply varied accounting policies when determining net earnings. Such discrepancies can impact the comparability of per-share metrics across companies.
inclusion: Variations arising from diverse accounting policies
Impacts on inter-company comparability
exclusion: Computational errors in weighted average shares
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from calculation rules by highlighting qualitative inconsistencies in underlying accounting policies.

descriptors.definition: This standard applies to companies that have issued ordinary shares and are subject to notified Ind AS under the Companies Act. Entities presenting both consolidated and separate financial statements must include the required disclosures in both statements based on their respective information sources.
inclusion: Entities issuing ordinary shares
Disclosures in consolidated financial statements
Disclosures in separate financial statements
exclusion: Entities without ordinary shares issuing only debt instruments
nearby_distinctions: Applies universally to all entities issuing ordinary shares that report under notified Ind AS frameworks.

descriptors.definition: An ordinary share represents a subordinate equity instrument participating in profits only after other share classes, while potential ordinary shares include convertible instruments, options, or warrants that may entitle holders to ordinary shares. Dilution denotes a reduction in earnings per share or an increase in loss per share assuming conversion or exercise of potential ordinary shares.
inclusion: Subordinate equity instruments
Convertible financial liabilities and equity instruments
Share options and warrants
Contingently issuable shares
exclusion: Senior equity instruments like fixed-rate preference shares prior to profit participation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes basic equity ownership from potential future dilution sources like warrants and options.

descriptors.definition: Measurement governs the systematic calculation of basic and diluted earnings per share, incorporating adjustments for potential dilutive instruments, options, warrants, and retrospective adjustments. It establishes how numerators and denominators are derived for reporting periods.
inclusion: Basic EPS earnings and share calculations
Diluted EPS adjustments
Treatment of options and warrants
exclusion: Non-financial operational performance metrics
nearby_distinctions: Encompasses both the fundamental basic metric structure and complex dilutive modifications.

descriptors.definition: Basic earnings per share is calculated by dividing the profit or loss for the period attributable to ordinary equity holders by the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding. The numerator reflects adjustments for preference dividends and equity classifications under relevant standards.
terminology: Weighted average number of ordinary shares
inclusion: Profit or loss attributable to ordinary equity holders
Weighted average ordinary shares denominator calculation
exclusion: Potential ordinary share impacts
nearby_distinctions: Excludes potential dilution effects which are reserved for diluted EPS calculations.

descriptors.definition: Basic earnings per share measures the interest of each ordinary share in parent entity performance by dividing attributable earnings by the weighted average shares. The resulting ratio standardizes per-share profitability for reporting periods.
terminology: Weighted average number of ordinary shares
Profit attributable to equity share holders
inclusion: Mathematical formula for basic EPS
Attributable profit determination
exclusion: Diluted share adjustments
nearby_distinctions: Represents the core unadjusted per-share performance metric.

descriptors.definition: Earnings for basic EPS adjust parent entity profit or loss for after-tax preference dividends, settlement differences, and items credited or debited to reserves instead of profit or loss. Cumulative and non-cumulative preference dividend adjustments are factored in depending on declaration status.
inclusion: After-tax preference dividend adjustments
Deductions for items routed through reserves
Cumulative preference dividend accruals
exclusion: Preference shares classified as liabilities where dividends are treated as finance costs
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates between equity-classified preference dividends requiring numerator adjustments and liability-classified preference dividends handled via finance costs.

descriptors.definition: The weighted average number of ordinary shares reflects the shares outstanding at the beginning of a period adjusted by shares issued or bought back, multiplied by a time-weighting factor. This factor proportions the duration days the shares remain outstanding against total days in the period.
terminology: Weighted average number of ordinary shares
inclusion: Opening ordinary shares
Time-weighted adjustments for share issuances
Time-weighted deductions for share buybacks
exclusion: Simple unweighted closing share balances
nearby_distinctions: Replaces simple period-end share counts with a time-apportioned average reflecting capital changes during the period.

descriptors.definition: Diluted earnings per share adjusts both the attributable profit numerator and the weighted average share denominator for the effects of all dilutive potential ordinary shares. Its objective is to measure ordinary share performance while accounting for potential future issuances.
inclusion: Inclusion of after-tax dividends and interest on potential shares
Addition of converted shares to weighted average denominator
exclusion: Antidilutive potential ordinary shares
nearby_distinctions: Extends basic EPS by factoring in hypothetical conversions that reduce per-share earnings.

descriptors.definition: Entities must calculate diluted earnings per share by adjusting profit attributable to ordinary equity holders and outstanding shares for all dilutive potential ordinary shares. The formula increases attributable profit by recognized interest and dividends on dilutive instruments and expands the share denominator by assumed conversions.
inclusion: Profit adjustments for dilutive instrument interest and dividends
Denominator expansion for assumed conversions
exclusion: Basic unadjusted share computations
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on prospective dilution mechanics rather than historical weighted share balances.

descriptors.definition: Diluted earnings per share measures an entity's performance interest per ordinary share by adjusting profit or loss and the weighted average shares for the effects of all dilutive potential ordinary shares. Numerators are adjusted for after-tax dividends and interest on potential shares, while denominators include incremental shares assumed converted.
terminology: Weighted average number of ordinary shares
Profit or loss attributable to ordinary equity holders
inclusion: Profit or loss from continuing operations attributable to ordinary equity holders
After-tax amount of dividends and interest on dilutive potential ordinary shares
Weighted average of additional ordinary shares from assumed conversions
exclusion: Antidilutive potential ordinary shares
Basic earnings per share computations without potential share adjustments
nearby_distinctions: Basic earnings per share reflects only currently issued ordinary shares without factoring in potential future conversions.

descriptors.definition: The share base for diluted earnings per share combines the weighted average of actual ordinary shares with incremental shares issuable from potential ordinary shares using the if-converted method. Potential shares are weighted for the active period they exist and are evaluated independently for each period presented.
terminology: Weighted average number of ordinary shares
inclusion: Ordinary shares issuable upon conversion of dilutive potential instruments
Cancelled or lapsed potential shares weighted for their active period
exclusion: Antidilutive potential ordinary shares
Interim weighted averages aggregated for year-to-date periods
nearby_distinctions: Unlike basic EPS which only tracks historical actual issuances, diluted EPS applies the if-converted assumption to prospective instruments.

descriptors.definition: Prior period diluted earnings per share is not restated for changed assumptions or conversion outcomes of past potential ordinary shares, though corrections of errors and retrospective accounting policies require restatement. Earnings per share must be presented with equal prominence for all reporting periods alongside required continuing and discontinued operation splits.
inclusion: Adjustments for bonus issues and share consolidations across current and prior periods
Presentation of basic and discontinued operation metrics
exclusion: Restatement of prior period diluted EPS for updated estimation assumptions on contingently issuable shares
nearby_distinctions: Structural changes in share capital without resource changes trigger retrospective adjustments, whereas changes in conversion assumptions do not.

descriptors.definition: Entities must present basic and diluted earnings per share with equal prominence within the statement of profit and loss for every presented period. Negative earnings amounts representing losses per share must be explicitly disclosed alongside distinct figures for continuing and discontinued operations.
inclusion: Basic and diluted amounts for profit or loss from continuing operations
Per share figures for discontinued operations in notes or financial statements
exclusion: Separate dual lines when no potential ordinary shares exist and basic equals diluted EPS
nearby_distinctions: Discontinued operations require separate per-share disclosure, distinguishing them from continuing operations performance metrics.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose numerators and denominators used in basic and diluted earnings per share calculations along with full reconciliation statements. Disclosures must also cover antidilutive instruments excluded from calculations and post-reporting period share transactions.
inclusion: Reconciliation of numerator and denominator components
Descriptions of significant post-reporting date share transactions
exclusion: Retroactive adjustments to reported EPS amounts for post-reporting period share transactions
nearby_distinctions: Post-reporting share transactions are described for informational context but do not alter historical period earnings calculations.

descriptors.definition: Earnings are allocated across ordinary shares, different classes of ordinary shares, and participating equity instruments based on their respective dividend or participation rights. Profit is adjusted for declared dividends before remaining earnings are distributed as if fully paid out.
inclusion: Allocation of profit or loss based on contractual dividend rights
Integration of participation formulas into per-share computations
exclusion: Instruments holding senior prior rights over ordinary equity holders without participation features
nearby_distinctions: Participating instruments share in undistributed earnings via predetermined formulas, unlike standard fixed-return non-convertible preference shares.

descriptors.definition: Equity structures containing instruments that share dividends via predetermined formulas or feature distinct dividend rates require profit allocation across classes. Earnings are distributed by accounting for mandatory dividend commitments first and then allocating residual earnings according to participation rights.
inclusion: Adjustment of parent profit by declared and contractual mandatory dividends
Distribution of remaining earnings as if fully distributed
exclusion: Instruments lacking participation rights or distinct class-based dividend terms
nearby_distinctions: Two-class allocations partition earnings dynamically across differing participation tiers rather than applying a single weighted average base.

descriptors.definition: Partly paid ordinary shares are factored into basic earnings per share as a proportional fraction based on their dividend entitlement relative to fully paid shares. Unpaid portions on partly paid shares are treated as option equivalents where the unpaid balance represents assumed proceeds to purchase shares for diluted calculations.
inclusion: Fractional share weighting based on relative amounts paid up
Unpaid balance treated as option exercise proceeds for diluted EPS
exclusion: Full share weightings for unpaid capital amounts lacking dividend participation rights
nearby_distinctions: Basic EPS treats partly paid shares via proportionate dividend fractions, whereas diluted EPS applies a treasury-stock style option model to unpaid balances.

descriptors.definition: Published financial disclosures from listed commercial entities illustrate practical reporting conventions for earnings per share metrics. These extracts demonstrate the application of disclosure standards across corporate annual reporting frameworks.
inclusion: Real-world corporate presentation examples from major listed companies
exclusion: Normative calculation rules or theoretical definitions
nearby_distinctions: Serves as an illustrative reporting exhibit rather than setting standard-derived computation mandates.
source_ambiguities: The source text consists purely of corporate headings and source citations without substantive rules or definitions.

descriptors.definition: Standard frameworks diverge on treatments for antidilutive disclosures, mandatorily convertible instruments, time-based issuances, and returnable shares. Ind AS mandates comprehensive disclosures and specific timing rules for contingent or mandatory instruments that local standards may omit.
inclusion: Inclusion of mandatorily convertible shares in basic EPS from contract entry date under Ind AS
Exclusion of contingently returnable shares from basic EPS until recall risk lapses
exclusion: Omission of returnable share guidance and passage-of-time rules in legacy standards
nearby_distinctions: Ind AS 33 requires tracking anti-dilutive future potential instruments in notes, a requirement absent in older local accounting frameworks.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide disclosures enabling users to evaluate the nature and financial effects of their business activities and economic environments. This disclosure mandates presenting operational insights from the exact perspective utilized by the entity's management.
inclusion: Financial effects of business activities
Economic environment factors impacting operations
exclusion: Segments reported in separate financial statements when consolidated statements exist
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general financial disclosures by enforcing a strict management viewpoint rather than standardized financial metric groupings.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies to companies required to follow Indian Accounting Standards notified under the Companies Act, 2013. When separate financial statements are presented alongside consolidated statements, segment information is required exclusively in the consolidated financial statements.
inclusion: Companies under notified Indian Accounting Standards
exclusion: Non-compliant disclosures labeled as segment information by exempt entities
Parent's separate financial statements when consolidated statements are present
nearby_distinctions: Restricts mandatory segment reporting exclusively to consolidated financial reports rather than duplicate separate filings.

descriptors.definition: An operating segment is an entity component engaging in business activities that earn revenues and incur expenses, whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, and for which discrete financial information is available. This approach relies entirely on the internal organizational structure utilized by management rather than generalized risk and return assessments.
inclusion: Start-up operations yet to earn revenues
Components with internal review by the CODM and discrete financial data
exclusion: Components lacking discrete financial information or regular review by the CODM
nearby_distinctions: Replaces the risk and return approach of AS 17 with the management approach focused on internal resource allocation.

descriptors.definition: Internal functional units integral to a company's operations, such as research and development, qualify as operating segments if discrete information exists and the chief operating decision maker regularly reviews their results. Similarly, discontinued operations meeting standard business activity, review, and discrete data criteria qualify as operating segments.
inclusion: Research and development functions with discrete reviewed data
Discontinued operations engaging in business activities with reviewed results
exclusion: Integral functions lacking discrete financial metrics or regular management review
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes internal support functions from ordinary revenue-generating segments by requiring active CODM review and discrete data.

descriptors.definition: Discontinued operations meet the definition of an operating segment if they continue engaging in business activities, their operating results are reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, and supporting discrete information is available. Merely examining revenue data alone without broader performance measures may fail to establish an operating segment unless aligned with specific market-building strategies.
inclusion: Discontinued units with ongoing business activities and discrete review data
exclusion: Units devoid of ongoing operational activity or management performance tracking
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates terminated business lines from active segments by requiring active persistence in business activities and active CODM oversight.

descriptors.definition: Entities must report separate information for each operating segment that is identified individually, results from aggregating multiple segments, or exceeds established quantitative thresholds. Additional specific situations defined by the standard may also mandate separate segment reporting.
inclusion: Segments exceeding quantitative thresholds
Aggregated segments meeting combination criteria
exclusion: Operating segments falling below thresholds and not meeting aggregation or utility criteria
nearby_distinctions: Separates broad operating segments from subsets that warrant individual reporting via quantitative metrics or aggregation rules.

descriptors.definition: Two or more operating segments can be combined into a single segment if they exhibit similar long-term financial performance and economic characteristics. Furthermore, the segments must align with the core principle and share identical traits regarding products, production processes, customer types, distribution methods, and regulatory environments.
inclusion: Segments sharing similar gross margins, products, processes, customers, and distribution methods
exclusion: Segments operating under distinct regulatory rules or conflicting economic environments without comparable metrics
nearby_distinctions: Permits consolidation of distinct operating units only when strict qualitative and economic likeness conditions are mutually met.

descriptors.definition: An operating segment becomes reportable if its reported revenue, absolute profit or loss, or assets equal or exceed 10% of the combined totals for all operating segments. Management may also discretionally report segments failing these numeric tests if deemed useful for financial statement users.
inclusion: Segments representing 10% or more of combined segment revenues
Segments holding 10% or more of absolute profit/loss or total assets
exclusion: Segments below the 10% limits unless voluntarily selected by management for user utility
nearby_distinctions: Applies strict mathematical cutoff values to isolate significant segments, distinct from discretionary management grouping.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose general information, performance measures, assets, liabilities, and measurement bases for each period presenting profit or loss statements. Comprehensive reconciliations linking segment totals back to corresponding entity-wide financial statement amounts must also be provided.
inclusion: General organizational factors and aggregation judgments
Reconciliations of segment revenues, assets, and liabilities to entity totals
exclusion: Unreconciled segment figures or missing prior period restatements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes core segment performance metrics from mandatory reconciliations required to tie internal reports to official financial statements.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose the factors utilized to identify reportable segments, encompassing organizational bases like products, services, or geography. Disclosures must also cover management judgments applied during segment aggregation and descriptions of products and services generating segment revenues.
inclusion: Organizational factors used for segment identification
Descriptions of products and services per reportable segment
exclusion: Omission of management judgment rationale or aggregation criteria descriptions
nearby_distinctions: Provides qualitative context regarding segment identification, supplementing the quantitative numerical tables.

descriptors.definition: Entities must report measures of profit or loss, total assets, and total liabilities for each reportable segment if regularly provided to the chief operating decision maker. Specific supplementary financial items like interest, depreciation, and equity-accounted investments must also be disclosed when included in metrics reviewed by the CODM.
inclusion: Revenues from external customers and intersegment transactions
Additions to non-current assets excluding financial instruments and tax assets
exclusion: Items never reviewed by the CODM and excluded from internal reporting measures
nearby_distinctions: Ties mandatory reporting items directly to the internal data package reviewed by the CODM rather than imposing universal line-item checklists.

descriptors.definition: Reported segment items must align with the exact measures supplied to the chief operating decision maker for resource allocation and performance evaluation. Entities must provide clear explanations of measurement bases, transaction accounting between segments, and the nature of differences separating segment totals from entity-wide financial figures.
inclusion: Measures matching internal CODM reporting standards
Explanations of measurement differences between segments and entity financials
exclusion: Arbitrary cost allocations lacking a reasonable basis
nearby_distinctions: Mandates that segment accounting rules mirror internal management reporting tools rather than standardizing separate independent measurement policies.

descriptors.definition: An entity must provide reconciliations of reportable segments' totals for revenues, profit or loss, assets, liabilities, and other material items to the corresponding entity amounts. All material reconciling items must be separately identified and described.
inclusion: Reconciliation of total segment revenues to entity revenues
Reconciliation of total segment profit or loss to entity profit or loss before tax
Reconciliation of segment assets and liabilities if reported
Reconciliation of other material items
exclusion: Disclosed segment amounts without entity-level totals
Unidentified lump-sum adjustments
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from segment revenue measurement because it bridges internal segment measures to external entity financial statements.

descriptors.definition: If an entity changes its internal organizational structure causing reportable segment composition to change, corresponding prior period information must be restated unless information is unavailable and development costs are excessive. When prior period information is not restated, current period segment information must be reported on both old and new bases.
inclusion: Restatement of interim and annual corresponding prior period data
Dual reporting on old and new bases when restatement is impracticable due to excessive cost
exclusion: Changes in accounting estimates without structural organization changes
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard prospective application by mandating dual-basis reporting for the change year if historical restatement is excessively costly.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide entity-wide disclosures regarding products, services, geographical areas, and major customers regardless of how their operating segments are organized. These additional disclosures use financial information utilized to produce the entity's financial statements.
inclusion: Revenues from external customers for products and services
Geographical revenue and non-current asset disclosures
Major customer reliance disclosures
exclusion: Information already reported directly as part of segment reporting requirements under the standard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard segment disclosures because they apply universally across the entity regardless of the internal management approach used to identify operating segments.

descriptors.definition: An entity should report revenues from external customers for each product and service or group of similar products and services based on financial statement data. Disclosure is excused only if necessary information is unavailable and development costs are excessive.
inclusion: Revenues for individual products and services
Revenues for groups of similar products and services
exclusion: Internal intersegment revenues
nearby_distinctions: Differs from geographical disclosures by focusing on product lines rather than physical or regional customer locations.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose external customer revenues and non-current assets attributed to the country of domicile and individual foreign countries, stating the attribution basis used. Material individual foreign country amounts must be presented separately from totals.
inclusion: Revenues attributed to domicile and foreign countries
Non-current assets located in domicile and foreign countries
exclusion: Financial instruments, deferred tax assets, post-employment benefit assets, and insurance rights from non-current asset totals
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from product disclosures by segregating metrics based on geographic locations of customers and asset holdings.

descriptors.definition: An entity must disclose its reliance on major customers if revenues from a single external customer reach or exceed ten percent of total revenues. Common control groups constitute a single customer, while government-controlled entities require judgment regarding economic integration.
inclusion: Disclosure of the fact of dependence when 10% threshold is met
Total amount of revenues from each such customer
Identity of the segment reporting the revenues
exclusion: Disclosure of the specific identity of the major customer
Breakdown of revenues each segment earns from that customer
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard segment revenue reporting by establishing specific customer-concentration disclosure thresholds at the entity level.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 108 adopts a management approach for identifying segments based on internal reports reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, contrasting with AS 17 which relies on primary and secondary risks and returns. Furthermore, Ind AS 108 measures amounts based on management resource allocation and performance evaluation rather than strict accounting policy conformity.
inclusion: Comparison of segment identification approaches
Comparison of reporting measurement bases
Comparison of aggregation criteria and single-segment disclosures
exclusion: Detailed procedural instructions for AS 17 application
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts current management-driven segment identification with older accounting standard frameworks that forced primary and secondary business versus geographical categorizations.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 115 applies to all contracts with customers to provide goods or services in the ordinary course of business for consideration. It excludes specific arrangements such as leases, insurance contracts, financial instruments, and certain non-monetary exchanges.
inclusion: Contracts with customers to provide goods or services as ordinary outputs
exclusion: Lease contracts
Insurance contracts
Financial instruments
Non-monetary exchanges between entities in the same line of business
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes transactions involving ordinary customers from collaboration arrangements where parties share risks and benefits.

descriptors.definition: This section sets out foundational terminology used throughout the revenue standard, including contracts, contract assets, contract liabilities, and performance obligations. These terms provide the technical definitions required to execute the five-step revenue recognition model.
inclusion: Standardized accounting definitions for revenue recognition mechanics
exclusion: Procedural guidance for step execution
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between contract assets conditioned on factors other than the passage of time versus unconditional rights to consideration.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 115 operates on a core principle requiring entities to recognize revenue depicting the transfer of goods or services at expected consideration amounts. This is implemented through a sequential five-step framework spanning contract identification, performance obligation determination, price determination, price allocation, and revenue recognition.
inclusion: Five sequential steps of revenue recognition
Full and modified retrospective transition approaches
exclusion: Detailed industry-specific application guidance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes the overarching five-step methodology from individual operational steps.

descriptors.definition: Entities apply Ind AS 115 either retrospectively or via a modified retrospective approach with cumulative effects recognized at initial application. The initial step requires identifying enforceable agreements with customers, which can be written, oral, or implied by customary business practices.
inclusion: Transition adjustment mechanics
Recognition of oral and implied contracts based on customary practices
exclusion: Performance obligation allocation methods
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes full restatement of prior periods from cumulative-effect opening retained earnings adjustments.

descriptors.definition: Step 1 acts as a mandatory gateway requiring an entity to establish that an agreement creates legally enforceable rights and obligations. Entities must evaluate local legal environments to confirm enforceability before applying subsequent steps of the revenue model.
inclusion: Legal enforceability assessment
Evaluation of written, oral, or implied agreements
exclusion: Subsequent performance obligation allocation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes preliminary negotiations lacking enforceability from binding contracts that pass the Step 1 gateway.

descriptors.definition: A contract is accounted for under Ind AS 115 only when approval, identification of rights, identification of payment terms, commercial substance, and probable collection of consideration are met. If these criteria fail at inception, no accounting contract exists and non-refundable consideration received is deferred.
inclusion: Five mandatory criteria for contract recognition
Deferral of non-refundable consideration when criteria are unmet
exclusion: Contracts meeting all criteria at inception requiring reassessment without significant factual changes
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes arrangements where collection is probable from high credit-risk arrangements failing initial contract criteria.

descriptors.definition: Once a contract passes Step 1, existence is not reassessed unless significant facts and circumstances change adversely, such as a customer's credit deterioration. The contract term covers the period in which parties have present enforceable rights and obligations.
inclusion: Prospective impact analysis for subsequent collectibility failures
Contractual period definition
exclusion: Retrospective reversal of previously recognized revenues or receivables
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes prospective adjustments on remaining obligations from retrospective restatements of transferred goods.

descriptors.definition: A contract does not exist if each party can unilaterally terminate a wholly unperformed contract without penalty. Substantive termination penalties establish enforceable rights and obligations throughout the penalty period, determining the accounting contract term.
inclusion: Evaluation of cancellation clauses and cancellation penalties
Determination of enforceable contract duration
exclusion: Contracts with non-substantive termination penalties extending beyond cancellation dates
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes penalty-free cancellable periods from periods bound by substantive termination penalties.

descriptors.definition: Entities must combine two or more contracts entered into at or near the same time with the same customer if they share a commercial objective, pricing interdependence, or constitute a single performance obligation. Such arrangements are accounted for as a single contract to reflect their commercial substance.
inclusion: Aggregation of contracts with linked pricing or single commercial objectives
exclusion: Contracts negotiated simultaneously but serving independent commercial objectives with distinct performance obligations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes integrated packages requiring combined accounting from separate contracts executed concurrently.

descriptors.definition: A contract modification is an approved change in contract scope, price, or both. Modifications are accounted for either as separate distinct contracts, as a termination of the old contract and creation of a new one, or through cumulative catch-up adjustments.
inclusion: Identification of scope and price amendments
Separate contract treatment for distinct goods priced at stand-alone values
exclusion: Unapproved operational changes lacking legal enforceability
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes modifications treated as separate standalone contracts from those requiring cumulative catch-up adjustments.

descriptors.definition: Performance obligations serve as the fundamental unit of account in Ind AS 115, dictating when revenue is recognized. Entities must evaluate explicit promises as well as implicit commitments arising from customary business practices or published policies.
inclusion: Explicit contractual promises
Implicit promises creating valid customer expectations
exclusion: Administrative steps unrelated to transferring promised goods or services
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes explicit contract terms from implied obligations generated by established business policies.

descriptors.definition: At contract inception, entities assess all promised goods or services to identify distinct performance obligations. Promises can encompass manufactured goods, retail merchandise, consulting tasks, standby availability, asset construction, intellectual property licenses, or future purchase options.
inclusion: Evaluations of various promised outputs including tasks, licenses, and future options
exclusion: Activities that do not transfer a promised good or service to the customer
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes distinct promises evaluated as separate performance obligations from integrated components of a single combined promise.

descriptors.definition: When goods or services in a contract are bundled such that they do not qualify as distinct on an individual basis, an entity must combine them with other items until a distinct bundle is formed. This combined group of promises is then accounted for as a single performance obligation based on the specific contract terms.
inclusion: Combining non-distinct goods or services into a single performance obligation
Assessing distinctness relative to specific contract bundling
exclusion: Treating individual goods or services as separate performance obligations when they are distinct on their own and unbundled
nearby_distinctions: Unlike separately distinct goods, non-distinct items are aggregated with others under the contract until a distinct bundle is identified.

descriptors.definition: Options granted to customers to acquire additional goods or services constitute a separate performance obligation only if they provide a material right that would not be received without entering into the contract. If the option merely offers a stand-alone market price, it is treated as a standard marketing offer rather than an advance payment for future goods.
inclusion: Customer award credits
Discounts exceeding normal market ranges creating a material right
exclusion: Marketing offers priced at standard stand-alone selling prices without conferring a material right
