descriptors.definition: If management refuses to correct identified misstatements, the auditor communicates with governance and evaluates reporting implications or legal withdrawal options. For post-report discoveries, the auditor takes appropriate legal steps to bring uncorrected errors to user attention.
inclusion: Post-audit report discovery actions
Communication with those charged with governance
exclusion: Direct alteration of the other information by the auditor
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between pre-report and post-report discovery workflows for uncorrected material items.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must include a designated Other Information section in the audit report under specified entity conditions, outlining management responsibility and stating that no assurance is expressed thereon. It also details whether the auditor has anything to report or needs to describe an uncorrected misstatement.
inclusion: Statements on management responsibility
Descriptions of auditor responsibilities
exclusion: Providing an audit opinion or assurance conclusion on the other information
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from the main opinion paragraph, acting as a transparency disclosure rather than an attestation.

descriptors.definition: The audit report must feature a dedicated section detailing management obligations, identification of reviewed documents, and an explicit lack of assurance on other information. This requirement triggers based on whether the entity is listed or unlisted and if documents are obtained.
inclusion: Mandatory section generation for listed entities expecting other information
Conditional section generation for unlisted entities
exclusion: Omitting the section when other information is neither obtained nor expected for unlisted entities
nearby_distinctions: Applies varying triggers depending on the corporate classification of the audited entity.

descriptors.definition: When regulations mandate specific layouts for referencing other information, the auditor may reference Standards on Auditing only if minimum content requirements like scope identification and outcome statements are met. This standard governs the boundaries of auditor liability regarding supplementary disclosures.
inclusion: Minimum compliance elements for statutory wording
References to auditing standards alongside regulatory formats
exclusion: Referring to SAs when mandated minimum elements are omitted
nearby_distinctions: Balances customized regulatory reporting templates against the baseline requirements of auditing standards.

descriptors.definition: Statutory provisions require company auditors to inquire into specific operational matters, such as loan securities, book entries, and share allotments. A separate report to members is necessitated only if the auditor uncovers adverse findings requiring special commentary.
inclusion: Inquiries into security of loans and advances
Checking cash receipts for share allotments
exclusion: Filing positive confirmation reports when statutory inquiries reveal no adverse conditions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general financial statement verification by focusing on specific statutory compliance checks mandated by corporate law.

descriptors.definition: Issued under statutory authority, the order mandates additional reporting disclosures for eligible companies alongside the primary audit report. Specific entity types, such as banking companies, insurance entities, and small companies meeting specific criteria, are exempt from these extra requirements.
inclusion: Additional reporting for qualifying corporations
Exemption evaluations for small and private companies
exclusion: Banking and insurance company inclusion
Consolidated financial statement applicability
nearby_distinctions: Acts as an supplementary reporting order rather than the standard financial statement audit opinion.

descriptors.definition: An independent auditor's report contains structured sections including the opinion, basis of opinion, and key audit matters. An emphasis of matter paragraph draws attention to critical disclosures, such as facility damage, without modifying the core audit opinion.
inclusion: Illustrative report formatting
Emphasis of matter disclosures
exclusion: Modifying the auditor opinion due to disclosed emphasis items
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between explanatory emphasis paragraphs and actual modifications or qualifications of the audit opinion.

descriptors.definition: Specialized auditing standards address distinct engagements including special purpose frameworks, single financial statements or specific elements, and summary financial statements. These engagements impose specific responsibilities regarding engagement acceptance, planning, performance, and reporting.
inclusion: Audits under special purpose frameworks
Audits of single financial statements or specific elements
Engagements on summary financial statements
exclusion: General purpose financial statement audits under standard series 100-700
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general purpose audits by focusing on specific user needs or specific financial components.

descriptors.definition: SA 800 governs special considerations for auditing financial statements prepared under a special purpose framework. It regulates engagement acceptance, planning, performance, and the formation of an audit opinion.
inclusion: Cash basis financial statements
Regulator-established financial provisions
Contractual financial provisions
exclusion: General purpose financial statements designed for common needs of wide range of users
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general purpose frameworks by targeting specific financial information needs of distinct users.

descriptors.definition: A special purpose framework is a financial reporting framework designed to meet the specific financial information needs of particular users. It determines the form, content, and completeness of the special purpose financial statements including related notes.
terminology: Complete Set of Special Purpose Financial Statements
inclusion: Summary of significant accounting policies
Other explanatory information
exclusion: Frameworks designed for common financial information needs of wide range of users
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with general purpose frameworks by catering exclusively to targeted user groups rather than general public or diverse stakeholders.

descriptors.definition: Acceptability of a special purpose framework depends on intended user needs and whether promulgated standards follow a transparent deliberation process. For frameworks arising from contracts, acceptability is evaluated by examining if the framework exhibits standard attributes under professional judgment.
inclusion: Standard-setting organization frameworks
Regulator-prescribed provisions
Contractual or other source provisions
exclusion: Frameworks lacking transparent stakeholder deliberation without established attributes
nearby_distinctions: Requires evaluating specific user needs rather than common broad user needs found in general purpose audits.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must comply with relevant auditing standards while adapting specific requirements, such as material judgments based on intended users rather than general groups. In contract-based statements, auditors must understand significant management interpretations and account for agreed misstatement thresholds.
inclusion: Evaluating significant contract interpretations
Assessing materiality tailored to intended users
exclusion: Standard general materiality calculations omitting specific user information needs
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general audits by focusing materiality and risk assessments on specific user needs and contract terms.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must evaluate whether special purpose financial statements adequately describe the framework and any significant contract interpretations. The auditor's report must describe the preparation purpose, identify intended users, and reference management's responsibility for framework acceptability.
inclusion: Description of purpose and intended users
Management framework acceptability responsibility
exclusion: Standard general purpose reporting paragraphs lacking purpose descriptions
nearby_distinctions: Requires explicit disclosure of the specific purpose and target users absent in standard general purpose audit reports.

descriptors.definition: To prevent misunderstandings from secondary usage, auditors include an Emphasis of Matter paragraph explaining that statements are prepared using a special purpose framework and may be unsuitable for other purposes. Auditors may also restrict report distribution exclusively to specified users.
inclusion: Emphasis of Matter paragraph regarding framework unsuitability
Distribution restriction clauses
exclusion: Unrestricted general purpose audit reports
nearby_distinctions: Mandates explicit warnings regarding unsuitability for alternative uses, unlike general purpose reports.

descriptors.definition: Auditors can restrict report distribution and use to specific contractual parties via dedicated report wording to prevent misuse. This is coupled with a basis of accounting reference highlighting the precise purpose of the financial statements.
inclusion: Designating specific intended corporate recipients
Explicit prohibition of distribution to third parties
exclusion: Publicly filed general purpose reports without circulation caps
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on legal and contractual boundaries limiting who can legally read or utilize the audit output.

descriptors.definition: Standards in the 100-700 series apply and are adapted for audits of single financial statements or specific elements, accounts, or items. When these components utilize a special purpose framework, SA 800 also applies to the engagement.
inclusion: Audits of single financial statements like cash flow statements
Audits of specific accounts like trade receivables
exclusion: Component auditor reports requested by a principal auditor for consolidated financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Applies audit requirements to standalone financial components instead of complete sets of financial statements.

descriptors.definition: A single financial statement is an individual financial statement, such as a cash flow statement, distinct from a complete set of financial statements. It includes relevant notes covering significant accounting policies and explanatory information.
inclusion: Individual financial statements with related explanatory notes
exclusion: Complete set of general purpose financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Represents only one standalone statement rather than an entire financial package.

descriptors.definition: An element means a specific element, account, or item of a financial statement, which includes related explanatory notes and accounting policies. Examples include trade receivables or cash and bank balances.
inclusion: Trade receivables
Cash and bank balances
exclusion: Full financial statements or aggregated category totals spanning multiple statements
nearby_distinctions: Targeted exclusively at micro-components or line items within a statement rather than whole statements.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must comply with all relevant SAs during single statement or element audits regardless of whether they audit the complete set. If not auditing the complete set, auditors must evaluate audit practicability given potential lack of entity understanding or corroborative records.
inclusion: Evaluating entity and internal control comprehension limitations
Assessing disproportionate audit work requirements
exclusion: Audits where the auditor simultaneously performs the complete entity financial statement audit
nearby_distinctions: Addresses feasibility hurdles when an auditor lacks broad background knowledge from a full entity audit.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must adapt all relevant standards as necessary when auditing single financial statements or specific elements. This includes evaluating risks like fraud, related party transactions, and going concern assumptions under the reporting framework.
inclusion: adaptation of auditing standards for specific elements
evaluation of related party transactions
assessment of going concern application
exclusion: audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements without modifications
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a full scope complete financial statement audit by focusing adaptation efforts solely on the specific requested element or single statement.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must evaluate whether the expected form of opinion is appropriate based on the applicable financial reporting framework and governing regulations. Factors include whether the framework explicitly or implicitly restricts itself to complete financial statement sets.
inclusion: evaluation of reporting phrases for fair presentation versus compliance frameworks
assessment of framework restrictions
exclusion: standard unmodified reporting on complete sets of financial statements without framework ambiguity
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard reporting by requiring specific checks on whether single statement presentations are explicitly addressed by the chosen framework.

descriptors.definition: The auditor applies Revised SA 700 and other relevant standards, adapted as necessary, when forming an opinion and reporting on single statements or elements. Specific disclosures must enable users to understand the effect of material transactions and events.
inclusion: evaluation of adequate disclosures for single statements
adaptation of going concern and key audit matter descriptions
exclusion: unadapted standard audit reports on standard general purpose financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on tailoring standard disclosure evaluation and specialized sections like key audit matters to limited financial contexts.

descriptors.definition: Auditors ordinarily accept engagements to report on summary financial statements only if they have also conducted the audit of the underlying financial statements. Management must apply acceptable criteria to ensure summaries are consistent and not misleading due to aggregation.
inclusion: prerequisite audit of source financial statements
evaluation of management's preparation criteria acceptability
exclusion: accepting summary reporting engagements where the auditor did not audit the full historical financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general engagement acceptance by enforcing a strict prerequisite dependency on prior full-set audit access and knowledge.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must evaluate whether summaries disclose their nature, identify audited statements, and agree with or recalculate from source data. Procedures ensure summaries are prepared using applied criteria and maintain an appropriate level of aggregation without being misleading.
inclusion: comparing summaries with audited financial statement information
evaluating disclosure of applied criteria and source availability
exclusion: performing full substantive re-audits of every individual underlying transaction category
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from detailed substantive testing by focusing on comparison, recalculation from source, and aggregation evaluation.

descriptors.definition: When expressing an unmodified opinion, the auditor states that summaries are consistent in all material respects with, or are a fair summary of, the audited statements based on applied criteria. If prescribed statutory wording causes user misunderstanding that additional explanations cannot mitigate, the auditor must decline or drop the engagement.
inclusion: specific unmodified opinion phrasing options
evaluation of user misunderstanding risks
exclusion: issuing standard audit opinions designed for complete general purpose financial statement sets
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with standard audit opinions by using specialized consistency or fair summary phrases tied directly to applied criteria.

descriptors.definition: When the underlying audit report contains modifications, emphasis of matter, or other special sections, the summary report must state this fact and describe the basis and effect on the summaries. The summary report date cannot precede the date of the underlying audit report or the collection of sufficient evidence.
inclusion: disclosure of underlying report modifications in the summary report
dating restrictions relative to the main audit report
exclusion: issuing clean summary reports when underlying reports contain adverse opinions or disclaimers
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard reporting updates by requiring explicit cascading descriptions of prior modifications and their specific impacts on summarized figures.

descriptors.definition: If the auditor's report on the audited financial statements contains a distribution restriction or an alert regarding a special purpose framework, a similar restriction or alert must be included in the summary financial report. This ensures users are properly notified of the constrained use or specialized basis of the underlying data.
inclusion: duplicating special framework alerts in summary reports
replicating distribution use limitations
exclusion: issuing unrestricted general-use reports when underlying data deployment is contractually or legally restricted
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by its derivative nature, mirroring limitations directly from the primary audit engagement context rather than establishing new ones.

descriptors.definition: The auditor determines the reasonableness of omitting comparatives in summary statements and handles reports involving predecessor auditors. Unaudited supplementary information presented alongside summaries must be clearly differentiated to avoid association issues.
inclusion: evaluating omitted comparatives reasonableness
handling another auditor's comparative reports
reviewing differentiation of supplementary information
exclusion: automatic acceptance of unverified supplementary data integrated without clear boundary separation
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on comparative omissions and supplementary data boundaries rather than primary summary figures generation.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must prevent inappropriate association or referencing when entities mention the auditor in documents containing summaries without including the actual report. Appropriate actions must be taken if management refuses to correct misleading references or omit auditor mentions.
inclusion: actions against unauthorized auditor name referencing
securing inclusion of audit reports in summary documents
exclusion: authorized report inclusions where the auditor was formally engaged to report on the summaries
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general review procedures by targeting external document references and protecting the auditor's professional reputation against misuse.

descriptors.definition: When summary reports are dated after the underlying audit report, the report must specify that neither summaries nor audited statements reflect subsequent events occurring after the original audit report date. Discovery of prior facts requires completion of subsequent event reviews before issuing summary reports.
inclusion: dating summary reports later than underlying audit reports
handling newly discovered facts existing at the original audit report date
exclusion: obtaining fresh audit evidence on underlying financial statements solely due to the passage of time before summary issuance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by addressing timing gaps between primary audit completion and summary reporting without requiring a re-audit of historical balances.

descriptors.definition: Non-assurance services provided by practicing chartered accountants are standardized under specific related services frameworks. These include agreed-upon procedures and financial compilation engagements where no truth and fairness opinion is expressed.
inclusion: Tax return preparation without assurance
Consulting and advisory engagements
Agreed-upon procedures engagements
exclusion: Engagements involving the expression of an audit opinion
Engagements providing direct assurance to users
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from assurance engagements by the absence of an evaluation conclusion designed to enhance user confidence.

descriptors.definition: An auditor carries out audit-nature procedures agreed upon with the entity and appropriate third parties to issue a factual findings report. No assurance is expressed, leaving users to draw their own conclusions.
inclusion: Procedures concerning individual financial data items
Comparison of supplier statements to trial balances
exclusion: Engagements providing an audit opinion
Reviews of financial statements expressing limited assurance
nearby_distinctions: Differs from audits and reviews because it entirely omits the expression of an assurance conclusion.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner performs agreed-upon audit-nature procedures with the entity and specified third parties to report factual findings. The engagement produces a restricted report devoid of any assurance conclusions.
inclusion: Carrying out specific verification steps on accounts
Reporting actual numerical variations without assurance
exclusion: Expressing an audit opinion
Providing general public assurance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard audits by restricting report distribution and omitting professional assurance.

descriptors.definition: An audit yields an opinion providing user assurance, whereas an agreed-upon procedures engagement reports only factual findings without any assurance. Users independently assess the reported findings to draw their own conclusions.
inclusion: Comparison of supplier names and balances
Obtaining and comparing third-party confirmations
exclusion: Issuing an opinion on financial statements taken as a whole
Providing moderate or high assurance
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with statutory audits which inherently require an expression of an opinion on truth and fairness.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must comply with ICAI ethical principles like integrity and objectivity while planning and executing agreed-upon procedures. Independence is not mandatory unless specifically required by engagement terms.
inclusion: Documenting key terms via an engagement letter
Stating lack of independence in the report if applicable
exclusion: Mandatory independence across all engagement instances
Performing procedures constituting an audit or review
nearby_distinctions: Unlike assurance engagements, independence is optional unless specified by the objective or terms of the engagement.

descriptors.definition: The factual findings report must detail the purpose and agreed procedures sufficiently while explicitly stating that no audit or review was performed. It requires specific elements including a restricted distribution statement and concrete exceptions found.
inclusion: Listing specific procedures performed
Describing errors and exceptions discovered
exclusion: Expressing an opinion or conclusion on the financial statements
Unrestricted public distribution of findings
nearby_distinctions: Differs from audit reports by omitting an opinion paragraph and explicitly denying the expression of assurance.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must maintain documentation that provides evidence supporting the reported factual findings and demonstrates that the engagement adhered to relevant standards and terms. This documentation forms the evidentiary basis for the issued report.
inclusion: Working papers supporting specific factual findings
Records showing compliance with professional standards
exclusion: Evidence required for statutory audit opinions
Documentation for unperformed procedures
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on supporting factual outcomes of agreed procedures rather than forming an overall audit opinion.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners assist management in preparing and presenting historical financial information using accounting expertise without gathering evidence for assurance. The standard applies equally to compilation engagements for other financial or non-financial information.
inclusion: Assisting management with mandatory periodic reporting
Preparing financial information for internal management use
exclusion: Engagements requiring audit opinions or review conclusions
Verifying accuracy or completeness of provided source data
nearby_distinctions: Unlike review or audit engagements, compilers do not verify information accuracy or gather evidence for conclusions.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner applies accounting and financial reporting expertise to help management prepare and present financial information under an applicable framework. The engagement concludes with a compilation report matching standard requirements without assurance.
inclusion: Applying technical accounting knowledge to draft statements
Issuing a compilation report
exclusion: Providing assurance on financial statements
Independent verification of underlying source data
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes technical preparation assistance rather than independent investigative auditing.

descriptors.definition: Compilation scope involves assisting management in preparing financial information based on management-provided data under a chosen reporting framework. Management retains full responsibility for the financial information, accounting policies, and estimates.
inclusion: Assisting with entity-specific accounting bases
Working with management-prepared draft statements
exclusion: Practitioner assumption of management financial preparation responsibilities
Independent testing of internal controls for assurance
nearby_distinctions: Management retains ultimate responsibility for judgments and estimates, while the practitioner merely applies technical compilation expertise.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners must adhere to relevant ethical requirements and identify and address threats to compliance. Because compilation is a non-assurance service, standard independence rules do not apply unless mandated by specific laws.
inclusion: Identifying ethical threats during compilation
Complying with statutory independence rules if prescribed
exclusion: Universal enforcement of strict independence for all compilations
Assurance-level ethical constraints
nearby_distinctions: Independence rules are non-mandatory for compilations unless specific local regulations dictate otherwise.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners must formally agree on engagement terms with management in writing before performing a compilation. Management remains explicitly responsible for the financial framework, internal controls, and data completeness.
inclusion: Documenting terms in an engagement letter prior to work
Evaluating recurring engagement continuance criteria
exclusion: Accepting engagements without agreed terms
Practitioner assumption of internal control maintenance
nearby_distinctions: Requires explicit written agreement regarding data completeness responsibilities before engagement execution begins.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner gathers sufficient understanding of the entity and framework to compile financial information from management records and discussions. If records are incomplete or amendments are refused, the practitioner must propose changes or withdraw from the engagement.
inclusion: obtaining understanding of entity operations and accounting system
reading compiled information against understanding prior to completion
requesting additional information for incomplete records
exclusion: expressing an audit opinion
performing verification of accuracy or completeness of provided data
nearby_distinctions: differs from assurance engagements because verification and testing of data are not performed
differs from management responsibilities as the practitioner only assists and compiles based on given data

descriptors.definition: The practitioner must timely communicate all significant engagement matters to management or those charged with governance. The resulting written report clearly details the engagement nature and responsibilities without providing an assurance opinion.
inclusion: communicating significant engagement matters on a timely basis
issuing a written report containing required elements
identifying the applicable financial reporting framework
exclusion: expressing an audit opinion or review conclusion
verifying underlying information accuracy
nearby_distinctions: differs from audit reporting because it explicitly states no opinion or review conclusion is provided
differs from informal updates by requiring a formal written report with specific mandated elements

descriptors.definition: A written report issued to clearly communicate the engagement nature and the practitioner role without expressing any assurance opinion. It includes structural elements such as responsibilities, reporting framework identification, and statements that verification is not performed.
inclusion: stating that the compilation is based on management information
describing management and practitioner responsibilities
explaining that compilation is not an assurance engagement
exclusion: expressing an audit opinion
expressing a review conclusion
nearby_distinctions: differs from audit and review reports by omitting any expression of opinion or conclusion
differs from engagement terms by serving as the final formal communication vehicle to users

descriptors.definition: The engagement partner assumes responsibility for ensuring overall engagement quality and adherence to firm quality control policies. Documentation must capture significant matters, reconciliation records, and the final compiled financial information copy.
inclusion: taking responsibility for overall engagement quality
recording how compiled information reconciles with underlying records
retaining a copy of the final compiled financial information and report
exclusion: delegating partner responsibility for quality control compliance
omitting reconciliation documentation
nearby_distinctions: differs from firm-wide quality control by focusing specifically on individual engagement execution and partner oversight
differs from general working papers by requiring specific acknowledgment of responsibility from management

descriptors.definition: The practitioner maintains comprehensive engagement documentation recording significant matters, how they were addressed, and reconciliation of financial information. It also preserves the final compiled version approved by management along with the practitioner report.
inclusion: documenting significant matters arising during the engagement
maintaining a reconciliation record with underlying documents
including copies of final compiled financial information and practitioner report
exclusion: excluding final management-acknowledged financial information from files
omitting records of how matters were addressed
nearby_distinctions: differs from management records by specifically constituting the practitioner working papers and engagement file
differs from preliminary drafts by containing the final version acknowledged by management

descriptors.definition: A review is a limited assurance engagement designed to reduce engagement risk to an acceptable level that is higher than in an audit. It evaluates historical financial statements through sufficient and appropriate evidence gathering to enhance user confidence.
inclusion: General purpose financial statements
Special purpose financial statements
Historical financial information
exclusion: Reasonable assurance engagements
Full scope statutory audits
nearby_distinctions: Unlike an audit which provides reasonable assurance, a review provides limited assurance with fewer procedures.

descriptors.definition: Standards on Review Engagements govern the performance of review services by practitioners on financial information. These standards form part of engagement standards where quality control is premised on the firm adhering to quality frameworks.
inclusion: Review of historical financial statements
Review of interim financial information
exclusion: Non-assurance compilation services
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from auditing standards by targeting lower assurance thresholds and procedure volumes.

descriptors.definition: SRE 2400 governs a practitioner's responsibilities when reviewing historical financial statements when they are not the entity's auditor. The practitioner primarily uses inquiry and analytical procedures, supplemented by additional procedures if potential material misstatements are identified.
inclusion: Practitioner responsibilities for non-audit clients
Form and content of the review report
exclusion: Reviews performed by the independent statutory auditor of the entity
nearby_distinctions: Applies specifically when the reviewing practitioner is independent of the recurring annual audit role.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner aims to obtain limited assurance on whether financial statements are free from material misstatement using inquiries and analytical procedures. If limited assurance cannot be obtained and modification is insufficient, the practitioner must disclaim a conclusion or withdraw.
inclusion: Expressing a negative assurance conclusion
Engagement withdrawal or disclaimer protocols
exclusion: Unmodified positive audit opinions
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on negative form conclusions rather than positive assurance opinions.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners must refuse a review engagement if there is no rational purpose, ethical or independence requirements fail, required information is unavailable or unreliable, or management integrity is doubtful. Engagements intended to satisfy statutory audit requirements lack a rational purpose for review.
inclusion: Evaluations of scope limitations
Assessment of management trustworthiness
exclusion: Engagements with statutory audit mandates requiring full audits
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between appropriate review scenarios and situations where a full audit or compilation is mandated.

descriptors.definition: Before accepting a review, the practitioner must verify the acceptability of the financial reporting framework and obtain management's agreement on responsibilities. Management must acknowledge responsibility for financial statement preparation, internal controls, and providing unrestricted access to information and personnel.
inclusion: Verification of framework suitability
Written acknowledgement of management duties
exclusion: Engagements lacking management commitment to internal controls or record access
nearby_distinctions: Mandates explicit preconditions similar to audits, tailored specifically for review engagements.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner must record agreed terms in an engagement letter prior to performance and evaluate changes when circumstances shift. Materiality for the financial statements as a whole must be determined and applied identically regardless of the lower assurance level.
inclusion: Engagement letter documentation
Materiality determination for financial statements as a whole
exclusion: Undocumented informal engagement terms
nearby_distinctions: Maintains the same concept of financial statement materiality as audits despite lower evidence collection.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner uses an Emphasis of Matter paragraph to draw attention to fundamental disclosed items in the financial statements supported by sufficient appropriate evidence. Other matters relevant to understanding the review or practitioner responsibilities are reported under an Other Matter heading.
inclusion: Emphasis of Matter paragraphs
Other Matter disclosures
exclusion: Matters not presented or disclosed in the financial statements placed in Emphasis of Matter
nearby_distinctions: Emphasis of Matter references disclosed financial data, whereas Other Matter addresses external review responsibilities.

descriptors.definition: Review documentation must provide a sufficient record of the work performed to enable an experienced practitioner with no prior connection to understand the procedures, results, and judgments. Documentation must capture the nature, timing, extent of work, review quality control details, and the resolution of inconsistent information.
inclusion: Recording work performer details and dates
Documenting quality control review extent
Resolutions of contradictory findings
exclusion: Undocumented oral discussions without engagement rationale
nearby_distinctions: Mirrors audit documentation stringency by requiring proof of procedure execution and professional judgment.

descriptors.definition: This concept covers documentation retention mandates and sets up the comparative distinction between audits and reviews. Reviews require fewer procedures and lower assurance thresholds compared to extensive audit testing.
inclusion: Summary records of review execution
Cross-comparison of audit and review characteristics
exclusion: Absence of audit-level control testing in reviews
nearby_distinctions: Bridges detailed documentation requirements with structural differences between audit and review modalities.

descriptors.definition: Audits provide reasonable assurance using extensive substantive and control testing with a positively worded opinion. Conversely, reviews deliver limited assurance through inquiry and analytical procedures, culminating in a negatively worded conclusion.
inclusion: Comparison of testing volume
Contrast between positive and negative reporting language
exclusion: Equating review conclusions with audit opinions
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts the high-assurance, procedure-heavy audit model with the inquiry-focused, low-assurance review model.

descriptors.definition: SRE 2410 governs the professional responsibilities of an independent statutory auditor when reviewing interim financial information for an audit client. Interim information comprises complete or condensed financial sets spanning periods shorter than a full financial year.
inclusion: Quarterly financial reviews by statutory auditors
Condensed interim statement evaluations
exclusion: Reviews performed by practitioners independent of the annual audit appointment
nearby_distinctions: Differs from SRE 2400 by specifically applying to the entity's incumbent independent auditor rather than an outside practitioner.

descriptors.definition: The objective is to enable an auditor to express a conclusion on whether anything causes them to believe interim financial information is not prepared in all material respects under the applicable framework. It utilizes inquiries and analytical procedures to reduce the risk of an inappropriate conclusion to a moderate level.
inclusion: Review of interim financial information by the independent auditor
exclusion: Expressing an audit opinion providing a true and fair view
nearby_distinctions: Differs from an audit by providing lower moderate assurance rather than reasonable assurance and omitting extensive corroborating tests.

descriptors.definition: The auditor and client must agree on engagement terms, which are usually documented in an engagement letter. This communication prevents misunderstandings regarding the scope, objectives, responsibilities, and reporting format.
inclusion: Recording agreed terms in writing
exclusion: Unwritten verbal understandings without documentation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from subsequent audit planning by establishing baseline roles and scope agreements explicitly.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must update their understanding of the entity, its environment, and internal control as relevant to both annual and interim financial information. This updated knowledge assists in identifying potential material misstatements and selecting appropriate review procedures.
inclusion: Reading preceding year audit documentation
Considering prior significant risks
exclusion: Relying solely on historical annual controls without interim verification
nearby_distinctions: Updates prior annual knowledge specifically focusing on differences pertinent to interim reporting periods.

descriptors.definition: Auditors perform inquiries primarily of financial management and analytical review procedures to evaluate the preparation of interim financial information. These procedures generally omit intensive record testing via inspection, observation, or confirmation.
inclusion: Reading governance meeting minutes
Inquiring of financial management
exclusion: Extensive physical inventory counts
Direct third-party balance confirmations
nearby_distinctions: Differs from audit testing by relying on inquiry and analysis rather than corroborative inspection and confirmation.

descriptors.definition: The auditor evaluates uncorrected misstatements and inadequate disclosures individually and in aggregate to determine if material adjustments are necessary. Professional judgment is applied to assess their impact under the financial reporting framework.
inclusion: Assessing individual and aggregate uncorrected items
Evaluating disclosure adequacy
exclusion: Ignoring minor discrepancies without professional evaluation
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on evaluating uncorrected items found during interim review procedures rather than full final audit adjustments.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must obtain specific written representations from management acknowledging responsibilities for internal controls, fraud prevention, compliance, and accurate interim presentation. These representations confirm management disclosures on uncorrected misstatements and subsequent events.
inclusion: Management acknowledgment of internal control responsibility
Disclosure of known frauds
exclusion: Verbal management assurances lacking formal written confirmation
nearby_distinctions: Serves as formal written confirmation of management's responsibilities specifically tailored to interim reporting assertions.

descriptors.definition: The auditor reads accompanying information to identify material inconsistencies with the interim financial information. If management refuses necessary amendments, the auditor considers report implications, withholding issuance, or engagement withdrawal.
inclusion: Reviewing documents accompanying interim statements
Evaluating alternative earnings measures
exclusion: Auditing information completely unrelated to financial reporting disclosures
nearby_distinctions: Focused on consistency checks with supplementary documents rather than core primary interim statements.

descriptors.definition: When review procedures reveal required material adjustments, fraud, or non-compliance, the auditor must communicate these matters promptly to management and those charged with governance. Oral communications must be documented appropriately.
inclusion: Reporting required adjustments to management
Documenting oral communications
exclusion: Withholding known fraud or significant non-compliance findings
nearby_distinctions: Mandates timely upward reporting of significant anomalies discovered during interim analytical reviews.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must issue a written review report containing an appropriate title, addressee, financial statement identification, and management responsibilities. It must explicitly state that the review followed applicable review standards and provides substantially less scope than an audit.
inclusion: Statement of management and auditor responsibilities
Description of review procedures
exclusion: Expressing a positive audit opinion or true and fair assurance
nearby_distinctions: Provides a descriptive conclusion on interim review results instead of a high-assurance audit opinion.

descriptors.definition: The auditor expresses a qualified or adverse conclusion when uncorrected material departures from the framework affect the interim financial information. The report must detail the nature of the departure and, if practicable, its financial effects.
inclusion: Adding explanatory paragraphs for departures
Issuing adverse conclusions for pervasive misstatements
exclusion: Issuing an unmodified clean report when material departures remain uncorrected
nearby_distinctions: Modifies the review conclusion due to accounting framework non-compliance rather than a lack of available evidence.

descriptors.definition: Scope limitations typically prevent completion of the review, requiring written communication of reasons to management and governance. If management imposes a scope limitation precluding completion, the auditor disclaims a conclusion or considers withdrawal.
inclusion: Written communication of incomplete reviews
Issuing disclaimers when required by regulation
exclusion: Accepting engagements with known unremovable management-imposed scope restrictions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from accounting framework departures by addressing unperformed procedures and restricted evidence access rather than erroneous calculations.

descriptors.definition: When material uncertainties regarding going concern come to attention and are adequately disclosed, the auditor adds an emphasis of matter paragraph to the review report. Inadequate disclosure requires a qualified or adverse conclusion.
inclusion: Adding emphasis of matter paragraphs for disclosed uncertainties
Expressing qualified conclusions for inadequate disclosures
exclusion: Ignoring continuing operational viability doubts during interim evaluations
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on reporting operational viability disclosures via specific emphasis paragraphs or modified conclusions during interim periods.

descriptors.definition: The auditor addresses situations where interim financial information references a review but lacks the proper review report, considering legal advice or resignation. Furthermore, when interim statements are condensed, the auditor evaluates whether users require explicit references to the latest audited financial statements to prevent misleading disclosures.
inclusion: Management agreement to include review reports alongside documents mentioning reviews
Action plans when modified review reports are omitted by management
Assessment of the necessity of referencing latest audited financial statements
exclusion: Full annual financial statement audits
Preparation of management discussion and analysis reports
nearby_distinctions: Differs from complete annual financial statement reporting by focusing on condensed updates presuming user access to prior audited figures.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must assemble review documentation that is both sufficient and appropriate to support the review conclusion. This documentation serves as evidence that the review engagement was executed in compliance with relevant standards and regulatory mandates.
inclusion: Working papers supporting the review conclusion
Evidence of compliance with SRE and regulatory provisions
exclusion: Audit working papers for annual statutory audits governed by completely different standards without context adaptation
Management prepared financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the financial results themselves by representing the auditor working records and evidence file rather than the published statement.
source_ambiguities: Text contains integrated case scenarios and test your understanding questions trailing off or overlapping without complete rule statements for specific scenarios.

descriptors.definition: Prospective financial information comprises future-oriented statements prepared by entities to evaluate loan and equity proposals. Practitioners perform attest functions under applicable assurance standards to examine these forward-looking statements.
inclusion: Projected cash flow statements
Profit forecast statements
exclusion: Historical financial information
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from historical financial audits by focusing on future events and expected actions rather than past transactions.

descriptors.definition: Standards on assurance engagements regulate professional responsibilities for examinations concerning non-historical matters such as prospective financial information or internal controls. These engagements deliver a moderate level of assurance to stakeholders.
inclusion: Examinations of prospective financial information
Assurance reports on internal controls
exclusion: Audits of historical financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Provides a moderate level of assurance, differing from the reasonable assurance typically associated with historical audits.

descriptors.definition: Forecasts are prospective financial statements built on best-estimate assumptions reflecting anticipated future events and actions. Projections instead utilize hypothetical assumptions or mixtures of both best-estimate and hypothetical conditions for start-up or major operational shifts.
inclusion: Best-estimate assumptions for anticipated conditions
Hypothetical assumptions for start-up or major change scenarios
exclusion: Historical financial information reports
nearby_distinctions: Forecasts rely on expected operational conditions, whereas projections rely on speculative or imagined hypothetical conditions.

descriptors.definition: SAE 3400 governs engagements to examine and report on prospective financial information including evaluation procedures for best-estimate and hypothetical assumptions. It does not apply to prospective financial information expressed strictly in general or narrative terms.
inclusion: Examinations of structured prospective financial information
exclusion: Prospective information expressed in general narrative terms like management discussion and analysis
nearby_distinctions: Excludes narrative management reports from its formal application scope.

descriptors.definition: Because prospective financial information involves future-oriented, speculative evidence, an auditor cannot express an opinion on whether the projected results will actually be achieved. Management remains entirely responsible for the preparation, presentation, and underlying assumptions.
inclusion: Evaluation of underlying assumptions
Review of profit and financial forecasts
exclusion: Vouching for the absolute accuracy of forecasts
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between reviewing the reasonableness of underlying assumptions and guaranteeing actual performance outcomes.

descriptors.definition: Management holds the sole responsibility for preparing and presenting prospective financial information, disclosures, and underlying assumptions. Chartered accountants may participate or review these forecasts provided they do not vouch for absolute accuracy.
inclusion: Identification and disclosure of prospective financial information
Explanation of forecast bases
exclusion: Vouching for the realization of estimated future earnings
nearby_distinctions: Separates the management's primary creation duty from the practitioner's objective review and reporting role.

descriptors.definition: The examining auditor must gather sufficient evidence to determine whether best-estimate assumptions are reasonable and hypothetical assumptions fit the engagement purpose. Furthermore, the auditor verifies correct preparation, appropriate accounting principles, consistent presentation, and adequate disclosure.
inclusion: Testing preparation methodology
Verifying assumption consistency
exclusion: Assurance on actual future target realization
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on testing the reasonableness of underlying inputs rather than certifying factual operational outcomes.

descriptors.definition: Before accepting a prospective information engagement, the auditor evaluates the intended use, distribution limits, assumption types, and reporting period. The auditor must decline or withdraw if assumptions are unrealistic or the information is inappropriate.
inclusion: Evaluating intended use and distribution scope
Assessing justification of historical reliance
exclusion: Acceptance of engagements with clearly unrealistic assumptions
nearby_distinctions: Serves as a preliminary filter before engagement commitments are finalized.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must evaluate the reliability of historical financial data, clarify engagement terms through engagement letters, and check assumption viability. Clear boundaries must be established regarding general versus limited distribution of the reports.
inclusion: Agreement on terms via engagement letters
Assessment of historical data reliance
exclusion: Unvetted third-party reliance without verification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard acceptance reviews from formal fieldwork execution.

descriptors.definition: Auditors assess the source and reliability of evidence supporting best-estimate assumptions while checking that hypothetical assumptions account for all significant implications. Procedures consider business stability, management competence, and previous engagement knowledge.
inclusion: Assessment of evidence from budgets and debt agreements
Verification of capacity limits under hypothetical growth
exclusion: Acceptance of inconsistent hypothetical scenarios
nearby_distinctions: Requires checking operational ripple effects, such as capacity investments, when applying hypothetical growth scenarios.

descriptors.definition: The auditor evaluates whether prospective presentations are informative, clear, and unmisleading, with properly disclosed accounting policies and assumptions. Clear distinctions must be drawn between best-estimate and hypothetical components along with associated uncertainties.
inclusion: Verification of adequate assumption notes
Evaluation of uncertainty sensitivity disclosures
exclusion: Misleading or biased range selections
nearby_distinctions: Separates disclosure compliance from underlying calculation verification.

descriptors.definition: The examination report must contain a title, addressee, prospective information identification, management responsibility statements, and negative assurance on the assumptions. It must also disclose preparation dates, range estimation bases, and accounting policy changes.
inclusion: Statements of negative assurance
Disclosure of preparation dates and range criteria
exclusion: Unqualified positive opinion on future target achievement
nearby_distinctions: Employs negative assurance regarding assumption adequacy rather than absolute positive opinions on future events.

descriptors.definition: The process of retaining crucial evidence to substantiate the examination report of prospective financial information in alignment with specific standards. It confirms that variances between actual outcomes and forecasts are expected due to changing events and hypothetical assumptions.
inclusion: Recording evidence supporting the examination report
Documentation demonstrating execution in accordance with relevant standards
exclusion: Using prospective financial information for purposes outside intended uses without caution
nearby_distinctions: Differs from historical financial statement documentation by incorporating forward-looking assumptions and management actions.

descriptors.definition: An assurance standard governing professional engagements to report on controls at a third-party service organization that affect user entities' internal controls over financial reporting. It assists user auditors in obtaining appropriate evidence regarding outsourced functions and relevant compliance objectives.
inclusion: Assurance reports for user entities and their auditors
Evaluation of controls relevant to financial reporting at a service organization
exclusion: Engagements reporting exclusively on whether controls operated as described without design assessment
Controls unrelated to financial reporting such as production or quality control
nearby_distinctions: Complements SA 402 by providing direct assurance reports on service organization controls capable of satisfying user auditor evidence requirements.

descriptors.definition: The standard applies strictly when a service organization is responsible for making assertions regarding the suitable design of controls relevant to financial reporting. It excludes engagements that solely test operational descriptions or evaluate controls unrelated to financial reporting.
inclusion: Controls affecting user entity financial reporting assertions
Aspects of information systems and internal control components maintained by the service organization
exclusion: Engagements reporting only on whether controls operated as described
Controls affecting production or operational quality control exclusively
nearby_distinctions: Differentiated from general internal control reviews by its specific limitation to third-party services impacting user financial statements.

descriptors.definition: The service auditor aims to acquire reasonable assurance regarding whether the system description fairly presents the implemented design and whether controls were suitably designed throughout a specified period. Additionally, it encompasses reporting findings on whether operational controls achieved stated control objectives.
inclusion: Evaluating fair presentation of system descriptions
Assessing design suitability and operating effectiveness of controls
exclusion: Providing opinions on operational areas outside financial reporting internal controls
nearby_distinctions: Type 1 focuses on design at a specific date, whereas Type 2 extends to operating effectiveness over a specified period.

descriptors.definition: A Type 1 report evaluates a service organization's system description and the suitability of design of its controls as of a specified date. Conversely, a Type 2 report includes an assessment of the operating effectiveness of those controls throughout a specified period alongside testing descriptions and results.
inclusion: Service organization written assertions
Service auditor assurance report detailing test results for Type 2
exclusion: Unverified service descriptions lacking management assertions
nearby_distinctions: Type 1 covers design at a point in time, while Type 2 covers both design and operational performance across a duration.

descriptors.definition: The procedural steps for executing a service organization assurance engagement require complying with ethical requirements, managing governance communications, and verifying professional competence. Furthermore, the practitioner must assess the suitability of criteria, determine materiality, and obtain systemic understanding.
inclusion: Evaluating engagement acceptance criteria
Assessing control criteria suitability and determining materiality
exclusion: Proceeding with engagements where scope limitations undermine utility for user entities
nearby_distinctions: Establishes a structured chronological progression from initial ethical compliance to systemic understanding and evidence gathering.

descriptors.definition: The formal documentation and communication framework detailing the service auditor's assurance opinion, basic elements, and management representations. It explicitly identifies unverified parts, complementary user controls, and subservice organization activities.
inclusion: Basic elements including title and addressee
Disclosures on non-compliance, fraud, and control design deficiencies
exclusion: Distribution to unintended external users outside user entities and their auditors
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard financial statement audit reports by incorporating specific service organization system descriptions and complementary control declarations.

descriptors.definition: The requirement for the service auditor to record engagement procedures, evidence obtained, and significant judgments to enable an experienced practitioner to understand the engagement. If evidence is insufficient or controls are deficient, the auditor must modify the assurance report opinion accordingly.
inclusion: Records of nature, timing, and extent of procedures
Clear descriptions of reasons for opinion modifications
exclusion: Omitting rationale behind significant professional judgments made during the engagement
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on service auditor working papers that validate system design and operational effectiveness findings.

descriptors.definition: A standard addressing reasonable assurance engagements where a practitioner reports on a responsible party's compilation of pro forma financial information in a prospectus. It illustrates the impact of an event or transaction on unadjusted financial data as if it occurred earlier.
inclusion: Reporting required by securities laws or stock exchange regulations
Illustrating transaction impacts on financial positions via pro forma adjustments
exclusion: Representing actual historical financial position, performance, or cash flows
nearby_distinctions: Differs from prospective financial information by illustrating hypothetical past impacts on existing figures rather than predicting future performance.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner aims to obtain reasonable assurance regarding whether the responsible party compiled pro forma financial information based on applicable criteria. Subsequently, the practitioner issues an appropriate report matching their investigative findings.
inclusion: Obtaining assurance on compilation accuracy
Reporting in accordance with findings
exclusion: Compiling the pro forma financial information directly on behalf of the entity
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on evaluating compilation processes rather than preparing the underlying financial models.

descriptors.definition: The process where the responsible party gathers, classifies, and summarizes financial data to showcase the simulated impact of significant events. It involves extracting unadjusted figures, making relevant adjustments, and presenting accompanying disclosures.
inclusion: Extracting data from unadjusted financial sources
Applying specific pro forma adjustments and disclosures
exclusion: Independent preparation of financial statements by the reviewing practitioner
nearby_distinctions: A preparatory function performed entirely by management or the responsible party rather than the external assurance practitioner.

descriptors.definition: The practitioner holds no obligation to compile pro forma information, as compilation rests exclusively with the responsible party. The practitioner's sole duty is to execute a reasonable assurance engagement evaluating whether compilation followed applicable criteria.
inclusion: Assessing whether applicable criteria provide a reasonable presentation basis
Performing procedures to report on compilation integrity
exclusion: Directly compiling or formulating the entity's pro forma financial data
nearby_distinctions: Separates management's duty to compile data from the practitioner's independent verification and reporting duty.

descriptors.definition: Before accepting an engagement to report on pro forma financial information included in a prospectus, the practitioner must evaluate competence, verify criteria suitability, and assess potential reporting obstacles. These checks ensure the compiled information remains reliable and avoids misleading intended users.
inclusion: Evaluation of practitioner capabilities and competence
Review of suitability of criteria and prevention of misleading information
Assessment of modified audit opinions on source or acquiree financial information
exclusion: Actual execution of substantive testing procedures
Drafting of the final assurance report
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from engagement planning because acceptance occurs prior to formal contract finalization and resource allocation.
source_ambiguities: The source text truncates abruptly at the end regarding acquiree historical financial information.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners must maintain comprehensive working papers and documentation throughout assurance engagements governing pro forma and prospective financial data. Reports on prospective information require careful evaluation of underlying assumptions and management responsibilities.
inclusion: Working paper documentation for assurance engagements
Examination of evidence supporting prospective project assumptions
exclusion: Management preparation of company projections
Unverified casual drafting of assurance conclusions without evidence
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from pro forma compilation reporting because prospective information deals with future projections rather than historical adjustments.
source_ambiguities: The excerpt transitions abruptly into an integrated case scenario with draft report text containing an incomplete sentence ending.

descriptors.definition: Digital audit involves placing assurance on the effectiveness of information technology systems implemented within an organization. It reviews technology-related controls to identify operational gaps, mitigate risks, ensure regulatory compliance, and build stakeholder trust.
inclusion: Assessing the effectiveness of IT systems
Reviewing technology controls
Identifying gaps and risks
exclusion: Traditional manual audits without technology integration
Pure financial balance sheet verification without IT scope
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general internal controls evaluation by specifically focusing on underlying digital infrastructure and automated processes.

descriptors.definition: Digital audit evaluates organizational IT effectiveness to uncover risks and ensure regulatory adherence. It empowers continuous operational improvement through robust technological security positions.
inclusion: Evaluating IT system effectiveness
Ensuring compliance through technology
exclusion: Non-digital procedural reviews
nearby_distinctions: Focuses directly on foundational digital controls rather than end-user output verification.

descriptors.definition: Key attributes include encouraging technological adoption, improving audit opinion quality, and enabling autonomous 24x7 real-time transactions. It standardizes processes and supports forward-looking digital strategies like artificial intelligence and analytics.
inclusion: Autonomous process orchestration
Standardized risk mitigation controls
Enhanced analytics capability
exclusion: Manual standalone audit methods
Static historical transaction testing
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes the intrinsic operational characteristics and forward-looking capabilities rather than mere procedural steps.

descriptors.definition: Digital audits enhance effectiveness by automating routine tasks, evaluating massive data volumes quickly, and reducing audit costs. They improve analytics and risk assessment, allowing efforts to target high-risk material misstatement sites.
inclusion: Automated routine reconciliations
High-volume transaction evaluation
Targeted risk-based testing
exclusion: Labor-intensive manual sampling
Traditional subjective error evaluations
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on measurable efficiency gains and risk-targeting benefits compared to traditional audits.

descriptors.definition: Organizations must align automation with broad digitalization strategies, prioritize change management, and standardize processes prior to automation. Proper governance and data security must be maintained within the risk framework to address IT environment changes.
inclusion: Evaluating IT environment changes
Addressing new technology revenue streams
Maintaining data governance
exclusion: Treating automation as an isolated standalone solution
Automating unstandardized flawed processes
nearby_distinctions: Concentrates on implementation obstacles and governance risks rather than core advantages.

descriptors.definition: Auditing digitally deploys technology advancements such as Robotic Process Automation, artificial intelligence, and sampling tools to execute effective audits. It involves leveraging specialized software and digital upskilling to test controls and analyze data accurately.
inclusion: Using software bots for control reperformance
Deploying data analytics for fraud identification
Executing automated sampling
exclusion: Purely manual vouching and tracing
Non-technical audit procedures
nearby_distinctions: Refers to how the auditor uses technology to conduct the audit, whereas digital audit evaluates the client's IT systems.

descriptors.definition: Auditing digitally integrates modern technology tools into audit execution to enhance precision and coverage. Auditors apply automated routines, such as bots pulling vendor change logs, to test management controls efficiently.
inclusion: Automated vendor master review testing
Digital sampling based on materiality
Specialized software integration
exclusion: Manual inspection of physical paper logs
Ad-hoc unstructured verification
nearby_distinctions: Centers on auditor-side tool deployment for engagement delivery rather than evaluating client internal IT systems.

descriptors.definition: Key benefits include improved audit quality via full population reviews, decreased human dependency, and enhanced transparency through digital audit trails. Automation and dashboards streamline testing, improve efficiency, and refine risk assessment.
inclusion: Reviewing full transaction populations
Tracing changes via ERP audit trails
Visualizing data via dashboards
exclusion: Restricted sample-based manual testing
Opaque ledger processing
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on audit execution benefits like full population testing and transparency rather than general auditee IT controls.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must strategically evaluate technology integration challenges, select appropriate automation tools, and upskill engagement teams. Automated solutions range from macros and business process automation to robotic and intelligent process automation.
inclusion: Assessing return on technology investment
Continuous staff training
Selecting rule-based or AI automation tools
exclusion: Ignoring personnel training requirements
Adopting tools without integration planning
nearby_distinctions: Addresses strategic planning and tool calibration for audit teams rather than client-side operational risks.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must understand how an entity relies on IT and how its infrastructure supports business transactions to identify risks. This assessment covers applications, operating systems, databases, network architecture, and governance structures.
inclusion: Documenting application and operating system details
Assessing IT integration and service organizations
Identifying automated process flows
exclusion: Ignoring underlying database structures
Treating IT as an isolated back-office function
nearby_distinctions: Directly mandated for risk identification under auditing standards, differing from general tech adoption.

descriptors.definition: Auditors focus on transaction flows, significant systems identification, and the mix of manual versus automated controls. They must also recognize emerging technologies like blockchain, robotics, and artificial intelligence to evaluate potential reporting risks.
inclusion: Tracking transaction flow changes
Identifying manual and automated control elements
Evaluating emerging technologies like blockchain or AI
exclusion: Reviewing financial outputs without tracking system data flow
Assuming zero impact from emerging technologies
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on specific structural components like transaction flows and control mixes rather than high-level IT architecture overview.

descriptors.definition: IT usage introduces risks such as unauthorized data access, segregation of duty breakdowns by IT personnel, and inappropriate manual interventions. Additional risks include data corruption, system downtime, cybersecurity breaches, and system integration failures.
inclusion: Identifying master file unauthorized changes
Evaluating cybersecurity and data loss risks
Assessing multi-system integration failures
exclusion: Traditional physical inventory miscounts
Manual arithmetic errors unrelated to systems
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on technology-driven vulnerabilities rather than standard business operational risks.

descriptors.definition: Auditors identify information technology risks by evaluating the nature of applications, cybersecurity protocols, and management reliance on automated controls. Higher volumes of automated controls and shared common databases increase exposure to vulnerabilities like data loss, downtime, and unauthorized access.
inclusion: Evaluating the volume and complexity of automated controls
Assessing risks related to system integration and compatibility
Identifying potential cyber threats and downtime causes
exclusion: Manual business process errors unrelated to IT systems
General economic industry risk factors
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general risk assessment because it focuses specifically on vulnerabilities arising from hardware, software, and network dependencies.

descriptors.definition: Risks arising from information technology include unauthorized data changes, segregation of duties breakdowns, data corruption, system downtime, and compatibility issues across platforms. These hazards threaten the reliability of transaction processing, data integrity, and compliance with regulatory frameworks.
inclusion: Unauthorized access or alterations to data and master files
System integration and compatibility failures
Regulatory compliance exposure due to technological changes
exclusion: Purely manual accounting calculation errors without IT involvement
Physical asset theft outside of data and IT environments
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on operational and compliance failures resulting directly from technology adoption rather than general business strategy risks.

descriptors.definition: IT dependencies represent the reliance of an entity on information technology to initiate, process, and report transactions for financial statements. Recognizing these dependencies through automated controls, reports, calculations, security, and interfaces helps auditors establish an efficient audit strategy.
inclusion: Automated business rule enforcement controls
System-generated reports used in audit testing
Automated accounting calculations and security restrictions
exclusion: Completely manual calculations performed entirely without system tools
Standalone physical security protocols unrelated to data systems
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general IT risks because it identifies specific system touchpoints where financial data is processed and relied upon for auditing.

descriptors.definition: Cyber risks involve malicious attempts to gain unauthorized access to computing networks with the intent to damage, steal, or disrupt data assets. Assessing these risks requires evaluating security objectives across application access, program changes, and data center operations.
inclusion: Evaluation of application access controls and user removal procedures
Review of program change management and segregation of duties
Assessment of data backup, recovery, and network operations
exclusion: Standard hardware wear-and-tear equipment failures
Internal human error unrelated to external attacks or security breaches
nearby_distinctions: Focuses explicitly on malicious digital intrusion and protective security architectures rather than general operational system downtime.

descriptors.definition: Cyber risk refers to potential harm or unauthorized access to computing systems and networks intended to compromise data integrity, confidentiality, or availability. Organizations must protect assets and maintain structured objectives regarding access security, program changes, and network operations.
inclusion: Unauthorized access attempts and malicious software threats
Security objectives governing user authentication and authorization
Data backup and operational continuity controls
exclusion: Lawful system maintenance performed by authorized personnel
Planned system downtime for scheduled hardware upgrades
nearby_distinctions: Presents the core definition and security objectives of cyber threats as opposed to the audit methodology steps for evaluating them.

descriptors.definition: The lifecycle of cyber risk management involves assessing common threat exposures, analyzing potential financial and operational impacts, and executing strategic mitigations. Organizations evaluate vulnerabilities like ransomware and phishing to understand regulatory, reputational, and financial consequences.
inclusion: Stage one assessment of common threats like phishing and insider actions
Stage two evaluation of impacts including regulatory costs and data loss
Stage three strategic management and alignment of cybersecurity programs
exclusion: Routine financial budgeting processes unrelated to security threats
General tax compliance reviews
nearby_distinctions: Frames cyber risk through a phased lifecycle approach from initial threat identification to impact analysis and strategic remediation.

descriptors.definition: A cybersecurity framework encompasses management strategies for identifying risks, protecting electronic assets, and responding to adverse security events. Entities must maintain information asset inventories, prioritize digital asset protection, and align programs with recognized security guidelines.
inclusion: Periodic risk assessments covering IT system failures and data access
Classification and prioritization of information assets
Governance structures establishing cybersecurity roles and responsibilities
exclusion: Physical inventory counts of tangible factory machinery without digital components
Manual financial statement preparation processes
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes the overarching governance and management framework for defending electronic assets rather than specific transaction-level software controls.

descriptors.definition: Entities must implement internal controls to safeguard against cyber schemes that target vendor modifications, electronic fund transfers, and patch management vulnerabilities. Robust verification protocols prevent fraudulent disbursements and the exploitation of unpatched system security flaws.
inclusion: Controls around vendor setup and master data changes
Authentication protocols for electronic funds and wire transfers
Patch management controls to address known security vulnerabilities
exclusion: Standard physical cash count procedures at retail store registers
Non-electronic paper voucher approvals
nearby_distinctions: Centers specifically on high-risk transaction vectors and operational controls vulnerable to targeted cyber scams rather than general network firewalls.

descriptors.definition: A remote or virtual audit utilizes electronic and online means to conduct audit procedures, review documentation, and interact with auditees. Proper planning, secure document sharing platforms, and encrypted connections like virtual private networks are essential to maintain data confidentiality and evidence reliability.
inclusion: Planning audit timelines and video conferencing methods
Using encrypted document sharing platforms with restricted access
Employing virtual private networks when accessing client IT systems
exclusion: Traditional physical onsite audit walkthroughs and inspections
Unsecured local file transfers without encryption
