allocating tax credit to deductees or alternate assessable persons based on reporting rules
exclusion: employer-paid tax on non-monetary perquisites and section 194N deductions from being deemed income received
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from primary deduction mechanics by establishing post-deduction tax accounting, income grossing rules, and credit attribution frameworks.

descriptors.definition: All taxes deducted under statutory provisions and eligible foreign tax deductions are treated as income received when computing an assessee's total income. Specific statutory outflows, such as non-monetary perquisite taxes paid by employers and certain cash withdrawal deductions, are excluded from this income-inclusion rule.
inclusion: all sums deducted under Chapter XVII TDS provisions
eligible foreign income tax deductions allowed as credit
exclusion: employer-paid tax on non-monetary perquisites
tax deducted under section 194N on cash withdrawals
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from gross cash receipts by legally mandating the addition of withheld tax amounts back into the taxpayer's computed income base.

descriptors.definition: Tax deducted at source and paid to the Central Government is treated as tax payment on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made or the owner of the relevant asset. Rule 37BA dictates that credit is given to the actual deductee or an alternate assessable person based on deductor information, aligned with the assessment year of the income.
inclusion: Credit given to the deductee based on deductor reporting
Proportional credit across multiple years if income is assessable across years
exclusion: Direct payment of tax without statutory deduction mechanism
Credit given without matching deductor information
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 200 duty to deposit, focusing instead on granting tax credit to the income earner.

descriptors.definition: Persons responsible for tax deduction must deposit the deducted sums to the Central Government's credit within prescribed timelines. They are also obligated to prepare, verify, and deliver prescribed periodic statements and correction statements for rectification.
inclusion: Remitting deducted tax within time
Filing periodic statements and correction statements
exclusion: Direct tax collection by the assessing officer without deductor intermediary
Tax collection at source mechanisms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Section 199 credit mechanisms, as this focuses on the active compliance burden of the deductor rather than the taxpayer's credit.

descriptors.definition: Failing to deduct or pay tax makes a person a deemed assessee-in-default, attracting mandatory simple interest liabilities. However, an exception applies if the payee has already reported the income, paid the tax, and an accountant's certificate is furnished.
inclusion: Interest at 1 percent per month for failure to deduct
Interest at 1.5 percent per month from deduction to payment date
exclusion: Standard tax remittance within statutory due dates
Penalties charged without proper opportunity of being heard
nearby_distinctions: Differs from routine tax compliance by imposing punitive default status and compounding interest rates for non-compliance.

descriptors.definition: Tax deduction at source represents solely one method available for recovering tax obligations. The Assessing Officer retains the statutory authority to deploy any alternative recovery mechanisms prescribed by law.
inclusion: Utilization of other recovery modes alongside TDS
exclusion: Exclusive reliance on withholding tax mechanisms for tax recovery
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with the bar against direct demand by ensuring recovery powers remain broad and unrestricted by the mere existence of TDS.

descriptors.definition: Deductors must issue a formal certificate specifying the deducted amount, rate, and other particulars to the deductee. Employers paying tax on non-monetary perquisites must similarly furnish a certificate of tax paid within prescribed periods.
inclusion: Issuance of certificates containing deduction rates and amounts
Adherence to prescribed timelines and forms
exclusion: Filing quarterly statements under Section 200(3)
Allotment of Tax Deduction Account Number
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from statements filed with authorities, as this certificate is provided directly to the payee/deductee.

descriptors.definition: Persons responsible for deducting or collecting tax must apply for a unique tax deduction and collection account number. This TAN must be compulsorily quoted across all statutory challans, certificates, statements, and returns.
inclusion: Mandatory quoting of TAN in challans and returns
Penalties for failure to obtain or willful false quoting of TAN
exclusion: Notified cases exempted by the Central Government
General permanent account numbers used by assesses
nearby_distinctions: Differs from individual PAN requirements, focusing specifically on the institutional identifier for entities withholding or collecting tax.

descriptors.definition: The statute explicitly defines the specific individuals or entities accountable for withholding tax depending on the nature of payment. This includes employers, corporate principals, authorized remittance agents, and government drawing officers.
inclusion: Designation of company principals for corporate payments
Designation of government drawing and disbursing officers
exclusion: General third-party commercial debtors lacking statutory withholding obligations
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from the general deductee concept, this isolates the legal entity legally mandated to execute the deduction.

descriptors.definition: Assessees cannot be directly demanded to pay tax themselves to the extent that tax has already been legally deductible at source from their income. This protects taxpayers from direct tax liabilities where the deductor failed to remit withheld amounts.
inclusion: Immunity from direct tax payment demands up to the deductible amount
exclusion: Income portions explicitly excluded from statutory tax deduction rules
nearby_distinctions: Differs from recovery provisions by restricting the revenue authority from pursuing the payee for tax that was supposed to be withheld by the payer.

descriptors.definition: Banking companies, co-operative societies, and specific housing finance public companies must furnish prescribed statements for resident interest payments not exceeding designated thresholds without tax deduction. Non-compliance invites daily monetary penalties under the statute.
inclusion: Reporting sub-threshold interest payments to residents
Filing correction statements for rectifying reporting mistakes
exclusion: Payments subject to full tax deduction at source requirements
Payments exceeding statutory monetary limits
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard TDS return filing because it specifically tracks exempt or sub-threshold payments made without withholding.

descriptors.definition: Deductees must mandatorily provide their permanent account number to the deductor, failing which tax must be withheld at significantly higher statutory rates. Invalid or mismatched PAN submissions are legally treated as non-furnishing of PAN.
inclusion: Tax deduction at higher rates including 20 percent defaults
Invalidation of fake or mismatched PAN numbers
exclusion: Exempted non-resident payments meeting specific conditions under rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular tax deduction rates by overriding normal thresholds with penal withholding rates for missing identifiers.

descriptors.definition: Tax must be deducted at higher rates for specified persons who failed to file income tax returns for the immediately preceding previous year and have aggregate withheld taxes exceeding statutory monetary limits. Specified non-residents without permanent establishments or notified entities are excluded.
inclusion: Double rate withholding for non-filers meeting previous year TDS/TCS thresholds
Exclusion of non-residents without Indian permanent establishments
exclusion: Standard deductions under exempted sections like salary or lottery winnings
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 206AA because it penalizes historical tax return non-filing rather than the failure to provide a permanent account number.

descriptors.definition: Sellers of specified goods and grantors of specific business leases or licenses are legally mandated to collect tax at source from buyers or licensees at prescribed percentages. Exemptions apply when resident buyers provide formal declarations that goods are intended for manufacturing or power generation rather than trading.
inclusion: Tax collection on specified forest produce, scrap, and minerals
Tax collection on lease or license of parking lots and mines
exclusion: Mining and quarrying of mineral oil
Transactions covered by manufacturing declarations submitted by resident buyers
nearby_distinctions: Differs from tax deduction at source (TDS) as it is collected directly by sellers or licensors from buyers or lessees during commercial sales or transfers.

descriptors.definition: Tax deduction and collection statements are processed centrally to rectify arithmetical errors or incorrect claims apparent from the data. The system computes applicable interest and late fees under section 234E to generate a final intimation specifying the net payable sum or refundable amount.
inclusion: Rectification of arithmetical errors in TDS/TCS statements
Adjustment of inconsistent entries or incorrect deduction rates
Computation and levy of late filing fees under section 234E
exclusion: Regular field scrutiny assessments
Detailed tax recovery proceedings
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from regular return processing under section 143(1) as it specifically addresses statements submitted by tax deductors and collectors rather than taxpayer income returns.

descriptors.definition: Assessees must discharge their tax liability on current income progressively during the financial year if the total advance tax payable meets the statutory threshold. Resident senior citizens with passive income and no business profits are exempt from this requirement.
inclusion: Tax payment obligations on current financial year income
Exemptions for resident individuals aged 60 or above without business income
exclusion: Assessees whose computed advance tax liability falls below the statutory threshold of 10000 rupees
nearby_distinctions: Differs from self-assessment tax or tax deducted at source by enforcing mandatory installment payments ahead of the assessment year based on estimated current earnings.

descriptors.definition: An obligation to pay advance tax is triggered whenever the computed tax liability reaches or exceeds ten thousand rupees for the financial year. Resident individuals aged sixty or older without business or professional income are exempted from this payment rule.
inclusion: Mandatory advance tax obligations for liabilities exceeding the statutory threshold
Relief provisions for elderly resident individuals with rental or interest incomes
exclusion: Taxpayers whose total advance tax liability remains under ten thousand rupees
Non-residents meeting age criteria
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general tax remittance because liability is conditioned specifically on crossing a minimum financial threshold and the absence of speculative business revenue for senior exemptions.

descriptors.definition: Assessees independently calculate advance tax on estimated current income using prevailing financial year rates, subject to modification via official administrative orders. The computed tax must account for tax deductible or collectible at source while ignoring un-deducted amounts.
inclusion: Self-computation of advance tax based on estimated current earnings
Modification of computation basis using higher historical regular assessments or returned incomes
Reduction for actual tax deducted or collected at source
exclusion: Reduction for tax deductible or collectible amounts that were not actually subjected to deduction or collection
nearby_distinctions: Differs from post-year-end tax calculations by relying strictly on ongoing estimations and official prior-year baselines rather than finalized annual financial statements.

descriptors.definition: Advance tax is payable across specified quarterly installment dates throughout the financial year with designated cumulative percentage thresholds. Eligible presumptive business and professional assessees fulfill this obligation through a single installment due by the final installment date.
inclusion: Standard quarterly installment schedules for corporate and non-corporate entities
Single installment relaxation for eligible presumptive income taxpayers
Credit assignment provisions for paid advance tax amounts
exclusion: Late payments treated as standard tax arrears without default status designation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard multi-stage corporate and non-corporate schedules from the simplified single-installment timeline granted to eligible presumptive business and professional taxpayers.

descriptors.definition: Payments made towards advance tax, excluding any associated interest or penalties, are officially recognized as tax payments for the relevant previous year. The corresponding tax credit is formally granted during the regular assessment procedure.
inclusion: Crediting recovered or voluntarily paid advance tax sums against final tax liabilities
Allocation of payments exclusively to income tax components
exclusion: Inclusion of interest payments or monetary penalties within the creditable tax pool
nearby_distinctions: Separates pure advance tax principal payments from penal or interest charges, ensuring only principal tax remittances qualify for assessment-stage tax credits.

descriptors.definition: Statutory interest is levied at specified monthly rates for procedural defaults such as delayed return filings or short-payments of advance tax. The calculation period and underlying base amount depend on whether determinations occur via summary processing or regular assessments.
inclusion: Interest charges for belated or omitted income tax return submissions
Penal interest frameworks for advance tax shortfalls and deferments
exclusion: Discretionary waiver of statutory interest outside explicit legislative provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes return-filing delay interest from advance tax default interest by targeting compliance failures at different stages of the annual tax cycle.

descriptors.definition: Simple interest is charged when an assessee fails to submit an income tax return by the statutory due date or omits filing entirely. The charge accrues monthly from the day following the due date until the actual filing date or best-judgment completion.
inclusion: Monthly interest computations for late or un-furnished tax returns
Reductions for advance interest payments made under section 140A
exclusion: Inclusion of additional income tax components specified under sections 140B or 143 within the interest calculation base
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on return submission timelines rather than installment payment milestones or tax deferment discrepancies.

descriptors.definition: Interest is attracted when an advance tax liable assessee fails to pay or pays less than ninety percent of the assessed tax. The charge applies at fixed monthly rates starting from the beginning of the subsequent financial year until the assessment determination date.
inclusion: Interest assessments when total advance tax paid drops below the ninety percent threshold
Adjustments for self-assessment tax payments made prior to final determination
exclusion: Inclusion of additional taxes under section 140B within the assessed tax base
nearby_distinctions: Differs from deferment interest by penalizing the aggregate annual shortfall of advance tax rather than intra-year installment timing mismatches.

descriptors.definition: Assessees who pay lesser advance tax than the specified cumulative percentages by designated quarterly dates face simple interest penalties on the shortfall. Presumptive business and professional income earners follow a modified single-installment threshold arrangement.
inclusion: Quarterly shortfall computations for corporate and non-corporate entities
Safégard tolerances for early installment payments
Single-date deferment assessments for presumptive income schemes
exclusion: Levy of interest where early installment shortfalls remain within permitted tolerance margins
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from total advance tax avoidance penalties by specifically targeting the phased under-payment across interim sub-periods of the financial year.

descriptors.definition: Late submission of tax deduction or collection statements incurs a mandatory daily fee capped at the total tax amount. Additional monetary penalties apply for missing statutory deadlines or providing incorrect statement information, with thresholds adjusted for extended delays.
inclusion: Daily statutory fees for delayed TDS and TCS statement filings
Monetized penalty ranges for un-furnished or incorrect statements
Conditional penalty waivers for compliance within specified grace periods
exclusion: Penalty impositions under section 271H when delayed statements are filed within the permitted one-year timeframe alongside due payments
nearby_distinctions: Separates administrative daily late-filing fees from substantive legal penalties, imposing both concurrently only when delays exceed extended statutory limits.

descriptors.definition: Demanded tax sums must be satisfied within thirty days of notice service, though administrative authorities can shorten or extend this duration. Failure to pay within the stipulated window triggers monthly interest liabilities that adjust dynamically based on subsequent appellate or rectification orders.
inclusion: Mandatory payment timelines following a notice of demand
Discretionary administrative extensions or installment permissions
Interest recalibrations resulting from appellate or rectification orders
exclusion: Unconditional extensions without official supervisory approval
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes general collection default mechanisms from advance tax shortfalls by tying enforcement to formal notices of demand and subsequent appellate revisions.

descriptors.definition: Amounts specified in a notice of demand must be paid within thirty days of service, though the Assessing Officer may extend time, permit installments, or shorten the period if revenue is endangered. Failure to pay within this period triggers simple interest liability for every month or part of a month of default.
inclusion: Demand payments within thirty days
Interest on unpaid dues
Reduction or increase of interest resulting from rectification or appellate orders
exclusion: Penalty levy mechanisms
Recovery proceedings through TRO
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 221 penalties as it deals strictly with statutory payment timelines and compounding interest rather than penal impositions for defaults.

descriptors.definition: When an assessee defaults in paying tax, advance tax, or interest, the Assessing Officer shall impose a monetary penalty after providing a reasonable opportunity of being heard, provided no good and sufficient reason is proven. Subsequent payment of the tax in arrears before penalty imposition does not absolve the assessee from this liability.
inclusion: Penalties for tax or advance tax default
Cancellation of penalty if the underlying tax demand is wholly reduced on appeal
exclusion: Basic interest computations for delayed tax payments under Section 220
nearby_distinctions: Unlike routine interest charged automatically under Section 220, Section 221 imposes a punitive charge requiring a hearing and subjective evaluation of good and sufficient reasons.

descriptors.definition: When an assessee is in default, the Tax Recovery Officer draws up a signed statement of arrears and initiates recovery through specific statutory modes such as property attachment and sale, arrest, or appointment of a receiver. Transferred properties to spouses or minor children for inadequate consideration are legally included in the assessee's recoverable pool.
inclusion: Movable and immovable property attachments
Arrest and detention
Inclusion of assets transferred to close relatives without adequate consideration
exclusion: Initial demand notices or direct Assessing Officer garnishments without certificates
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Section 220/221 because it represents an escalated administrative recovery stage executed specifically via a formal certificate drawn up by a designated recovery officer.

descriptors.definition: Recovery actions under Section 222 are handled by the Tax Recovery Officer within whose jurisdiction the assessee carries on business, resides, or owns property, with jurisdiction assigned by higher tax authorities. If full recovery cannot be achieved locally or if expedition is required, the certificate may be transferred to another TRO where the assessee holds property.
inclusion: Assignment of territorial and functional jurisdiction
Inter-jurisdictional transfer of recovery certificates
exclusion: Substantive rules governing asset attachment methods
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on geographical and administrative competence for executing recovery rather than the mechanics of the recovery modes themselves.

descriptors.definition: An assessee is barred from disputing the correctness of any recovery certificate drawn up by the Tax Recovery Officer on any ground. However, the Tax Recovery Officer holds the discretionary authority to cancel the certificate or amend clerical and arithmetical mistakes.
inclusion: Correction of formal errors in certificates
Discretionary cancellation of certificates by the TRO
exclusion: Assessee challenges on substantive tax liabilities during execution
nearby_distinctions: Unlike assessment orders which can be contested on merits in appeals, the certificate itself cannot be challenged by the assessee on substantive grounds.

descriptors.definition: The Tax Recovery Officer is authorized to grant time extensions for tax payments, which operates to stay recovery proceedings until that time expires. Additionally, if tax demands are reduced via appellate proceedings that remain subject to further challenge, recovery for the reduced portion must be stayed accordingly.
inclusion: Stays granted upon extension of payment time
Stays during pending further litigation on reduced appellate demands
Modification or cancellation of certificates upon final appellate outcomes
exclusion: Initial drawing of recovery certificates
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from Section 224 as it deals with halting or adjusting active recovery proceedings due to time grants or pending higher-level appeals rather than correcting intrinsic certificate errors.

descriptors.definition: Income-tax authorities and Tax Recovery Officers can recover tax arrears through alternative statutory channels, including garnishee notices on third parties holding money for the assessee, attachments of funds in court custody, or State Government channels. Objections on oath regarding third-party liabilities carry personal liability consequences if proven false.
inclusion: Third-party debt attachments
Recovery through court-held funds
State government recovery channels
exclusion: Standard movable and immovable property sales managed solely via Second Schedule certificates
nearby_distinctions: Provides supplemental direct intervention tools (such as freezing third-party debts) that operate alongside or independently of standard TRO certificate recovery methods.

descriptors.definition: Tax recovery can be executed across international borders via bilateral agreements where foreign tax authorities send certificates to the Central Board of Direct Taxes for local enforcement. Conversely, Indian tax authorities can forward domestic recovery certificates to the Board for execution against residents holding overseas assets in treaty-partner countries.
inclusion: Enforcement of foreign tax certificates in India
Transmission of Indian tax recovery certificates abroad
exclusion: Domestic-only recovery mechanisms lacking international treaty frameworks
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard domestic recovery under Sections 222–226 by establishing a cross-border cooperative recovery mechanism governed by international agreements.

descriptors.definition: Non-domiciled individuals visiting India for business, profession, or employment must furnish an employer undertaking guaranteeing tax payments before leaving the country. Persons domiciled in India must generally provide their Permanent Account Number or specific certificates at departure unless exempted.
inclusion: Undertakings for non-domiciled business visitors
Permanent Account Number disclosures for departing Indian domiciliaries
Exemptions for foreign tourists
exclusion: General domestic tax assessment procedures
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a pre-departure regulatory control measure rather than a post-assessment recovery mechanism for tax arrears.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government is empowered to notify schemes for faceless collection and recovery of tax to eliminate physical interfaces between authorities and assessees. This framework covers lower deduction certificates, default orders, interest waivers, and recovery certificate operations using dynamic jurisdiction.
inclusion: Faceless processing of lower deduction or collection certificates
Digital handling of installment extensions and penalty levies
Automated resource optimization and team-based assessments
exclusion: Traditional physical field enforcement operations not covered under the notified scheme
nearby_distinctions: Replaces traditional localized administrative touchpoints with an automated, virtual, team-based jurisdiction model across recovery and deduction functions.

descriptors.definition: Assessing Officers and the Government maintain the legal right to pursue alternative modes of recovery under any applicable laws or institute civil suits to collect tax arrears. These methods operate as concurrent remedies alongside specialized income-tax recovery provisions.
inclusion: Filing civil suits for tax recovery
Utilizing general legal mechanisms for recovering government debts
exclusion: Exclusive reliance on internal departmental certificates under Section 222
nearby_distinctions: Unlike internal departmental recovery steps like TRO certificates, this section enables formal civil litigation and general legal suits outside the direct machinery of the tax statute.

descriptors.definition: Assessees are entitled to claim tax refunds when total taxes paid exceed their properly chargeable liability for an assessment year. Such claims typically arise from excess tax deducted at source, advance tax overpayments, or appellate reductions of original tax assessments.
inclusion: Refund claims for excess tax payments
Claims filed by legal representatives for incapacitated or deceased assessees
Direct refund applications under Section 195 arrangements
exclusion: Tax liabilities matching or exceeding payments made
nearby_distinctions: Inverts recovery provisions by addressing the return of excess funds collected by the Government rather than the extraction of tax arrears from the assessee.

descriptors.definition: Statutory penalties and rigorous imprisonment are attracted when a person fails to deduct tax at source, collect tax at source, or remit such withheld amounts to the credit of the Central Government. These provisions apply equivalently whether the underlying consideration is monetary or delivered in kind under specific statutory provisions.
inclusion: Penalty equal to un-deducted tax under section 271C
Rigorous imprisonment from 3 months to 7 years with fine for failure to pay deducted tax under section 276B
Penalty equal to un-collected tax under section 271CA
Rigorous imprisonment from 3 months to 7 years with fine for failure to pay collected tax under section 276BB
Penalties for failure to pay or ensure payment when consideration is in kind under relevant provisos
exclusion: Prosecution under section 276B if payment is made to the credit of the Central Government on or before the prescribed statement filing time w.e.f. 1.10.2024
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between civil monetary penalties levied by the Joint Commissioner and criminal prosecution involving rigorous imprisonment.
Distinguishes between defaults relating to tax deduction at source versus tax collection at source.

descriptors.definition: The Income-tax Act establishes a hierarchical administrative machinery headed by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, followed by various classes of directors-general, chief commissioners, commissioners, and subordinate officers. The CBDT functions under the Ministry of Finance to exercise statutory control, supervise the department, and frame necessary rules for proper administration.
inclusion: Central Board of Direct Taxes
Directorate ranks
Commissioner ranks
Assessing Officers including ACIT, DCIT, and authorized ITOs
exclusion: Judicial courts outside the income-tax department hierarchy
Non-statutory bodies without administrative linkage
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from appellate dispute resolution panels and general civil courts by operating purely within the direct tax administrative machinery.

descriptors.definition: Income-tax authorities must exercise their statutory powers and perform assigned functions in accordance with the regulatory directions issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes. The CBDT distributes and regulates these administrative authorities based on criteria including territorial area, classes of persons, types of incomes, or specific cases.
inclusion: General or special orders assigning officer jurisdiction
Higher authorities exercising powers of lower authorities under board direction
Delegation of assessment functions to additional or joint commissioners
exclusion: Self-assigned jurisdiction by officers without specific board authorization or statutory backing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general administrative powers because it specifically governs the territorial and functional distribution of official authority across taxpayers and cases.

descriptors.definition: Specific income-tax authorities possess the same powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure when handling matters such as discovery, enforcing attendance, and compelling document production. These powers can be invoked for inquiry or investigation purposes even when no active proceeding is pending if tax concealment is suspected.
inclusion: Issuing commissions
Compelling production of books of account
Investigating suspected concealed income prior to formal proceedings
exclusion: Arbitrary extra-judicial actions unaligned with formal civil procedure principles
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general survey or search actions by strictly adopting judicial trial powers like examination on oath and discovery under civil procedural rules.

descriptors.definition: Specific income-tax authorities possess the same powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure when handling matters such as discovery, enforcing attendance, and compelling document production. These powers can be invoked for inquiry or investigation purposes even when no active proceeding is pending if tax concealment is suspected.
inclusion: Issuing commissions
Compelling production of books of account
Investigating suspected concealed income prior to formal proceedings
exclusion: Arbitrary extra-judicial actions unaligned with formal civil procedure principles
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general survey or search actions by strictly adopting judicial trial powers like examination on oath and discovery under civil procedural rules.

descriptors.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
exclusion: Non-residents unless specific conditions apply
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

descriptors.definition: Compulsory filing provisions mandate certain entities and individuals to submit a return of income on or before the due date regardless of income levels. This includes companies, firms, and residents holding foreign assets or signing authority, excluding certain beneficiaries whose income is included by the primary asset owner.
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Residents with foreign beneficial assets or signing powers
exclusion: Beneficiary whose asset income is already taxable in the hands of the beneficial owner
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from voluntary returns because statutory compliance is mandatory based on entity type or asset holding rather than income thresholds alone.

descriptors.definition: Interest under section 234A is levied when an assessee fails to furnish a return of income by the statutory due date. Simple interest at one percent per month applies to the net tax liability for the duration of the default period.
inclusion: Assessees filing returns after the due date
Assessees failing to furnish any return
exclusion: Assessees filing valid returns within the prescribed due date
nearby_distinctions: Calculated specifically on tax on total income reduced by advance tax and TDS, unlike late filing fees under section 234F.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government may exempt specific classes of taxpayers from filing a return of income to minimize compliance burdens. This includes non-corporate non-residents and foreign companies whose sole Indian income derives from specified International Financial Services Centre investment funds subject to tax deduction at source.
inclusion: Non-corporate non-residents with fund income in IFSC
Foreign companies with fund income in IFSC
exclusion: Taxpayers earning other Indian-sourced incomes outside the specified exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard filing requirements by granting total exemption from submitting returns under section 139(1) via executive notification.

descriptors.definition: A return of loss must be filed within the normal due dates to enable the carry forward and set-off of specified business, capital, or specific activity losses. Failure to file this return on time forfeits the right to carry forward those specific categories of losses.
inclusion: Business losses
Speculation losses
Capital losses
exclusion: House property losses and unabsorbed depreciation which can be carried forward even without timely filing
nearby_distinctions: Mandatory filing is strictly required for business and capital losses, unlike house property losses which tolerate delayed filings for carry forward purposes.

descriptors.definition: A belated return is filed by any person who missed the original due date, submitted prior to three months before the end of the assessment year or before assessment completion. Filing a belated return incurs interest, late fees, and restrictions on carrying forward certain losses or claiming specific deductions.
inclusion: Returns submitted after the section 139(1) due date within permitted statutory windows
exclusion: Returns filed after the expiry of the belated filing deadline
nearby_distinctions: Unlike original timely returns, belated returns restrict loss carry-forward privileges and strip eligibility for specific tax incentive deductions.

descriptors.definition: Every person in receipt of income held under a trust for charitable or religious purposes must furnish a return of income if total income before exemptions exceeds the basic exemption limit. Representative assessees must file these returns voluntarily within prescribed timelines.
inclusion: Trusts holding property for charitable or religious obligations
Institutions receiving voluntary contributions
exclusion: Trusts whose gross income before exemptions stays at or below the basic exemption limit
nearby_distinctions: Differs from individual returns by computing income thresholds prior to applying statutory charitable exemptions under sections 11 and 12.

descriptors.definition: The chief executive officer of a political party must file a return of income if the party's total income before specific exemptions exceeds the basic exemption limit. Submitting this return and completing mandatory audits are prerequisites for claiming tax exemptions.
inclusion: Political parties exceeding the basic exemption limit prior to exemptions
exclusion: Political parties with total income below the basic exemption threshold
nearby_distinctions: Conditioned strictly on mandatory audit requirements to secure tax exemptions unavailable to generic non-compliant associations.

descriptors.definition: Specific specialized entities such as research associations, news agencies, and trade unions are statutorily required to file returns of income if their total income, before factoring in specific statutory exemptions, exceeds the basic exemption limit. These returns follow the procedural parameters applicable to standard corporate filings.
inclusion: Research associations
Mutual funds
Trade unions exceeding basic exemption limits
exclusion: Entities falling below the basic exemption limit prior to exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Applies to an exhaustive list of specialized statutory entities whose exemption claims are contingent upon threshold-based return filings.

descriptors.definition: Universities, colleges, and specified scientific research institutions not otherwise mandated under other return provisions must file an annual return of income or loss. All operational provisions governing standard income returns apply directly to these educational institutions.
inclusion: Universities and colleges referred in section 35(1)
Institutions lacking other return obligations
exclusion: Institutions already required to file under alternative provisions of section 139
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on educational and research institutions specified under scientific research provisions rather than general commercial entities.

descriptors.definition: Every business trust must furnish a return of its income or loss for every previous year if it has no separate filing mandate under other subsections. Standard procedural rules and provisions applicable to regular income returns govern these business trusts.
inclusion: All business trusts not otherwise filing under alternative provisions
exclusion: Business trusts covered under separate compulsory clauses
nearby_distinctions: Imposes universal annual filing obligations specifically tailored to business trust structures regardless of income performance.

descriptors.definition: Investment funds defined under specific statutory pass-through provisions must furnish an annual return of income or loss for every previous year. General tax provisions regulate these submissions as if they were standard returns filed under primary provisions.
inclusion: Investment funds referred to in section 115UB
exclusion: Funds already filing under alternative statutory sub-sections
nearby_distinctions: Specifically targets specialized investment funds governed by pass-through taxation mechanics rather than standard corporate entities.

descriptors.definition: A taxpayer who discovers any omission or wrong statement in an initially filed return may submit a revised return prior to three months before the end of the relevant assessment year or before assessment completion, whichever is earlier. The latest submitted revised return entirely supersedes all previous filings made for that assessment year.
inclusion: Returns originally filed under section 139(1) or 139(4)
Returns filed under sub-sections (1A), (3), (4A) to (4F) of section 139
exclusion: Submissions attempted after the statutory time limit or after completion of assessment
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from an original return because it corrects prior errors rather than establishing initial filing, and distinct from an updated return.

descriptors.definition: Prescribed return forms require specified categories of taxpayers to disclose comprehensive financial details alongside their income declarations. These mandatory disclosures encompass exempt income, beneficial or other asset holdings, bank accounts, credit cards, and specified high-value outgoings.
inclusion: Income exempt from tax
Assets held as beneficial owner or otherwise
Bank account and credit card details
Expenditure exceeding prescribed limits
exclusion: General business audit reports governed under separate sub-sections like section 139(6A)
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from basic income computation schedules by focusing on specific asset ownership, bank linkages, and external financial indicators.

descriptors.definition: Taxpayers engaged in any business or profession must submit specific commercial particulars with their return, including statutory audit reports and principal operational locations. Additionally, they must disclose names, addresses, and profit-sharing ratios of all partners or association members.
inclusion: Tax audit report referred to in section 44AB
Location and style of principal place of business and branches
Names and addresses of partners
Names of members and profit shares in an association of persons or body of individuals
exclusion: Non-business individual disclosures such as general personal bank accounts or credit cards
nearby_distinctions: Specifically targets commercial entities and professionals requiring structural disclosures like partnership details and audit reports, unlike general asset disclosures under section 139(6).

descriptors.definition: An Assessing Officer may flag a return as defective if mandatory computation schedules, tax payment proofs, or required audit reports are missing or incomplete. The taxpayer is given an opportunity to rectify these defects within fifteen days, extendable upon request, to prevent the return from becoming invalid.
inclusion: Incomplete computation columns or statements
Missing tax computation statements or tax audit reports
Absence of tax deduction, collection, or advance tax payment proofs
exclusion: Returns where tax deduction certificates were unissued under section 203 or 206C and produced within two years
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from a revised return because it represents a procedural cure initiated by an Assessing Officer notice rather than a voluntary taxpayer correction.

descriptors.definition: Returns furnished pursuant to a specific order issued by the CBDT under statutory relaxation powers attract the regular provisions of section 139. This mechanism streamlines return processing, curtails legal disputes, and facilitates structured scrutiny selections.
inclusion: Income returns filed under specific administrative orders of the CBDT
exclusion: Standard returns filed directly under statutory due dates without administrative relaxation orders
nearby_distinctions: Applies specifically to exceptional filings authorized via administrative discretion rather than standard statutory filing windows.

descriptors.definition: A monetary fee is levied when a person mandated to file an income return fails to complete the submission within the specified statutory time limit. A tiered fee structure applies based on whether total income crosses the statutory threshold amount.
inclusion: Default in furnishing return of income within the time limit under section 139(1)
exclusion: Timely filed returns complying with prescribed deadlines
nearby_distinctions: Represents a specific penal fee for filing delays, distinct from substantive tax liabilities or interest calculations.

descriptors.definition: Following a business reorganisation order from a competent judicial or adjudicating authority, a successor entity must submit a modified electronic return in Form ITR-A within six months. The Assessing Officer is then required to modify completed assessments or complete pending proceedings to align with the reorganisation order.
inclusion: Entities undergoing business reorganisation under court, tribunal, or IBC orders
Modified returns filed in Form ITR-A within the stipulated timeline
exclusion: Standard voluntary revisions of income returns unrelated to formal business reorganisation judicial orders
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by its mandatory link to external corporate restructuring judicial directives rather than routine self-correction of tax errors.

descriptors.definition: Specified categories of taxpayers and entities engaged in high-value financial transactions or meeting income thresholds must mandatorily apply for a Permanent Account Number within prescribed timelines. This requirement extends to key managerial personnel of reporting entities and individuals executing large cash deposits.
inclusion: Persons with income exceeding the maximum unchargeable limit
Businesses with turnover likely to exceed specified monetary limits
Entities entering into high-value financial transactions and their key management personnel
exclusion: Persons falling entirely below statutory income and transaction thresholds without mandatory application triggers
nearby_distinctions: Distinct as an identification number allocation framework, whereas section 139 governs return filing procedures.

descriptors.definition: Eligible individuals must quote their Aadhaar number when applying for a PAN or submitting an income tax return. Failure to link PAN with Aadhaar within designated windows renders the PAN inoperative according to prescribed regulatory mechanisms.
inclusion: Quota requirements in PAN application forms
Mandatory quoting in returns of income
Intimation of Aadhaar to designated systems authorities
exclusion: Exempted classes of persons specifically excluded from mandatory Aadhaar quoting rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from PAN allocation because it mandates biometric identifier cross-referencing and integration into existing tax databases.

descriptors.definition: The CBDT is empowered to notify a scheme enabling specified classes of small taxpayers to prepare and file their income returns through authorized Tax Return Preparers. Qualified preparers assist eligible individuals and HUFs while being strictly restricted from acting as preparers if they are bank officers, legal practitioners, chartered accountants, or company employees.
inclusion: Individuals and Hindu Undivided Families utilizing authorized Tax Return Preparers
Preparation and signature assistance by certified preparers
exclusion: Companies and taxpayers whose accounts require mandatory tax audits under section 44AB or other laws
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from self-filing or direct professional representation because it provides a dedicated administrative facilitation scheme for smaller taxpayers.

descriptors.definition: Statutory provisions explicitly designate which individuals possess the legal authority to sign and verify income tax returns on behalf of different assessee types. Depending on circumstances such as absence, mental incapacity, winding up, or corporate insolvency, specific representatives like power-of-attorney holders, managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals are authorized.
inclusion: Assessee himself for individuals under normal circumstances
Authorized power-of-attorney holders during absence or incapacity
Managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals for companies
exclusion: Unauthorized third parties lacking specific legal designation or valid power of attorney
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on the legal competence to sign and authenticate return documents, separate from the actual preparation or computation of income.

descriptors.definition: Before submitting any required return of income, an assessee must self-assess and pay any remaining tax liability along with applicable interest and fees. Payments made are adjusted sequentially first against fees, then against interest, and finally towards the underlying tax due.
inclusion: Computation of net tax payable after deducting TDS, advance tax, and eligible tax credits
Mandatory payment of interest and fees prior to return submission
exclusion: Taxes assessed independently by the Assessing Officer through regular scrutiny assessment without prior taxpayer self-computation
nearby_distinctions: Represents taxpayer-driven pre-filing tax clearance, differing from post-filing departmental assessments and demand notices.

descriptors.definition: Assessees can furnish an updated return for any previous year within 24 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, regardless of whether original, belated, or revised returns were previously filed. However, updated returns are prohibited if they report a loss, decrease tax liability, result in or increase refunds, or if search, survey, or related proceedings apply.
inclusion: Returns filed within 24 months from the end of the relevant assessment year
Returns furnishing additional income
exclusion: Loss returns
Returns decreasing total tax liability
Returns creating or increasing refunds
Cases involving search, requisition, or certain surveys
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from belated returns under section 139(4) and revised returns under section 139(5) by its specific purpose of updating income with additional tax payments and strict non-applicability to loss or refund scenarios.

descriptors.definition: Before furnishing an updated return, the assessee must pay the due tax, additional income-tax, interest, and fees. Computations account for advance tax, tax deducted or collected at source, and eligible tax credits or reliefs.
inclusion: Tax payment prior to submission
Interest and fee calculations
Adjustments for TDS, TCS, and advance tax
exclusion: Returns filed without prior proof of tax and interest payment
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular return filing by the mandatory prepayment of an additional income-tax component alongside applicable interest and fees before submission.

descriptors.definition: The Assessing Officer may serve a notice to require a return, production of accounts and documents, or written information regarding assets and liabilities. Account production is restricted to periods not exceeding three years prior to the previous year, and asset statements require joint commissioner approval.
inclusion: Issuance of notice to furnish returns
Production of accounts and documents
Submission of written information on assets and liabilities
exclusion: Requiring accounts relating to a period more than 3 years prior to the previous year
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from summary processing under section 143(1) by involving active inquiries, document production demands, and notices issued directly by tax authorities.

descriptors.definition: The Assessing Officer can direct an assessee to get accounts audited by a chartered accountant or inventory valued by a cost accountant based on account complexity, volume, doubts, or business nature. Such direction requires previous approval from specified higher income-tax authorities after providing the assessee an opportunity of being heard.
inclusion: Audit of accounts by a nominated chartered accountant
Valuation of inventory by a nominated cost accountant
exclusion: Unapproved audit directions
Directions issued without giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from routine statutory audits by requiring specific direction from the Assessing Officer and nomination of the auditor by high-ranking tax authorities in revenue interests.

descriptors.definition: The Assessing Officer can reference a Valuation Officer to estimate the fair market value or value of any asset, property, or investment for assessment purposes. The Valuation Officer must submit the report within six months, and the Assessing Officer utilizes it after granting the assessee a hearing opportunity.
inclusion: Reference for estimating fair market value of assets, properties, or investments
Best judgment estimation upon non-cooperation
exclusion: References made without affording an opportunity of being heard before final assessment integration
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from special audits under section 142(2A) as it focuses strictly on estimating asset, property, or investment values through a specialized Valuation Officer rather than financial account auditing.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government may notify a faceless scheme for conducting inquiries, issuing notices, ordering special audits or inventory valuations, and making valuation references. This aims to eliminate physical interfaces, optimize resource utilization through functional specialization, and introduce team-based processing with dynamic jurisdiction.
inclusion: Faceless issuance of notices
Electronic inquiries and audits
Team-based valuation references
exclusion: Physical interface processes not exempted or modified by the official notification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from traditional physical inquiries by substituting physical interactions with an electronic, team-based framework governed by a notified Central Government scheme.

descriptors.definition: Summary assessment is a computerized preliminary processing of income returns where arithmetical errors, incorrect claims, late-filing loss set-offs, and audit report adjustments are corrected. Intimation is issued to the assessee before adjustments are finalized, allowing a response period of 30 days.
inclusion: Correction of arithmetical errors
Rectification of incorrect claims apparent from information
Disallowance of late-filed loss claims and specific deductions
exclusion: Adjustments executed without prior intimation and lapse of the 30-day response window
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from scrutiny or best judgment assessments by being an automated, preliminary computational review rather than a detailed investigative inquiry.

descriptors.definition: A Joint Commissioner may examine pending assessment records independently, on reference, or via assessee application to issue binding guidance directions to the Assessing Officer. Prejudicial directions require prior opportunity of being heard for the assessee, excluding general investigative lines.
inclusion: Issuance of guidance directions by Joint Commissioners
Examination of pending assessment records
exclusion: Prejudicial directions issued without giving the assessee an opportunity to be heard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular assessment orders by providing internal administrative guidance and binding instructions to the Assessing Officer rather than final liability determinations.

descriptors.definition: Faceless assessment conducts scrutiny, best judgment, or income escaping assessments electronically through a designated portal via automated case allocation. The National Faceless Assessment Centre coordinates responses, inquiries, and technical assistance between the assessee and specialized assessment, verification, or technical units.
inclusion: Automated allocation of cases via NFAC
Electronic responses and notices
Cross-functional coordination with verification and technical units
exclusion: Manual face-to-face assessment proceedings outside the designated electronic portal
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from traditional physical assessments by operating entirely through electronic portals with segregated functional units rather than a single local Assessing Officer.

descriptors.definition: The Assessing Officer can refer an arrangement to the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner to declare it an impermissible avoidance arrangement. The authority issues notices, evaluates objections, and may refer the matter to an Approving Panel which issues binding directions for completion.
inclusion: References for declaring arrangements as impermissible avoidance arrangements
Approving Panel binding directions
exclusion: Arrangements finalized without giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard tax evasion inquiries by targeting complex tax avoidance arrangements through a specialized multi-tier review involving the Principal Commissioner and Approving Panel.

descriptors.definition: Eligible assessees facing prejudicial variations in transfer pricing or non-resident assessments can seek alternate dispute resolution through a Dispute Resolution Panel. The panel issues binding guidance directions after reviewing draft orders and assessee objections.
inclusion: Draft assessment order forwarding for eligible assessees
Filing objections with the Dispute Resolution Panel
exclusion: Proceedings under Chapter XIV-B for search cases
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular assessment appeals by providing a pre-assessment fast-track collegium review mechanism specifically for eligible non-residents and transfer pricing cases.

descriptors.definition: Reassessment provisions govern the assessment of escaping income, while historical search regimes under sections 153A and 153C apply only to searches initiated on or before a specified cutoff date. Subsequent search cases are channeled into a separate block assessment framework under Chapter XIV-B.
inclusion: Reassessment of escaped income
Search assessments initiated on or before the statutory cutoff date
exclusion: Search cases initiated after the statutory cutoff date under the general reassessment sections
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard scrutiny assessments by requiring specific conditions of income escaping detection, and separated from modern search actions handled under Chapter XIV-B block assessments.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government may notify a faceless assessment framework for processing income escaping assessment, issuing notices, or passing orders under specific tax provisions. This framework eliminates direct interfaces, optimizes resource utilization through functional specialization, and deploys team-based dynamic jurisdiction assessments.
inclusion: Assessment, reassessment or recomputation under section 147
Issuance of notice under section 148
exclusion: Regular physical proceedings not covered under the notified scheme
nearby_distinctions: Differs from conventional face-to-face scrutiny assessments by incorporating automated risk management allocations and team-based workflows.

descriptors.definition: Escaping income assessed under specific reassessment provisions is chargeable at the tax rates applicable to the respective assessment years when the income ought to have been taxed. Additionally, assessees can claim to drop reassessment proceedings under certain conditions provided they have not contested the original order.
inclusion: Taxation of escaped income at historical rates
Assessee claims for dropping section 147 proceedings
Application of pre-amendment provisions for specified search dates
exclusion: Matters concluded by specific rectification or revision orders where appeals were challenged
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between current reassessment rules and transitional provisions applicable before specific legislative amendment dates.

descriptors.definition: Statutory time limits regulate the completion of assessments, reassessments, or fresh assessments based on the specific assessment year or the date of service of notices. These prescribed periods restrict when tax authorities must finalize orders following returns, searches, or appellate remands.
inclusion: Time limits for regular scrutiny or best judgment assessments
Time limits for reassessments following section 148 notices
Time limits for fresh orders after appellate set-aside actions
exclusion: Unspecified assessment procedures outside the statutory provisions of this section
nearby_distinctions: Varies strictly by assessment year and the specific procedural trigger such as regular filings versus appellate remands.

descriptors.definition: Income-tax authorities may amend any order, intimation, or deemed intimation to rectify mistakes that are glaring, obvious, and apparent from the record. Such rectification can encompass clear errors of fact or law, including those arising from subsequent Supreme Court interpretations or retrospective legislative amendments.
inclusion: Amendment of past assessment orders and statutory intimations
Rectification of clear legal or factual oversights without long-drawn debates
exclusion: Debatable issues requiring complex reasoning or subjective changes of opinion
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes self-evident mistakes correctable under section 154 from debatable matters requiring prolonged legal interpretations or appeals.

descriptors.definition: Assessment orders must be amended within specific time frames to reflect adjustments made in related entities or primary assessments, such as disallowances of partner remuneration or modifications in AOP/BOI incomes. These consequential amendments calculate limitation periods from the end of the financial year in which the final order for the primary entity was passed.
inclusion: Rectification of partner assessments following firm-level disallowances
Consequential adjustments to member assessments due to AOP income variations
exclusion: Standard rectifications governed strictly by general four-year limitation windows without specific cross-entity triggers
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general rectification rules by tying limitation periods directly to the final resolution date of the primary entity's assessment.

descriptors.definition: Assessing officers must serve a notice of demand specifying any payable sum consequent to orders passed under the Act, with certain intimations automatically qualifying as notices of demand. Co-operating or appearing in assessment proceedings cures procedural defects regarding service timeliness or validity unless specifically objected to beforehand.
inclusion: Issuance of formal demand notices for taxes, penalties, or fines
Deemed demand notices arising from processing intimations
Timeline rules for paying taxes on specific perquisite shares under start-up exemptions
exclusion: Recovery proceedings undertaken without serving a valid or deemed notice of demand
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between standard notices and statutory deeming provisions where active co-operation cures minor procedural notice defects.

descriptors.definition: When tax demands are reduced by orders from competent insolvency or appellate tribunals, the assessing officer must adjust and reissue the notice of demand in conformity with those rulings. Such modified notices operate as statutory demands under the governing tax framework.
inclusion: Demand revisions following Adjudicating Authority orders under insolvency laws
Subsequent revisions aligning demands with NCLAT or Supreme Court outcomes
exclusion: Original demands that have not undergone reduction by recognized insolvency or judicial authorities
nearby_distinctions: Applies strictly when financial liabilities are adjusted through statutory insolvency proceedings rather than normal tax appeals.

descriptors.definition: During total income assessments, the assessing officer must officially notify the assessee in writing about the computed amount of eligible carry-forward losses. This written intimation covers specific categories including business losses, speculative losses, capital losses, and racehorse maintenance losses.
inclusion: Written official orders quantifying carry-forward business and capital losses
Loss tracking for speculative businesses and racehorse activities
exclusion: Losses that are unverified or ineligible for carry-forward under statutory provisions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general tax assessment orders by focusing exclusively on quantifying and notifying eligible carry-forward losses.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government may establish a faceless scheme for executing rectifications, statutory amendments, demand notices, and loss intimations. This framework aims to maximize operational efficiency and transparency through automated, team-based processing and dynamic jurisdiction.
inclusion: Faceless processing of rectification applications and order amendments
Team-based issuance of demand notices and loss intimations
exclusion: Manual rectification and amendment workflows not incorporated into the notification
nearby_distinctions: Applies specifically to post-assessment administrative functions like rectifications and notices rather than original scrutiny assessments.

descriptors.definition: Block assessment consolidates investigations for search and requisition cases initiated after a specific date to improve efficiency and minimize multiple proceedings. The block period spans the six preceding assessment years plus the period up to the execution of the final search authorization.
inclusion: Determination of the block period based on prior assessment years and search execution dates
Consolidated search investigations across multiple prior years
exclusion: Searches initiated outside the specified date thresholds governed by separate reassessment rules
nearby_distinctions: Replaces fragmented reassessments with a comprehensive consolidated block timeline for search-related investigations.

descriptors.definition: An assessee aggrieved by specific adverse orders passed by an Assessing Officer below the rank of Joint Commissioner can challenge the determination before the appellate authority. This includes objections to income amounts, tax computations, loss determinations, or penalty impositions.
inclusion: Orders under section 143(3) or 144 regarding assessed income or tax
Assessment orders under section 147
Default orders under section 201 or section 206C(6A)
exclusion: Orders passed by or with the prior approval of an income-tax authority above the rank of Deputy Commissioner
nearby_distinctions: Differs from second appeals to the Appellate Tribunal as it forms the initial statutory tier of grievance redressal against subordinate assessing authorities.

descriptors.definition: Aggrieved assessees can challenge specific administrative and appellate determinations, including orders from the Joint Commissioner (Appeals) or Commissioner (Appeals), before the constitutionally established multi-member tribunal. The appellate mechanism covers diverse statutory disputes such as tonnage tax exclusions, general anti-avoidance rule consequences, and specific penalty impositions.
inclusion: Orders disposing of appeals by the Joint Commissioner (Appeals) or Commissioner (Appeals)
Penalty orders under sections 270A, 271A, 271AAC, 271AAD, and 271J
exclusion: Initial assessment orders passed directly by low-ranking Assessing Officers without prior appellate disposal or specialized panel directions.
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a second appellate tier situated above the first appellate authorities and below the jurisdictional High Court.

descriptors.definition: Parties aggrieved by an Appellate Tribunal order can file a direct appeal before the High Court provided the case involves a substantial question of law. The High Court must formulate the specific question and restrict its hearing to that defined legal issue.
inclusion: Appeals filed by the Principal Chief Commissioner, Chief Commissioner, Principal Commissioner, Commissioner, or assessee
Matters involving formulated substantial questions of law
exclusion: Pure findings of fact or disputes lacking a substantial question of law
nearby_distinctions: Restricted exclusively to substantial questions of law, unlike lower appellate tiers that evaluate both factual findings and legal applications.

descriptors.definition: An appeal lies to the Supreme Court against any High Court judgment if the High Court certifies the case as a fit one for appeal. The procedural rules of the Code of Civil Procedure govern these proceedings alongside discretionary cost awards by the apex court.
inclusion: High Court judgments certified as fit for appeal
Appeals where procedural rules of civil procedure apply similarly to high court decrees
exclusion: High Court judgments lacking a formal certificate of fitness for appeal
nearby_distinctions: Represents the final tier of judicial review above High Courts, requiring a specific fitness certification.

descriptors.definition: Higher administrative authorities can examine records and modify or cancel subordinate assessment or transfer pricing orders if found erroneous and prejudicial to revenue interests. An order is deemed prejudicial if passed without mandatory inquiries or contrary to statutory board instructions and jurisdictional rulings.
terminology: Prejudicial to the Interests of the Revenue
inclusion: Orders passed without conducting necessary inquiries or verifications
Orders granting relief without inquiring into claims
Orders violating CBDT instructions or binding jurisdictional court decisions
exclusion: Matters already considered and specifically decided in an earlier appeal concerning the same order
nearby_distinctions: Initiated suo motu by high-ranking commissioners to protect revenue, contrasting with assessee-driven appeal mechanisms.

descriptors.definition: The central board is empowered to set financial thresholds that regulate when tax authorities can file appeals or reference applications before tribunals and courts. Failure to appeal in a specific case due to these monetary limits does not prevent the authority from litigating the same issue in other assessment years or against different assessees.
inclusion: Departmental appeals restricted by prescribed monetary thresholds
Future filings on identical issues for other assessment years or assessees
exclusion: Appeals exceeding the specified monetary cutoffs where merits justify litigation
nearby_distinctions: Regulates administrative discretion to litigate based on financial stakes rather than the legal merit of the underlying dispute.

descriptors.definition: The partial merger doctrine allows rectification or revision only for matters untouched by a prior appeal, whereas total merger extinguishes lower revision powers once an order becomes the subject matter of an appeal. Consequently, rectification or selective revision can proceed alongside appellate proceedings only for distinct unlitigated issues.
inclusion: Rectification of matters unconsidered in prior appeal proceedings under section 154
Revision powers under section 263 extending to unconsidered appeal matters
exclusion: Revision under section 264 if the order has been made the subject matter of an appeal to the appellate authorities or tribunal
nearby_distinctions: Partial merger permits concurrent administrative review of unaddressed issues, whereas total merger completely bars revision of any part of an order subjected to appeal.

descriptors.definition: The Income-tax Settlement Commission ceased operations from February 2021, and pending cases are handled by Interim Boards for Settlement. A dispute resolution scheme via Dispute Resolution Committees was introduced to provide early tax certainty for small and medium taxpayers.
inclusion: Pending settlement applications as of January 31, 2021
Disputes eligible for Dispute Resolution Committee
exclusion: New applications to the Settlement Commission filed on or after February 1, 2021
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between legacy settlement applications handled by Interim Boards and future dispute prevention handled by Dispute Resolution Committees.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government constitutes regional Dispute Resolution Committees comprising two retired senior revenue officers and one serving commissioner to resolve specified tax variations. Eligible taxpayers can apply to the committee in the prescribed form along with the specified fee.
inclusion: Taxpayers opting for dispute resolution for variations in specified orders
Applications accompanied by the prescribed fee
exclusion: Taxpayers not fulfilling the specified conditions
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts the multi-member panel composition of retired and serving officers with single-officer adjudication authorities.
source_ambiguities: The source text cuts off mid-sentence while detailing the draft order under section 144C(1).

descriptors.definition: Accepting loans, deposits, or specified sums equal to or exceeding 20,000 rupees must be executed through account payee cheques, bank drafts, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. Specified sums include advance monies receivable regarding immovable property transfers, subject to specific institutional exemptions and agricultural conditions.
inclusion: Loans or deposits of 20,000 rupees or more
Unpaid earlier loans or deposits aggregating 20,000 rupees or more
Specified sums receivable for immovable property transfers
exclusion: Transactions involving the Government or banking companies
Transactions where parties derive income solely from agriculture
Transactions where neither party has taxable income
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 269T which governs loan repayments rather than acceptance
Differs from Section 269ST which governs general daily or transactional cash receipt limits

descriptors.definition: Receiving an amount of 2,00,000 rupees or more is prohibited unless executed through account payee instruments, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. This restriction applies to daily aggregates from a single person, single transactions, or transactions relating to a single event or occasion.
inclusion: Receipts of 2,00,000 rupees or more in aggregate from a person in a day
Receipts of 2,00,000 rupees or more in respect of a single transaction
Receipts relating to one event or occasion from a person
exclusion: Receipts by the Government, banking companies, post office savings banks, or co-operative banks
Transactions of the nature referred to in section 269SS
Cash withdrawals by any person from a bank, co-operative bank, or post office savings bank
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 269SS which specifically targets loans, deposits, and immovable property advances
Applies a higher monetary threshold of 2,00,000 rupees compared to the 20,000 rupees limit under Section 269SS and Section 269T

descriptors.definition: Businesses with total sales, turnover, or gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees in the preceding financial year must provide facilities for accepting payments through prescribed electronic modes. Non-compliance attracts a daily penalty under section 271DB, while system providers are prohibited from imposing charges for using these mandated modes.
inclusion: Businesses with gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees
RuPay debit card payment facilities
BHIM-UPI and BHIM-UPI QR code payment facilities
exclusion: Assessees whose gross receipts do not exceed the 50 crore rupee threshold
Specified persons having exclusively B2B transactions with at least 95 percent non-cash receipts
nearby_distinctions: Mandates the provision of electronic payment acceptance facilities rather than restricting transaction modes like sections 269SS, 269ST, and 269T

descriptors.definition: Banking companies, co-operative banks, companies, firms, and other persons are prohibited from repaying loans, deposits, or specified advances of 20,000 rupees or more except via account payee cheques, bank drafts, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. This rule evaluates aggregate outstanding balances or specified advances held on the repayment date, including interest.
inclusion: Repayment of loans or deposits aggregating 20,000 rupees or more
Repayment of specified advances totaling 20,000 rupees or more
Higher limit of 2,00,000 rupees for primary agricultural credit societies and primary cooperative agricultural and rural development banks
exclusion: Repayments made by crediting the amount directly to the recipient's savings or current bank account
Repayments of loans, deposits, or advances taken from the Government, banking institutions, or statutory corporations
nearby_distinctions: Mirrors the restrictions in Section 269SS but explicitly governs the repayment phase of loans, deposits, and specified advances rather than their initial acceptance

descriptors.definition: Asset transfers executed by an assessee during or after tax proceedings before service of recovery notices are deemed void against tax, penalty, or interest claims exceeding 5,000 rupees. However, transfers made for adequate consideration without notice of pending proceedings or executed with prior Assessing Officer permission are valid, provided the assets do not form stock-in-trade.
inclusion: Sales, mortgages, gifts, exchanges, or other asset transfers during tax proceedings
Asset values exceeding 10,000 rupees with tax liabilities exceeding 5,000 rupees
exclusion: Transfers made for adequate consideration without notice of proceedings or tax liabilities
Transfers executed with the prior written permission of the Assessing Officer
Transfers of assets representing the stock-in-trade of the business
nearby_distinctions: Deems completed asset transfers void post-proceeds to protect revenue recovery, whereas Section 281B empowers pre-emptive property attachment during ongoing proceedings

descriptors.definition: Assessing officers are empowered to provisionally attach an assessee's property during pending assessment, reassessment, or penalty proceedings with high-ranking administrative approval to protect revenue interests. Such attachments remain valid for six months, extendable up to two years or sixty days post-assessment, but can be revoked if the assessee furnishes a scheduled bank guarantee.
inclusion: Provisional attachment of property during pending assessment or reassessment
Attachments for anticipated penalty under section 271AAD exceeding two crore rupees
Revocation of attachment upon furnishing a scheduled bank guarantee
exclusion: Extensions exceeding a total period of two years or sixty days after assessment/reassessment, whichever is later
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a precautionary attachment mechanism during active proceedings, distinct from Section 281 which retroactively voids fraudulent transfers

descriptors.definition: Tax communications, notices, and summons may be served by post, approved courier services, Code of Civil Procedure methods, electronic records, or other CBDT-prescribed transmission means. Specific statutory addressees are designated for serving notices corresponding to distinct entity types such as firms, Hindu Undivided Families, companies, and associations.
inclusion: Service by post or approved courier services
Service via electronic records under IT Act chapter IV
Designated addressees for firms, companies, HUFs, and local authorities
exclusion: Unapproved non-statutory communication channels lacking CBDT backing
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on the procedural modes and mandatory recipient addressees for serving notices, whereas Section 282A governs the authentication and signing validity of those notices
